2026-08-25-beyond-digital-adoption-strat.summary: A study of Uganda's education sector finds that digital adoption has no statistically significant direct effect on operational efficiency, and works only through strategy implementation, which fully mediates the relationship. Data came from structured questionnaires put to 55 administrators and teachers between May and June 2025, analysed by partial least squares structural equation modelling. The authors recommend that institutions and policymakers prioritise strategic execution, leadership support, digital infrastructure and continuous capacity building.

2026-08-25-cabo-verde-cmsv-plataforma-di.summary: São Vicente's municipal council presented São Vicente Digital, a municipal services platform due for public presentation in October and operation by the end of 2026, opening with 17 services. Residents will be able to submit applications, track cases in real time, make payments and receive official documents with legal validity. It is funded by the UN Joint Office in Cabo Verde; the minister for family, inclusion, social development and labour argued for keeping and improving counter services for those still facing difficulties with digital access.

2026-08-25-china-botswana-ai-support.summary: China's ambassador to Botswana has publicly offered artificial-intelligence cooperation in smart mining, digital government and talent training, pitching Chinese technology as a lever for the economic diversification Botswana is pursuing away from minerals. The offer is placed against Xi Jinping's July pledge at the Shanghai World AI Conference of 5,000 training places for developing countries and AI application cooperation centres for bodies including the African Union. It is a media note from an embassy, not an agreement.

2026-08-25-cnib-carte-nationale-identite.summary: The national police's standing page for Burkina Faso's identity card sets out what the outgoing credential is and how it is checked: compulsory from the age of fifteen, valid for ten years, and matched at the identification office against demographic similarity and fingerprints, with facial biometrics added to that stack in 2009. The page carries no date of its own, and the card it describes is the one the regional biometric card has been replacing since December 2025.

2026-08-25-collective-x-digital-skills-i.summary: The South African non-profit Collective X has removed the fixed application windows on its R200 million Digital Skills Impact Fund, so employers can apply year-round for co-funding of work-integrated digital skills programmes. It reports more than 1,800 young people through the fund across all nine provinces, 97% of them absorbed into employment and over 75% still employed after six months, against targets of 40,000 digitally skilled workers a year by 2030 and 500,000 young people into digital roles by 2034. The R200 million is a standing application envelope rather than a commitment to a named recipient.

2026-08-25-comores-ia-mariama-madi-ameri.summary: A scientific and technology conference at the American Corner on 19 August put the rise of artificial intelligence to an audience of students, school-leavers, professionals and researchers, led by seismologist Mariama Madi of the Centre National de Documentation et de Recherche Scientifique. The theme set the technology's harms against its advances and asked what critical thinking, research and innovation can offer the Comoros in response.

2026-08-25-depeches241-gabon-mbigou-moov.summary: At Mbigou, a departmental capital and a commune since 1996, Moov Africa Gabon Telecom sells data bundles on a network that barely functions: coverage appears and disappears while prepaid credit and bundle validity run down normally. Dépêches 241 puts the regulator's inaction to the president of ARCEP's Conseil de régulation. No quality-of-service determination, decision or sanction is published.

2026-08-25-diario-economico-mocambique-5.summary: Mozambique's INCM issued spectrum licences to Tmcel, Vodacom and Movitel carrying a June 2027 deadline for 5G service in every provincial capital, with the same package covering urban centres, industrial zones, economic poles and tourism destinations, and 4G obligations reaching border and rural areas in a later phase. Also provided for are 700,000 subsidised smartphones under a government-led, World Bank-supported programme starting at $5 million and able to grow to $25 million. Tmcel and Movitel representatives put on record that many target localities have no grid electricity, roads or backhaul.

2026-08-25-diggers-zra-astrophysics-bord.summary: The Zambia Revenue Authority signed a memorandum with US firm Astrophysics Inc. on 24 August to equip the Livingstone border post with scanning and security technology. Its director general framed the arrangement as data-driven supply-chain assurance and as delivery of a presidential instruction to use technology in tax administration and trade facilitation. No commitment amount, equipment specification or delivery timetable is stated.

2026-08-25-egypt-digital-identity-bank-c.summary: An Egyptian banking commentator argues that digital identity and remote account opening would cut banks' operating costs on branches, staff and paperwork, offset by investment in the technology and the cyber-security it requires, with the net effect positive and the larger gain accruing to customers through flexibility and financial inclusion. It is named commentary on a television channel rather than an announcement: no institution, instrument or date is attached to it.

2026-08-25-esatic-presentation.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's Ecole Supérieure Africaine des Technologies de l'Information et de la Communication, created by decree in 2012 and supervised by the Ministry of Digital Transition, describes itself as a public higher-education institution training ICT professionals and carrying a research and development mandate, with more than 900 students enrolled for 2025-2026. It succeeds two earlier posts-and-telecommunications schools running back to 1967. This is a standing institutional page with no publication date of its own, captured today.

2026-08-25-ghana-uk-cybersecurity-cooper.summary: Ghana's Cyber Security Authority reports talks with the British High Commission on deepening cyber cooperation, covering cyber-enabled crime and financial fraud, child online protection, capacity building and international cyber governance, with the Pall Mall Process and wider African participation in it a particular focus. No agreement, instrument, funding or timeline is announced; it is an engagement reported as discussion.

2026-08-25-intic-amia-mozambique-ai-stra.summary: Mozambique's INTIC presented its draft National Artificial Intelligence Strategy to the Mozambican Association of Artificial Intelligence at a meeting chaired by board chairman Lourino Chemane, describing it as still under development through an open multi-sector consultation covering public service delivery, public-administration modernisation, innovation and productivity. No adoption date, budget or governance instrument for the strategy is stated.

2026-08-25-itu-sub-saharan-broadband-pus.summary: The ITU has opened a five-day intermediate GIS and data-management course in Lilongwe for broadband-mapping practitioners from Malawi, Zimbabwe, Botswana and Zambia, hosted by the Malawi regulator MACRA, funded by the European Union and delivered by Esri South Africa College. It sits under the Africa-BB-Maps project, which runs to 2028 and is meant to establish or strengthen harmonised national broadband mapping in eleven sub-Saharan regulators, from Benin and Botswana to Uganda, Zambia and Zimbabwe.

2026-08-25-kagame-africa-shape-ai-future.summary: President Paul Kagame urged African countries to take an active role in shaping the future of artificial intelligence, telling a news conference in Kigali that the continent has the knowledge and talent to compete globally and should not accept being left behind. He noted that many Africans with the expertise to develop AI systems already work for the institutions and companies building them, and argued that the broader constraints keeping the continent from competing on equal terms are what have to be resolved.

2026-08-25-kenya-elections-tech-servers-.summary: The Elections (Amendment) Bill 2024, whose clause 23 would vest ownership of the intellectual property in Kenya's election technology and access to its election servers in the IEBC, remains stalled in the National Assembly. It passed the Senate in December 2024 and was read a first time in February 2025, since when the Justice and Legal Affairs Committee has tabled no report. The provision is set against the 2017 refusal to open IEBC servers hosted in France and a vendor's 2022 refusal of server access on intellectual-property grounds.

2026-08-25-liberia-regles-marche-telecom.summary: The Liberia Telecommunications Authority has drawn up guidelines covering orbital and ground satellite services, with particular attention to direct-to-device, cybersecurity, data protection and national security. They span geostationary and non-geostationary constellations and cover gateway, VSAT, satellite broadband, backhaul, broadcasting, managed data and direct-to-device services, each requiring authorisation from the authority. The text still has to be signed and published in the National Gazette before it takes effect.

2026-08-25-lisk-blockchain-shutdown-tech.summary: Swiss blockchain company Lisk said it will discontinue its chain on 31 October and wind down its DAO, ending a funding and accelerator pipeline that had backed African early-stage Web3 companies including Azza and ClapMi in Nigeria, LovCash in South Africa and Afrikabal in Rwanda. It cited chain revenue insufficient to support the LSK token, proposes burning 100 million tokens to cut supply from 400 million to 300 million, and has arranged a migration path onto Celo. African blockchain startups raised $90.1 million in 2025, down 26.6% on the year.

2026-08-25-malawi-ghana-digital-governme.summary: A Malawian delegation travelled to Accra to structure a digital-government cooperation with Ghana's communications ministry, under which Ghana is to make more than a dozen technology companies available to help Malawi build digital systems and infrastructure. The Ghana Card is cited as the reference implementation at more than 19 million holders; Malawi brings a high-coverage national ID system, a data centre and a government data exchange platform. The visit is dated only as recent, and no memorandum, budget or timetable is named.

2026-08-25-moniepoint-monieworld-wind-do.summary: Moniepoint is phasing out MonieWorld, its UK diaspora remittance product, less than 18 months after an April 2025 launch, and redirecting resources to Nigeria and Kenya. The group incorporated Moniepoint GB in February 2024, committed £1.2 million in setup expenditure, spent $1.26 million between February and December 2024, and placed a $2.5 million equity deposit in July 2025 to acquire FCA-authorised Bancom Europe, against $7.39 million earmarked for the London expansion in 2025 filings. No transition timeline was given.

2026-08-25-mozambique-tablu-tech-digital.summary: Mozambique's INTIC has opened discussions with local partner Tablu Tech on a platform called MoDi Sign to modernise the country's advanced digital signature system, extending digital identity, signatures and public key infrastructure into a national digital trust layer for public and private transactions. It follows a May tender by the digital transformation agency ATDI for a national mobile digital identity and electronic signature infrastructure, and a February memorandum with Brazil's ITI covering credentialing, auditing, training and technical assistance for running a root certification authority.

2026-08-25-mtn-nigeria-30-million-fintec.summary: MTN has set a medium-term target of 30 million fintech customers in Nigeria against five million today, group chief executive Ralph Mupita telling TechCabal that converting 30% or even 50% of the telecom base is the measure of success. The operator is bringing in technology from Alibaba, Alipay and Ant International to compete with OPay, PalmPay and Moniepoint, and will increasingly lend off its own balance sheet rather than only through the partner banks that currently score its customer data for credit.

2026-08-25-namibian-new-system-rewrites-.summary: The Namibia Statistics Agency has moved producer price index compilation off a spreadsheet system onto an automated processing engine, disclosed in the second-quarter bulletin released on 21 August and carrying retrospective revisions back to 2015. Missing prices are now imputed as a turnover-weighted average of observed price relatives within the product group rather than by unweighted class mean, imputation is capped at three consecutive periods before an item must be replaced, and automated validation flags extreme swings and entry errors across establishment files.

2026-08-25-niger-local-electronics-plant.summary: Niger's communications and vocational-training ministers inspected the DHY Technologie electronics assembly plant under construction at Hamdallaye in Tillabery region on 20 August, with the authorities reporting the smartphone, computer and tablet facility more than 60% built after six months. The government frames locally assembled devices for citizens and public institutions as a way to build domestic technical capacity and cut dependence on imported equipment.

2026-08-25-nigeria-national-cloud-taskfo.summary: Nigeria has inaugurated the National Sovereign Cloud Initiative Implementation Taskforce, moving its sovereign-cloud programme from framework to implementation. The taskforce is to align regulators, government institutions and private operators behind technical standards, cloud governance, infrastructure assurance and investment, monitor progress and clear the bottlenecks that slow adoption. Two figures frame it: Nigerian organisations are estimated to spend about US$850 million a year on foreign cloud infrastructure, and the National Digital Cloud Policy targets US$750 million of private cloud and data-centre investment within 24 months.

2026-08-25-nitda-national-sovereign-clou.summary: NITDA's own account of the same inauguration sets out the sequence and the mandate: the taskforce follows the launch of the initiative's regulatory, technical, assurance and investment instruments, and is the principal multi-stakeholder mechanism for putting them into effect, with responsibilities spanning regulatory concurrence, institutional coordination, implementation monitoring, indigenous capacity and investment mobilisation. The agency states that it complements rather than replaces the statutory responsibilities of the regulators and agencies taking part.

2026-08-25-partech-2025-africa-tech-vent.summary: Partech's annual account of African tech venture capital reports that 2025 diverged from the global market's concentration on artificial intelligence, with growth instead in enterprise software, e-commerce, cleantech and mobility, and Series A and B activity picking up in both deal count and capital. Its headline finding is debt: debt financing passed its 2021 peak and made up almost half of all capital raised, which the authors read as a sign that more companies now have the cash-flow visibility and governance to borrow rather than dilute. The page carries no date of its own and is captured here as a reference study.

2026-08-25-pida-eccas-data-centre-infras.summary: A continental infrastructure prospectus would put six new data centres in Burundi, the Central African Republic, Sao Tome and Principe, Chad, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon, and reinforce five existing centres in Angola, the Republic of Congo, Cameroon, Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It is costed at US$9m across the eleven countries, is a quarter of the way through, and is still at project-definition stage.

2026-08-25-please-call-me-vodacom-data-t.summary: A reconstruction of the twenty-year Please Call Me claim against Vodacom turns on the operator's position that the data needed to value the idea did not exist: it told the Constitutional Court it retains only six months of operational data and holds no record linking a Please Call Me message to any call it induced, so both sides' figures were modelled rather than measured. Court documents record that Vodacom decided in 2013 not to track the revenue, having been advised to, and the settlement reached at the end of 2025 is confidential, so the amount is not on the record. The case is a data-retention and record-keeping story as much as a compensation one.

2026-08-25-raxio-civ1-data-centre-cote-d.summary: Raxio's own page for CIV1, its Côte d'Ivoire facility, describes the country's first carrier-neutral Tier III data centre, built at Grand Bassam inside the VITIB technology village 30 km from Abidjan, with 2,000 square metres of white space on major fibre routes and serving the wider UEMOA region. It is an undated operator product page captured today, so it records the facility's specification rather than any event.

2026-08-25-sidwaya-ministre-communicatio.summary: Burkina Faso's communications minister and a delegation were received at Chinese broadcaster StarTimes' Beijing headquarters on 22 August, at the chief executive's invitation, to examine partnership in audiovisual and digital broadcasting. The exchanges went to the terms of collaboration with the national broadcaster RTB and the transmission company SBT. No memorandum, commitment, value or timetable is stated.

2026-08-25-somalia-eaqoonsi-digital-id-a.summary: Somalia's identification authority renewed its public call for citizens to adopt the eAqoonsi digital ID app, restating that the app-held credential is legally equivalent to the physical card. The app has passed 50,000 downloads, against more than one million digital IDs issued as of November 2025 and a target of 15 million by 2029. An estimated $125 million is still needed to implement the World Bank-funded programme in full, and inclusion complaints over weak connectivity and low digital literacy were reported in April.

2026-08-25-south-korea-loan-ai-digital-t.summary: South Korea has approved a US$170 million concessional loan from its Economic Development Cooperation Fund to build an artificial-intelligence and digital training institute in Tanzania, covering campus and laboratory construction, programmes in AI, robotics, data analytics and the internet of things, equipment, curriculum and operations support, tied to procurement from Korean firms. Further training institutes and a large-scale data centre are said to be planned. The source gives no approval or signature date, only its own publication date, so the loan is not recorded as a dated commitment in the finance layer.

2026-08-25-sudantribune-rsf-ferme-aswaq-.summary: The Rapid Support Forces ordered every public market in En Nahud, West Kordofan closed and Starlink services cut off indefinitely from 26 August. A local emergency room warned that severing satellite connectivity would cut displaced families off from relatives and from incoming remittances, in a locality already under deteriorating security and living conditions. The order coincided with reinforcements arriving from Darfur.

2026-08-25-techcabal-nigeria-fibre-inter.summary: Fibre has overtaken fixed wireless as Nigeria's largest fixed-broadband technology for the first time, with fibre-to-the-premises connections rising from 84,141 in late 2025 to about 265,000 by June, and the median fixed download speed up 155% since 2023 to 34.47 Mbps on Ookla's data. The gain is concentrated at the bottom of the distribution — the slowest tenth of connections improved almost threefold while the fastest tenth barely moved — so the country is raising its broadband floor rather than its ceiling. What follows is harder: affordability, the cost of rural build, and long-distance fibre concentrated among the few operators able to fund backbone, with the Wholesale Fixed Broadband Market Assessment the instrument meant to force sharing and open access.

2026-08-25-thisday-nac-framework-nigeria.summary: Nigeria's National Addressing Council, chaired by the Vice-President, ratified the preliminary framework for a national digitised addressing system and named the science and technology ministry as its secretariat for technical implementation, systems integration, interoperability and standards. NIMC takes individual verification, the Corporate Affairs Commission business address verification, NIPOST postcode administration, and states and local governments implementation. The framework replaces the 2017 addressing policy, described at the meeting as obsolete, focused on mail delivery and silent on business address verification.

2026-08-25-thriveagric-commercial-paper-.summary: ThriveAgric raised ₦5.3 billion, about $3.93 million, in the first series of a ₦50 billion commercial paper programme approved by Nigeria's securities regulator, oversubscribed against a ₦5 billion target. The proceeds fund working capital for aggregating smallholder produce for off-takers rather than production. The company says its operating system is accumulating the farmer transaction and farm-activity data intended to let financiers underwrite those farmers directly.

2026-08-25-tmcel-angosat2-satellite-tria.summary: Mozambique's state operator Tmcel has begun proof-of-concept testing of Angola's ANGOSAT-2 satellite, a step towards a commercial agreement to carry communication and broadcasting signals across Mozambique over Angolan space infrastructure. It follows the public broadcaster's own trial transmitting television by the same satellite and implements a bilateral memorandum signed in June. Angola is running a parallel pilot with Telecom Namibia for satellite backhaul, both framed as work under the SADC regional infrastructure master plan.

2026-08-25-universite-de-bangui-institut.summary: The University of Bangui's technology institute describes itself as the source of most of the Central African Republic's professional engineering graduates, across civil, industrial, computing, mining and geological engineering, and runs a master's in engineering sciences. It is the first university or research document the repository holds for the country, and it publishes no enrolment or output figure of its own.

2026-08-25-verascient-1-2m-raise-techafr.summary: South African enterprise AI startup Verascient raised $1.2 million, about R19.5 million, in an oversubscribed round backed by Founder Collective, Andrena Ventures, Cambridge Enterprise and Summit Ventures. Its platform builds workflows and agents over institutional knowledge scattered across email, spreadsheets, meeting records and legacy software, on a temporal knowledge graph that tracks how information changes while preserving provenance, access permissions and historical context. It is aimed first at financial services, insurance and logistics.

2026-08-26-360mozambique-tmcel-strategic.summary: Mozambique's Council of Ministers set a January 2027 deadline to identify a strategic investor for the state telecoms operator and settle the terms of a partial divestment of the state's stake. A resolution of 21 August 2026 authorises the finance and communications ministers, with the state shareholding institute, to negotiate by private negotiation and report within 135 days with a draft decree.

2026-08-26-7news-morocco-video-games-inn.summary: Morocco added the video-game industry to its innovation support fund for 2026 to 2028, covering up to 70 per cent of a prototype's cost to a ceiling of one million dirhams and up to 30 per cent of pilot production to a ceiling of three million. It sits inside a wider sector plan targeting five billion dirhams of gaming revenue by 2030.

2026-08-26-africaguinee-geda-gestion-dec.summary: Guinea's government defended the president's decision to take personal charge of the electronic system that manages decrees and orders, calling it an acceleration rather than a correction. The ruling, made at an extraordinary Council of Ministers on 14 August 2026, puts the decree-and-order chain under direct presidential follow-up to cut the delay between a decision and the instrument giving it effect.

2026-08-26-africaguinee-ministere-modern.summary: Guinea's president named new senior management across the ministry of modernisation of the administration and the public service, including the director-general of the national state digitalisation agency. The appointee previously ran planning, statistics and the unified civil-service payroll file at the public service directorate.

2026-08-26-agenceecofin-mozambique-amend.summary: Mozambique's regulator may now convert telecom operators' regulatory fines into universal-service obligations, under a licensing regulation adopted by decree in July 2026 and reported in force in a communique of 21 August. It is a further funding route for coverage, set against ICT access of 80 per cent in urban areas versus 20 per cent rural.

2026-08-26-airtel-africa-foundation-digi.summary: A mobile operator's foundation relaunched a renovated digital skills laboratory at a Dar es Salaam secondary school, with the operator's money arm and a national business incubator as partners. The programme has reached more than 5,800 students, teachers, young people, entrepreneurs and women to date, on the foundation's own count.

2026-08-26-angola-soberania-digital-cent.summary: Angola's telecommunications ministry put a requalified government technology centre into service, presenting it as the place where state and citizen data will be stored and protected inside national territory. Minister Mário Oliveira said after visiting the facility on 25 August that protecting citizens' data and reinforcing digital sovereignty remain executive priorities, and placed the centre within the country's digital-transformation policies.

2026-08-26-arc-iscw-earth-observation.summary: South Africa's agricultural research council maintains a coarse-resolution satellite imagery database going back to 1985, used for crop production and grazing capacity estimation, funded by the agriculture department with the monitoring system built on science department funding. It is one of the longer continuous earth observation archives held by an African public institution.

2026-08-26-blu-label-cell-c-write-down-i.summary: Blu Label Unlimited booked a R4.9 billion full-year loss writing its Cell C stake down to the R9 billion the operator's November listing priced it at, a 297% year-on-year swing in net income. Stripping out the write-down, the year to May produced net profit after tax of R677 million on revenue of R9.4 billion; the company declared a 10c dividend, adopted a policy of paying out 30% to 50% of core headline earnings excluding Cell C, and has started buying back its own shares. It retains 49.53% of Cell C, whose market value of R8.7 billion now exceeds Blu Label's own R7.3 billion.

2026-08-26-blu-label-electricity-play-af.summary: A South African digital distribution group built on airtime, vouchers and payments is moving into electricity, holding a multi-year trading licence granted in February 2026, having identified around 400MW of potential capacity and planning to deploy up to 180MW in the near term. The strategy is to use the payments, vending and municipal billing infrastructure it already runs as the intermediary layer between producers, municipalities and large users.

2026-08-26-businessdaily-fiscal-constitu.summary: An argument that Kenya needs a fiscal settlement for its digital build-out, written from the point at which a planned billion-dollar data centre at Olkaria could not proceed as designed because its first phase alone would have drawn 100 megawatts. The piece treats power, tax and public finance as the constraints on data-centre investment.

2026-08-26-cair-structure-and-history.summary: South Africa's national artificial intelligence research centre is a distributed network rather than a building: nine established and two emerging research groups across eight universities, funded mainly by the science department and coordinated by the state research council, with its directorate in a Cape Town computer science department. It was established in 2011, and the research groups run from computational logic and knowledge representation to the ethics of artificial intelligence and artificial intelligence for development.

2026-08-26-cameroon-says-5g-groundwork-n.summary: Cameroon's telecoms regulator says the preparatory work for 5G is practically complete but has set no date for commercial launch. Its director-general said the regulator had consulted the Presidency, the Prime Minister's Office and the telecommunications ministry, reviewed operators' investment plans and inspected data centres and network sites; reliable electricity and fibre capacity remain the open questions.

2026-08-26-cassava-ai-factory-top500-36t.summary: A pan-African technology group's artificial intelligence computing facility was ranked 36th in the latest global list of the most powerful supercomputers, which the company presents as the point at which Africa's computing gap stops being a discussion and starts being capacity. What the ranking measures is the machine; it says nothing about who gets to use it or on what terms.

2026-08-26-cloud-dependence-african-ai-s.summary: An artificial intelligence and cloud infrastructure practitioner argues that renting computing capacity is not itself the risk for African startups - almost all of them rent rather than own - but that concentrating the workload with a single provider exposes growth and margins to that provider's terms. The argument is about dependence rather than cost, and is one practitioner's assessment with no survey behind it.

2026-08-26-clubofmozambique-intic-data-p.summary: The president of Mozambique's information and communication technologies institute told a Maputo debate that passing the recent data protection and digital space laws is the easier half, and called for institutional capacity, technical skills and working oversight and accountability mechanisms to enforce them - and for citizens to know what rights they now hold and how to use them.

2026-08-26-clubofmozambique-pm-ai-deepfa.summary: Opening a meeting of the regional forum of electoral commissions in Maputo, Mozambique's prime minister set digital disinformation and manipulated video against electoral integrity, and argued in the same speech for using artificial intelligence to administer elections - managing voter registers, communicating with voters and strengthening data analysis. What is asked for is stronger technical and operational capacity in the region's electoral bodies; no instrument or rule follows from the speech.

2026-08-26-com-200-millions-de-francs-de.summary: A fault between the Comoros mobile-money service and the utility's prepaid electricity meters on Moheli let subscribers credit their meters without the amounts being debited from their accounts. A source close to the case puts the potential loss above 200 million Comorian francs, with one meter said to have taken more than nine million; neither party has confirmed the figures.

2026-08-26-cote-divoire-68-millions-575-.summary: Côte d'Ivoire is continuing its FCFA 38 billion, about $68 million, Programme national de connectivité rurale to bring mobile and internet coverage to 575 localities, and set out its phase figures in a government communiqué of 24 August. Phase one, at FCFA 10 billion, was completed in 2024 with 160 radio sites serving 175 localities and about 221,267 inhabitants; phase two commits FCFA 18 billion for 240 further localities and phase three FCFA 10 billion for 160 more. The national broadband backbone stood at 5,207 km with 4G covering 65% of the territory in 2024.

2026-08-26-cps-hspr-frame-update.summary: South Africa's statistics agency is reengineering its household survey programme, with the first phase updating the master sample - the geographic frame from which household surveys draw - to reflect new housing and current population. The agency says it is also exploring telephone and web collection, which is a change in method rather than in frame.

2026-08-26-dawan-somalia-financial-inclu.summary: An argument that Somalia's financial progress should be measured by whether financial services create resilience and security rather than by access alone, written against the central bank's own 2026 financial access survey. It is a reading of a published dataset rather than new evidence.

2026-08-26-digwatch-ghana-malawi-digital.summary: A Malawian government delegation visited Accra to discuss a planned collaboration with Ghana's communications ministry on digital government, public sector innovation and the delivery of digital public services. The emphasis is on strengthening Malawi's own digital government programmes.

2026-08-26-dji-forum-national-sur-l-ia-l.summary: Djibouti briefed journalists ahead of its first national artificial-intelligence forum, held under the president's patronage and bringing together public officials, international partners, researchers, entrepreneurs, technology companies and young people. The briefing was about how the event will be covered.

2026-08-26-dji-intelligence-artificielle.summary: An assessment of where Djibouti actually stands on artificial intelligence, written ahead of the country's first national AI forum and drawing on a readiness report prepared by the digital economy ministry with UNESCO. The report is to be the basis of the forum's debates and few in the country have read it.

2026-08-26-djibouti-numerique-emploi-dip.summary: Djibouti's labour ministry presented Djibouti Emploi on 24 August, a single digital portal meant to centralise its employment services and interconnect the institutions working in the field, aimed at jobseekers, employers and the administration alike. The World Bank's Djibouti Economic Monitor of May 2026, over data collected in the first two quarters of 2025, puts 51.8% of the working-age population outside the labour force, 46.2% of 16-to-24-year-olds not in employment, education or training, and 52.7% of jobs in the informal sector.

2026-08-26-doj-fbi-seize-qscan-qtrouter-.summary: United States authorities seized the domains behind two hacking platforms operated by a Chinese state-sponsored group employed by a Nanjing technology company, naming victims including the space agency, the Federal Reserve, three federal departments and the Senate. The item carries no African place, and is held here for what it shows about how state-sponsored intrusion infrastructure is built and taken down.

2026-08-26-dsbd-incubation-and-digital-h.summary: South Africa's small business department reports 101 incubators established against a target of 96, including twenty-two rapid-incubation centres in technical colleges and universities, with a further twenty-seven planned mainly in townships and rural areas and an expected 1,290 new enterprises from them. The headline target of 250 incubation and digital hubs by 2024 is the one the page does not report against.

2026-08-26-dza-immatriculation-sayoud-ex.summary: Algeria's interior minister called for rapid correction of technical problems and malfunctions in the national vehicle registration information system, in a working session with regulatory directors from several wilayas. No fault description or completion date is given.

2026-08-26-ebrd-s-venture-capital-fund-t.summary: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is putting US$8 million into a pan-African venture capital fund, its first commitment to one, to back early-stage technology companies with a focus on Côte d'Ivoire, Egypt, Morocco, Nigeria and Senegal.

2026-08-26-eca-supports-cameroon-to-faci.summary: Cameroon's trade ministry, with the UN Economic Commission for Africa, convened a Douala workshop to validate new tools for giving economic operators access to trade information under the African continental free trade area. The work is donor-funded and the tools are at validation stage.

2026-08-26-ecofinagency-yas-tanzania-zan.summary: Tanzania's second-largest operator launched fibre-to-the-home in Dodoma and plans 300 billion shillings of investment over twenty years to deploy fibre across Zanzibar's two main islands, targeting 100,000 subscribers within three years. It had 9,804 fixed-internet subscribers at the end of March 2026, seventh in the market.

2026-08-26-egy-egypt-and-iraq-explore-en.summary: Egypt's communications minister met his Iraqi counterpart to discuss cooperation in telecommunications and information technology, including digital transformation, artificial intelligence and data centres. Nothing is agreed.

2026-08-26-egy-egypt-launches-biometric-.summary: Egypt launched a national biometric verification and electronic-signature system letting users complete identity checks for telecoms services from a mobile application instead of a company branch. It was built by the telecoms regulator with the IT industry agency, a Cairo firm and licensed e-signature providers, and runs as a pilot that operators will roll into their own apps as their readiness allows.

2026-08-26-egy-huawei-bid-to-build-egypt.summary: Huawei has bid, with a blacklisted speech and surveillance firm, to build the Egyptian government's AI data centres, while the US State Department tries to assemble a rival consortium of Nvidia, AMD and Microsoft. The tender proposes exporting 2,008 chips on a twelve-month build and would be the first confirmed export of Huawei's top-end accelerators anywhere; the proposal bundles vehicle and individual recognition.

2026-08-26-egypt-offshoring-sector-5-2bn.summary: Egypt generated $5.2 billion in offshoring services exports in 2025, across 252 companies operating 282 delivery centres, 177 of them multinational, employing more than 195,000 specialists. A prime-ministerial tour of Teleperformance, Concentrix, Vodafone Intelligent Solutions and Sutherland in Alexandria — which together employ nearly 15,000 there — was used to press the case for growing the industry outside Cairo and moving it from back-office work into generative-AI-enabled services.

2026-08-26-eth-eagle-lion-and-tsedey-ban.summary: An Ethiopian technology group and a bank signed an agreement to digitise the agricultural input supply chain end to end, from regulatory agencies down to smallholder farmers. The platform is said already to count millions of active farmers and to launch within days; it is described as the first partnership between a domestic fintech and a state-affiliated agricultural bank to cover logistics and regulation together.

2026-08-26-four-african-cloud-startups-t.summary: A trade outlet names four African-founded cloud and artificial intelligence infrastructure companies as an emerging alternative to hyperscale providers based in the United States and Europe, offering sovereign, low-latency capacity and keeping data on the continent. The roundup is a description of a direction rather than a measure of it: no capacity, customer count or market share appears for any of the four.

2026-08-26-france-maroc-ia-act-optin-vil.summary: An analysis of what two regulatory changes mean for the France-Morocco call-centre and customer-relations business: the transparency obligations of the European Union's AI regulation, and a French telephone opt-in rule. Both bear on an offshore industry that Morocco's digital sector depends on.

2026-08-26-intron-sahara-v2-5-code-switc.summary: Intron released Sahara v2.5, adding code-switching speech recognition in 12 African languages and what it says is the first African trilingual model, built for Rwanda's Kinyarwanda-English-French mix. On its own benchmarks and evaluation set the Lagos-founded company reports an average word error rate of 34.3% on code-switched African speech against 53.8% for Google's Gemini 3.6, and coverage of 31 languages after adding Nupe, Kanuri, Nigerian Fulfulde, Tigrinya, Kikuyu, Dholuo and Somali. It says the models are deployed at more than 40 organisations across six countries, with US patents filed on the trilingual algorithms.

2026-08-26-kenya-artificial-intelligence.summary: Kenya's information and digital economy ministry, its technopolis authority and the United Nations development programme opened a call for high-impact artificial intelligence use cases in public service delivery and the green transition, running 24 August to 6 September 2026 and open to public institutions, universities, research entities, startups and individual innovators. Successful applicants are offered stage-appropriate access to computing, data preparation and technical assistance rather than cash.

2026-08-26-kenya-health-data-sovereignty.summary: A health policy analyst argues in The Standard that Kenyan health data is being collected to train AI medical devices sold globally while the communities it comes from receive nothing, citing a European inventor who sought a proof-of-concept study in a Nairobi settlement because European regulatory requirements were too demanding. He credits three convergent policy developments — the Pharmacy and Poisons Board's 2025 guidelines on AI-powered medical tools, the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025–2030 naming data sovereignty a priority, and the Artificial Intelligence Bill 2026 tabled in the Senate — but says each stops short of settling who owns the training data or who profits when the tools go global.

2026-08-26-korea-backs-kenya-digital-eco.summary: A University of Seoul and Korea Development Institute delegation visited Nairobi to evaluate what South Korea's development assistance to Konza Technopolis has actually produced, covering institutional support for Konza and delivery through Korea's Knowledge Sharing Programme, Economic Innovation Partnership Programme and Economic Development Cooperation Fund. ICT principal secretary John Tanui said the two governments also explored extending cooperation into digital media infrastructure and the Kenya Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, for which Korea Eximbank has committed over $100 million in concessional loans.

2026-08-26-lagdeguinea-sigf-modernizar-a.summary: Equatorial Guinea launched an integrated civil-service management system intended to run across every state institution, on an eighteen-month timetable to full implementation. The steering committee's first session was chaired by the minister secretary general, who framed it as an instrument of transparency and control over the management of public servants rather than a technology tool.

2026-08-26-lca-consumer-perception-surve.summary: Lesotho's communications authority is running its 2026 consumer perception survey, inviting consumers by text message through their mobile networks. The notice carries a warning to use only the link published through official channels, which is itself an account of the fraud risk around any state survey delivered by SMS.

2026-08-26-lemarche-finance-perceptions-.summary: A long report on how Senegalese users see their banks finds sharply divided views: complaints about cash machines and administrative delay set against approval of mobile applications and bank-to-wallet transfers. It is a picture of perception rather than a measure of access.

2026-08-26-liberianinvestigator-liberia-.summary: Liberia's trade information portal, a single online source for trade and regulatory information funded by the World Bank, was put to government institutions and stakeholders at an introductory workshop. The special economic zones authority said it could cut the time and cost of doing business.

2026-08-26-libyaherald-libyan-experts-fo.summary: The first Libyan Experts Forum closed in Tripoli recommending that the national digital addressing platform be expedited, that the digitised transfer and registration of real-estate ownership documents be completed, that a unified health identification number and electronic medical record be launched, that a national artificial-intelligence and cybersecurity strategy be developed, and that reliance on external cloud services for sensitive data be reduced.

2026-08-26-liquid-targets-kenya-connecti.summary: Kenya's ICT principal secretary John Tanui met Liquid Intelligent Technologies Kenya chief executive Neeraj Pradhan in Nairobi to discuss accelerating broadband and extending public Wi-Fi into public spaces and underserved communities, with no agreement, cost or timeline announced. The talks are framed against the Digital Superhighway target of 100,000 km of fibre and 25,000 public Wi-Fi hotspots across all 1,450 wards, backed by a $390 million World Bank programme and state budget allocations.

2026-08-26-m42-enters-africa-with-10-yea.summary: An Abu Dhabi health group signed a ten-year strategic partnership with Botswana's health ministry covering digital health transformation, a national genomics programme, precision medicine and capacity development — its first health-systems partnership in Africa. The agreement was signed in Gaborone, with a second Emirati partner joining on pharmaceuticals and medical equipment.

2026-08-26-maroc-inde-ia-langues-nationa.summary: Morocco's digital transition minister and India's minister of state for information technology agreed in Rabat on 24 August to create a joint commission on languages and digital technology, aimed at artificial intelligence models that handle Moroccan Arabic and Amazigh. The purpose stated is getting both languages into government digital services; no budget, timetable or institution is named.

2026-08-26-mastercard-foundation-cchub-g.summary: A foundation and a Nigerian innovation hub opened applications to a five-year programme intended to train more than 400,000 young Nigerians in artificial-intelligence-enhanced digital skills and connect them to global gig work, across tracks including graphic design, digital marketing, interface design and video production. Training is paired with portfolio development and gig-work readiness rather than offered alone.

2026-08-26-mediaguinee-reforme-administr.summary: Guinea opened a workshop to consolidate the legal framework of its public administration around three bills: a rewritten law on the organisation and functioning of the administration, a public service charter, and a law simplifying administrative procedures. The simplification bill is intended to fix processing deadlines.

2026-08-26-naom-monari-bena-care-soins-d.summary: A Kenyan nurse turned founder runs a home-care service built on a mobile application with geolocation, connecting patients to nurses, physiotherapists and specialists within their area for nursing, palliative care, post-operative follow-up and chronic disease management. It was founded in 2017 and is presented against hospital congestion and distance from care centres; no patient volume or clinical governance arrangement is given.

2026-08-26-narssa-managing-electronic-re.summary: South Africa's national archive sets out what it requires of government bodies managing electronic records, endorsing the international standards for records management, records metadata, the trustworthiness of electronically stored records and the functional requirements for digital records systems. It is a statutory requirement on every governmental body rather than guidance offered.

2026-08-26-ncc-mtn-ihs-conditional-appro.summary: Nigeria's NCC granted MTN Nigeria a conditional Approval-in-Principle in mid-July for the acquisition of IHS Towers' Nigerian business, disclosed by the regulator on 25 August and separate from the competition clearance the FCCPC had already given. The conditions are compliance with the NCC's corporate governance guidelines, a bar on amending existing contracts as a consequence of the transaction, a prohibition on the deal conferring exclusivity on MTN Nigeria, and an investment plan with measurable milestones; final approval is withheld until the regulator confirms compliance. Nigeria carries 15,848 of IHS's roughly 28,000 African tower sites, more than half the portfolio, in a transaction valuing IHS at about $6.2 billion enterprise value and the stake purchase at about $2.2 billion.

2026-08-26-ndoh-chief-directorate-health.summary: South Africa's health department sets out what the national health insurance fund requires of its digital information systems: universal and preferably international coding used by public and private providers alike, and a portable electronic health record for every person that each provider adds to at every encounter. The stated purpose is measuring equity and access well enough to purchase strategically against the gaps.

2026-08-26-nigeria-project-bridge-90000k.summary: Stakeholders question whether Project BRIDGE, the 90,000 km fibre deployment starting in October, has addressed what has frustrated Nigerian fibre for years: right-of-way charges, multiple taxation, approval delays, vandalism and fibre cuts running at an average of about 1,100 a week on the NCC's earlier count. The programme takes the national backbone from about 35,000 km to 125,000 km across all 36 states and more than 770 local government areas, financed by $500 million from the World Bank, $100 million from the EBRD and a €22 million EU grant. ALTON and ATCON both name state right-of-way pricing and damage to existing infrastructure, rather than the laying itself, as the risk to the investment.

2026-08-26-nita-uganda-digital-skills-fr.summary: Uganda's IT authority invited expressions of interest for consultancy services to develop a National Digital Skills and Competence Framework, under a World Bank-financed digital acceleration project. Nothing is yet awarded.

2026-08-26-nitda-sandbox-technical-worki.summary: Nigeria's IT development agency inaugurated a technical working group to build a multi-agency national regulatory sandbox, deliberately sector-agnostic, letting innovators test emerging technologies with several regulators at once before full market approval. The agency's case is that regulators operating in silos are a structural obstacle to innovation.

2026-08-26-partenariat-pour-un-gouvernem.summary: Benin is preparing its first Open Government Partnership national action plan around four axes: budget transparency and accountability; access to information and digital governance; anti-corruption and integrity; and citizen participation and access to justice. Local consultations ran in twenty-three communes and departmental consultations across all twelve departments.

2026-08-26-payangel-450m-remittance-plat.summary: PayAngel, founded in 2013 after a diverted tuition payment cost a relative their university place, routes diaspora remittances to verified schools, hospitals, insurers and retailers directly rather than to a family member trusted to forward them, identifying the payer through each institution's own reference system. The company says it has processed more than $450 million, has over 100,000 active remitters across 22 countries and an annualised revenue run rate of about $4 million, and holds regulatory approval in the United Kingdom, United States, Canada, Australia and Ghana. A sender transferring at least £100 a month qualifies their beneficiary for rolling life and hospitalisation cover, and a separate product lets African businesses collect from diaspora customers directly.

2026-08-26-powered-by-people-leve-des-fo.summary: A platform connecting independent artisans in more than thirty countries directly to large international retailers raised funding led by a European clothing group's foundation, to be spent on its technology and on artificial intelligence for product search. Neither the amount raised nor the number of artisans on the platform is stated.

2026-08-26-protection-des-consommateurs-.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's telecoms regulator validated a harmonised procedure for handling consumer complaints against operators and internet service providers, agreed at a two-day workshop with operators and consumer associations. It now goes to the regulator's board for possible adoption, under a consumer-protection mandate given by a 2024 law.

2026-08-26-sa-digital-migration-progress.summary: South Africa's broadcasting digital migration programme told Parliament's communications committee on 25 August that 52,869 households registered for subsidised set-top boxes still cannot be located, down from about 80,000 at the previous meeting, and that no analogue switch-off date has been set pending a steering committee of broadcasters and stakeholders. A SITA-facilitated cleaning of registration data dating to September 2015 cut the installation target from 447,815 to 401,803 households, against which 290,506 installations are complete and verified. The department said the state has spent close to R2 billion on dual illumination, and MPs described the programme as failed and wasteful.

2026-08-26-safaricom-ethiopia-subscriber.summary: The consortium board behind Ethiopia's second mobile operator reviewed five years of operation and put the pace in comparative terms: the Vodacom group chief executive said the operator reached its current subscriber scale in five years where the industry typically takes fifteen to twenty, and the Safaricom chief executive said the Ethiopian team built in four years half the number of towers Safaricom has deployed in Kenya over twenty-six. No subscriber or tower figure is given with either comparison.

2026-08-26-sasria-ai-national-risk-forec.summary: South Africa's state-owned special risks insurer is combining artificial intelligence with human intelligence and social science, in collaboration with the state research council, to read social and behavioural signals for the conditions that precede unrest and destructive events. An executive told a summit panel that triangulating social media with other data can identify potential unrest weeks ahead; no accuracy figure or evaluation is offered for the claim.

2026-08-26-sierraloaded-digital-protecti.summary: Sierra Leone put draft sector-specific protection plans for critical information infrastructure in energy, health, education, and defence and security to stakeholder validation. They were developed by the national cyber security coordination centre and the communications ministry under the 2021 cyber security act, with World Bank support.

2026-08-26-sinazongwe-smart-zambia-ict-d.summary: SMART Zambia's e-Government Division has equipped Sinazongwe Town Council in Southern Province with high-speed internet, telepresence systems, desktops and laptops, and solar power to keep the offices running through load-shedding. The deployment is presented as part of the Government Wide Area Network programme to connect all 116 councils and government institutions to a secure national backbone, with training for local ICT staff running alongside the hardware. No cost, vendor or completion date for the wider rollout is stated.

2026-08-26-somalilandcurrent-credit-regi.summary: The Central Bank of Somaliland, the International Finance Corporation and the World Bank set up a steering committee and technical working groups for a credit information system and a secured-transaction collateral registry. A Hargeisa workshop reviewed implementation milestones, IT infrastructure needs and the legal reform the registries would require.

2026-08-26-south-korea-dpi-aid-exports-i.summary: A study traces how South Korea has used concessional lending to export its own digital government platforms - customs and public procurement systems - and finds recipients adopt the administrative procedures and certification standards embedded in them, not only the software. It puts a number on the commercial return: a one percent rise in Korean digital public infrastructure aid is associated with a 0.44 percent rise in exports to the recipient within one to two years, strongest where internet penetration and logistics capacity are already good. The benefits are asymmetric, and the study says so.

2026-08-26-starlink-users-in-kinshasa-fa.summary: Starlink's constellation over Kinshasa has hit its residential bandwidth ceiling, with four to six months of degraded speeds expected while more satellites are deployed. An authorised reseller is steering new Kinshasa customers to the paid priority package and disclaims liability; the constraint is stated as applying to Kinshasa only.

2026-08-26-statehouse-seychelles-cabinet.summary: Seychelles' Cabinet approved the signing and ratification of the African Charter on Statistics and the SADC Protocol on Statistics, alongside other legal and policy memoranda. Both commit the national statistical system to regional and continental standards.

2026-08-26-tamko-clarence-cameroun-bouti.summary: A Cameroonian software engineer co-founded a platform that lets a trader stand up an online shop in minutes with no technical skill, ending in a personal link to be shared on messaging apps and social networks, with order tracking, customer messaging and analytics behind it. It was founded in 2021; no merchant count or transaction volume is published.

2026-08-26-togofirst-national-malaria-da.summary: Togo approved the modules of a National Malaria Data Repository, a platform centralising malaria data to show trends, identify the areas and populations most at risk and coordinate the parties involved. No launch date is given and no operator is named.

2026-08-26-tshwane-shuts-online-food-sto.summary: The City of Tshwane shut the Hatfield fulfilment premises of Zulzi, Yassir and Uber Eats Market on Friday 21 August in a health-department enforcement operation — Yassir and Uber Eats Market for allegedly trading without a Certificate of Acceptability or business licences, Zulzi over what the city describes as fraudulent compliance documents including a fraudulent liquor licence. The city says it will also investigate the sale and dispatch of medicines through the Zulzi platform, and that a digital storefront does not displace the municipal health, licensing and food-safety obligations attached to the physical premises behind it. Uber Eats says the merchant is unavailable on its app while the matter is addressed; Yassir says the store stays closed until the requirements are satisfied.

2026-08-26-uganda-nin-data-protection-ob.summary: Uganda's Personal Data Protection Office says about 14,000 organisations are registered to handle personal information while more than 500,000 entities — businesses, schools, hospitals and informal vendors — collect or process it outside the legal framework. The Observer argues that the gap turns routine demands for a National Identification Number into an open licence to harvest identity, and that individual vigilance cannot substitute for registration backed by audits and consequences. PDPO national director Baker Birikujja says collecting personal data without registration is a criminal offence.

2026-08-26-uk-south-sudan-fintech-cooper.summary: Bank of South Sudan governor Addis Ababa Othow met British ambassador David Ashley in Juba to discuss monetary policy, digital banking regulation and public sector financial management, with no agreement, figure or timeline announced beyond the meeting itself. The central bank and the finance ministry are engaging telecommunications companies and mobile money operators to integrate the National Payment System, which is intended to connect commercial banks directly with mobile network operators and move a cash-dominated economy onto interoperable electronic infrastructure.

2026-08-26-undp-executive-board-second-r.summary: The development programme's administrator opened the year's second regular Executive Board session with technology placed at the centre of the development argument rather than beside it - the question being whether it becomes a bridge to opportunity or a new dividing line. The statement is a policy framing for the agency's country work across the continent rather than a commitment to any of it.

2026-08-26-ursb-uganda-non-individual-re.summary: Uganda's registration bureau opened its 2026/27 stakeholder engagements for the register of non-individual legal entities, aimed at awareness and compliance with registration requirements. The first is in Moroto.

2026-08-26-ustda-zenith-bank-nigeria-clo.summary: A United States trade agency awarded a training grant to a Nigerian commercial bank as it moves onto a hyperscale cloud platform sold by a Washington-based vendor, covering governance and financial management of cloud services for senior managers and non-technical adaptation training for staff. The agency's director framed it as strengthening American competitiveness in the market for sensitive digital infrastructure, which is the second thing the grant is for. No grant value is stated.

2026-08-26-ventures-platform-second-fund.summary: Ventures Platform closed VP Pan-African Fund II at $84 million, 1.8 times its first institutional fund, adding the EBRD, Norfund, the Dutch family office Alphatron and the Ashesi University Foundation to the limited partners from the $64 million first close in November 2025. The firm will back roughly the same number of companies with larger cheques — up to $3 million, averaging about $1.5 million — targeting entry stakes of 10% to 12%, on founding partner Kola Aina's reading that secondary sales are its most reliable route to liquidity and that a small stake leaves nothing to sell. Nigeria's iDICE programme is an anchor limited partner and wrote one of the fund's largest individual cheques.

2026-08-27-afrinic-police-forgery-electi.summary: Mauritius police confirmed that two alleged forgery cases arising from AFRINIC's annulled June 2025 board election remain under investigation by the Central CID. The registry has never stated its reasons for the annulment, and the irregularities were reported by South Africa's ISP association: a proxy vote cast under a power of attorney the resource holder says it never gave, and a recorded power of attorney missing from the file. The registry also published a consultation update in which its bylaws committee said it will not recommend a dispute resolution clause and is considering options around the board's power to terminate members.

2026-08-27-angop-angosat-2-bengo-quiage.summary: A Conecta Angola connectivity point was restored at Quiage commune in Bengo, stated to serve five thousand residents, under the programme carrying internet over the ANGOSAT-2 satellite to border zones and isolated communities. The figure is a beneficiary estimate for a commune rather than a connection count.

2026-08-27-apd-questoes-sobre-proteccao-.summary: Angola's data protection agency published a questions page setting out the reach of the data protection law — automated and partly automated processing, and manual processing of personal data held in files, by controllers established in the country and outside it where Angolan law applies by force of international law — together with the fee schedule approved by Presidential Decree 60/21 of 10 March 2021.

2026-08-27-capacity-mtn-150mw-gulf-data-.summary: MTN's half-year results to 30 June 2026 disclosed that MTN Digital Infrastructure had, after the reporting period, entered a strategic partnership with a UAE-based data-centre investment platform; the partner is Dubai-based Gulf Data Hub founder Tarek Al Ashram, and the venture's first phase targets 150MW of AI data-centre capacity across Nigeria and South Africa.

2026-08-27-comesa-consultancy-digital-in.summary: The COMESA secretariat invited technical and financial proposals from eligible firms to develop a Digital Information Knowledge and Collaboration Platform, under contract reference CS/CC/06/(846-2026), with the minimum technical requirements in annexed terms of reference. No budget, timetable or scope beyond the title is published.

2026-08-27-consulta-publica-do-minttics-.summary: Angola's telecommunications ministry consultation portal still carries the September 2025 draft Artificial Intelligence Bill, recording 18 contributions from companies, 18 from specialists and 5 from the general public as at 27 August 2026. The 20-page draft carries an explanatory memorandum and a comparative section reviewing artificial-intelligence regulation in the United States, the European Union, China, Japan, Canada and Brazil, and the national AI strategies of Egypt, Kenya, South Africa and Rwanda.

2026-08-27-datacentresafrica-ibtc-dc-aca.summary: Two South African firms joined a data-centre operations academy as industry partners and are sponsoring a full candidate cohort for its 2026 intake, the first to fund a whole cohort. One opens a newly launched Midrand OEM training facility and the other a live operational data centre to supply the practical component of a graduate-to-employment pipeline, which its sponsor frames as a recruitment expense rather than a training one.

2026-08-27-digitalbusiness-tchad-azerbai.summary: Chad's telecommunications minister received a delegation from an Azerbaijani firm in N'Djamena to explore e-government cooperation on digital health, AI-equipped smart schools and secure identity-document production. The talks sit under a bilateral memorandum signed in January 2026; nothing further is agreed.

2026-08-27-digitalmag-5g-adoption-pays-a.summary: A GSMA Intelligence survey sets out 5G adoption country by country across eight African markets, giving start dates, current population coverage and projections to 2030. It supplies dated positions for several countries whose 5G record had rested on announcements rather than measurement.

2026-08-27-ecofin-protection-mineurs-res.summary: African states are moving from a minimum age for opening a social media account towards duties on how platforms are built. Gabon's February 2026 ordinance fixes digital majority at 16 and obliges platforms to limit certain publication and interaction functions, disable contacts from unidentified users by default and provide age-verification mechanisms; Rwanda is preparing a restriction on under-16s, Nigeria is consulting on age limits, identity verification and platform liability, and Zimbabwe has adopted a policy covering cyber-harassment, sextortion and data protection. The African Union's 2024 child online safety policy already asks states to require protection by design and by default, and the constraint named here is enforcement rather than law.

2026-08-27-fao-giews-earth-observation-g.summary: FAO's earth-observation indicators for Guinea-Bissau, carrying thirty-six months of seasonal, vegetation and precipitation measures. It is a standing data service rather than a development, and it is one of the few continuous geospatial series the repository holds for the country.

2026-08-27-fij-nin-bvn-illegal-data-mark.summary: An underground market trading Nigerian national identity and bank verification numbers shut down after an investigation named its operator, with two linked technical services taken offline and a private messaging community closed. The data-protection commission continues to hold the operator as a registered licensee.

2026-08-27-guardian-ng-digital-sovereign.summary: Technology and business leaders in Nigeria argued that access to technology is no longer the constraint and that control of the infrastructure, data and technology businesses depend on is the harder question. The argument was made at the launch of a technology survey and a national database forum.

2026-08-27-guineabissau-ohchr-treaty-bod.summary: The UN treaty body database record for Guinea-Bissau, which sets out which human-rights instruments the country has ratified and which it has not. It is a reference position rather than a development, and it is the baseline any claim about the country's data-protection and privacy obligations has to be read against.

2026-08-27-horonyafinance-umoa-monnaie-e.summary: The West African monetary union counted 78 institutions offering electronic money at the end of 2025 against 63 a year earlier, according to its banking commission: 59 banks working through operator or technical partnerships, 18 licensed issuers and one microfinance institution, alongside four national treasuries. Licensed issuers rose from 14 to 18 and are spread unevenly, with five in Senegal and one each in Burkina Faso, Niger and Guinea-Bissau; provisional turnover across seventeen active issuers reached FCFA 323.2bn, up 12%.

2026-08-27-imani-au-continental-ai-strat.summary: A policy analyst at Ghana's IMANI Centre put African governments' committed public capital for the AU Continental AI Strategy at about US$150m against an implementation cost the strategy itself prices between US$250bn and US$500bn, and an ambition to add US$1.5 trillion to Africa's GDP by 2030. He also set the strategy's assumption of cross-border data flows against the Malabo Convention's data-localisation obligations, and noted that indigenous African languages make up under 0.02% of web content the models would train on.

2026-08-27-iso-dsnpq-guinea-bissau-natio.summary: The ISO membership record for Guinea-Bissau's national standards body, held in the trade ministry. It records no technical-committee liaisons at all, which is the measure of how far the country participates in setting the standards its digital sector will be held to.

2026-08-27-iso-member-record-iniq-angola.summary: Angola's national quality-infrastructure institute is listed by the International Organization for Standardization as a correspondent member, the category for bodies that follow the organisation's work without a vote on technical committees.

2026-08-27-itweb-bolt-e-hailing-complian.summary: An e-hailing platform took its compliance programme to South Africa's provinces, holding a North West regulatory engagement in Rustenburg on 18 August attended by more than 150 operators and a Western Cape transport dialogue in Cape Town on 21 August, at which the provincial mobility department's director of licensing and adjudication undertook to add e-hailing as a service option on the operating-licence application. The North West provincial regulatory entity put its pending operating-licence backlog at 3,000 to 5,000 applications.

2026-08-27-itweb-women-must-be-active-ar.summary: A three-day digital-skills initiative for South African women opened at a vendor campus in Johannesburg, arguing that women should be building the local artificial-intelligence economy rather than being left out of it. The figures behind the argument: women are about 23% of the South African ICT workforce and, on one recruitment platform's August 2026 reading, about 32% of professionals listing AI skills, up from 25% three years ago, against a global estimate that 30.5% of AI professionals are women.

2026-08-27-itwebafrica-digital-assets-dr.summary: Rwanda's Capital Market Authority is benchmarking its new virtual-asset framework against the United Arab Emirates' and the two regulators have begun work towards a memorandum of understanding, after a study tour that included Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority. Rwanda gazetted its first dedicated legislation regulating virtual-asset businesses in May 2026, making the authority the primary licensing and supervisory body; the UAE side frames the cooperation as part of an initiative to expand regulatory partnerships with emerging markets across Africa.

2026-08-27-itwebafrica-intron-launches-a.summary: A Nigerian startup released Sahara v2.5, an African speech-recognition model built to follow speakers who switch between English and a local language mid-sentence, unveiled at the 2026 Deep Learning Indaba in Lagos. It supports bilingual recognition across 12 African language pairs alongside trilingual Kinyarwanda-English-French recognition; the published benchmarks are the developer's own.

2026-08-27-itwebza-1stream-iso-42001-ai-.summary: A South African customer-experience technology provider says it is the first in the country certified to ISO/IEC 42001, the international management-system standard for artificial intelligence. It gives no certification date of its own, and presents the standard as a way of operating to a recognised governance regime ahead of domestic rules.

2026-08-27-itwebza-reunert-ai-governance.summary: A diversified South African technology group set out its approach to buying, governing and deploying artificial intelligence across the business, with employees using commercial assistant tools under licence. It is an account of corporate adoption rather than of any public instrument.

2026-08-27-kenyans-co-ke-kabogo-ai-platf.summary: Kenya's ICT cabinet secretary put up a platform, hosted on his own official website, intended as a single entry point routing citizens to the agency or service responsible for a given digital programme. Its developers say it will launch once the underlying information, routing systems and review safeguards are in place, so it is not yet answering questions; no operator, data source, budget or accountability route is stated for a public-information service sited outside a government domain.

2026-08-27-lapresse-tunisia-viescolaire-.summary: Tunisia made school enrolment compulsorily online, and the platform's opening week left parents unable to complete it: non-functional form fields, a re-assignment option offering only private-to-private transfers, and validated entries missing from the printed confirmation. Parents resorted to third parties and public internet shops to finish enrolment and payment.

2026-08-27-mtn-group-africa-data-hub-uae.summary: MTN's formal announcement of the Africa Data Hub Holding partnership named its UAE backer for the first time: Tarek Al Ashram, founder of the Dubai colocation operator Gulf Data Hub. MTN Digital Infrastructure will develop AI-ready data-centre capacity through the joint vehicle with an initial focus on South Africa and Nigeria, with the group's connectivity business a shareholder supplying open-access connectivity; its half-year results booklet of 24 August had named the vehicle but not the partner behind it.

2026-08-27-namibiansun-mtc-n625m-network.summary: Namibia's largest mobile operator said it will put N$624.9 million into telecommunications infrastructure in its 2025/26 financial year, covering coverage expansion, fibre rollout, upgrades and accelerated 5G deployment. The figure is a stated capital programme rather than delivered spend.

2026-08-27-number-of-internet-users-in-b.summary: Burundi's telecommunications regulator put internet penetration below 10 per cent at a workshop on the transformation of digital regulation. Its acting director named unresolved regulatory texts as a constraint, said digital financial services have not improved, and said operators benefit from digital services more than the government does; a universal service fund has been created.

2026-08-27-pulse-uganda-uncdf-digital-in.summary: The UNCDF's six-year digital inclusion programme closed in Uganda, with district officials and implementers urging the government to take over the systems it built before they collapse. Its stated results since 2019 include more than 3.4 million people registered for supported digital services, over a million active users and more than 21,000 digital agents recruited, concentrated in northern Uganda and West Nile.

2026-08-27-rfi-maroc-fuite-donnees-agent.summary: A hacker group said on 24 August that it had published the personal data of 70,000 Moroccan police and intelligence agents, a leak former members of the intelligence services judge at least partly authentic and which discloses details not previously public, including the date of birth of the head of the police and internal intelligence. Whether it is a new breach is contested — a Moroccan outlet calls it an assemblage of data compromised in earlier hacks — and Moroccan media have covered it only marginally.

2026-08-27-swalanyeti-ntsa-sh42bn-ppp-sm.summary: Kenya's transport and safety authority announced a Sh42 billion public-private partnership to design, supply, install and maintain smart driving licences and associated services over twenty-one years. No concessionaire, financial close or first issuance date accompanies the announcement.

2026-08-27-techafricanews-airtel-africa-.summary: Airtel Africa's foundation is offering full fellowships to 20 first-year undergraduates in Uganda reading technology-focused subjects. No selection criteria, value or duration accompanies the announcement.

2026-08-27-techafricanews-connecting-lan.summary: The ITU puts internet use across Africa's 16 landlocked developing countries at 25% in 2024 against 68% globally, while 86% of their population is covered by a mobile broadband signal — a gap between availability and use it attributes to affordability and to insufficient international connectivity infrastructure. Landlocked states cannot reach a submarine cable directly, so their international capacity rests on terrestrial routes and commercial arrangements crossing neighbours, which is the part a national fibre build does not settle.

2026-08-27-techafricanews-ghana-mof-eskw.summary: Ghana's finance ministry adopted a legal artificial-intelligence platform across its legal directorate, reported as the first team-wide deployment of legal AI inside a government institution in the country. The directorate will use it for legal research and advisory work; no contract value or evaluation is published.

2026-08-27-techafricanews-kenya-ca-spect.summary: The Communications Authority of Kenya completed training for its technical officers on operating its Spectrum Monitoring Sub-System, covering interference detection and direction finding, under the maintenance contract awarded to Rohde & Schwarz in 2025. The regulator has published no spectrum audit.

2026-08-27-techafricanews-kenya-tanzania.summary: Tanzania's communications regulator made a two-day benchmarking visit to its Kenyan counterpart to exchange practice in regulating satellite communications. Nothing was signed and nothing issued.

2026-08-27-techafricanews-mtn-uganda-sta.summary: MTN Uganda extended its group-level partnership with Starlink, adding satellite capacity to its enterprise offer for customers in remote and hard-to-reach areas. No coverage target, site count or tariff is given.

2026-08-27-techafricanews-nitda-homegrow.summary: Nigeria's technology development agency reviewed 1,092 IT project proposals from 326 ministries, departments and agencies between July 2023 and July 2026, worth more than N4.24 trillion, and cleared 1,056 of them worth N3.84 trillion. Its director-general urged public institutions towards a Nigeria First approach in procurement so that public spending creates market for indigenous suppliers. The clearance criteria, and the basis on which 36 proposals were not cleared, are not published.

2026-08-27-techafricanews-rwanda-cma-dub.summary: Rwanda's Capital Market Authority concluded a two-day visit to Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority as part of a study tour in the United Arab Emirates, on regulatory knowledge exchange around virtual assets and emerging technologies. It follows Rwanda gazetting its first dedicated virtual-asset legislation in May 2026, under which the authority is the primary licensing and supervisory body.

2026-08-27-techafricanews-safaricom-odpp.summary: Safaricom ran a three-day training with Kenya's Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions on cybercrime, financial technology, digital evidence and emerging technologies, pairing technical and prosecutorial expertise.
