No caseload, conviction or capacity figure accompanies it.

2026-08-27-techafricanews-stratos-lab-ec.summary: Three partners announced a 7.2 EFLOPS deployment they describe as Africa's most powerful AI cloud, running on more than 50 NVIDIA B300 HGX servers carrying over 400 GPUs in carrier-neutral Tier-3+ colocation in South Africa. The pitch is residency: keeping African training and inference workloads, and the data behind them, on the continent. The performance figure is the partners' own and no independent benchmark, customer or price is published.

2026-08-27-techafricanews-zambia-ict-inf.summary: The e-government agency's Northern Province unit is onboarding government employees in Mpulungu, Mbala and Lupososhi districts onto an e-payslip self-service portal, replacing manual payslip distribution with round-the-clock access to employment records, and has connected the Lupososhi district administration to the Government Wide Area Network with a wireless access point so officials can use internet calling rather than unreliable mobile coverage. The same unit is inspecting government office equipment against national standards covering acquisition, registration, maintenance, use and disposal. No enrolment count or completion date is published.

2026-08-27-techcabal-bolt-mombasa-county.summary: A ride-hailing platform and the Mombasa county government launched a programme to license 400 delivery riders through Kenya's Recognition of Prior Learning framework, the platform committing KES 1.5 million to it. Riders complete 21 days of accredited training at a certified driving school before the national transport and safety authority licenses them on demonstrated competency, and the platform will share trip and demand data with the county for infrastructure planning including the siting of electric-vehicle charging points. A 2025 parliamentary report puts the sector at more than two million riders.

2026-08-27-techcabal-hidden-danger-of-ai.summary: A column argues that accuracy benchmarks are the wrong test for artificial-intelligence systems entering life-or-death decisions in Africa, citing global models misreading Nairobi's altitude and giving harmful clinical advice in Kenyan trials. It opens on the reconstructed chat logs of a woman who died by suicide after months of using a chatbot as a therapist, and its claim is that present standards do not measure the failures that matter where users are most exposed.

2026-08-27-techcabal-three-companies-con.summary: Regulator data released on 25 August put active licensed-ISP subscribers in Nigeria at 420,989 in June 2026, up 19.6% from 352,006 in December 2025, with three providers holding close to 70% of the market — Spectranet 111,384, Starlink 98,642 and FibreOne 56,486 — and points of presence up from 2,508 to 2,893. That whole market is 0.27% of the country's 156.4 million active internet subscriptions, and 126 of the 230 licensed ISPs are reported to have a single active subscriber.

2026-08-27-techreviewafrica-smart-africa.summary: The founder of ARED Group argued that Smart Africa should use its relationships with ministers, regulators and policymakers to become a commercial distribution route for African technology companies expanding across borders, questioning why comparable structures exist for global technology firms embedded in the alliance but not for African innovators.

2026-08-27-telquel-affaire-jabaroot-pole.summary: Morocco's national security and territorial surveillance directorates categorically denied any intrusion into their information systems or security databases after a group published what it presented as records of 70,000 police and intelligence personnel on 24 August. They said the data was old material downloaded from databases run by insurance companies and social and health cover bodies, and warned against doctored photographs and falsified documents circulating as security material.

2026-08-27-wearetech-fcsl-invested-plus-.summary: A Nigerian asset manager launched InvestEd+, a free mobile application that lets young Nigerians practise trading shares with notional money against live Nigerian Exchange prices, with explanatory videos and a plain-language glossary.

2026-08-27-wearetech-keagan-stokoe-veras.summary: A South African startup founded in 2025 connects more than a thousand common business services — mailboxes through to project-management tools — so that a company's scattered records can be searched by context, origin and history rather than by keyword. Its co-founder, a lawyer turned software engineer, is its chief executive; no customer count or funding figure is published.

2026-08-27-wearetech-kenya-47-comtes-mar.summary: Kenya's National Treasury gave all 47 county governments until 30 September 2026 to finish integrating the electronic government procurement platform with the Integrated Financial Management Information System, so that tendering, award and contract monitoring connect to budget planning, spending and payment. The deadline lands on a rollout that has already slipped: a first phase launched in April 2025 for extension to all national and local administrations from 1 July 2025, against resistance from the Council of Governors over pace and service disruption, with more than 900 public entities migrated by February 2026.

2026-08-27-wearetech-kenya-flowt-leve-de.summary: A Kenyan startup raised funding for a platform that reads small firms' bank and accounting statements to verify actual revenue, in place of a traditional lender's paperwork, so that small green businesses can borrow quickly to buy stock. No amount, investor or customer figure is given.

2026-08-27-wearetech-ronald-richman-esti.summary: A South African startup founded in 2024 sells ReserveAI, a tool that reads an insurer's own claims history to estimate the reserves needed for future payouts, combining actuarial expertise with data analysis. It is in use with several clients internationally; no client count, pricing or accuracy measure is published.

2026-08-27-wearetech-senegal-gambie-coop.summary: Senegal and the Gambia moved their June 2026 telecommunications and digital-economy memorandum into implementation around four priorities — connectivity, cybersecurity, skills and digital transformation — with Senegal's minister travelling to Banjul to agree the first joint work, and the two regulators separately deepening cooperation on frequency coordination, service quality and cross-border roaming. The structural case is the Gambia's limited terrestrial fibre build and its dependence on a single submarine cable, with only limited terrestrial redundancy through Senegal.

2026-08-27-ynews-kenya-anitrac-digital-l.summary: Kenya's agriculture and livestock cabinet secretary is championing a nationwide rollout of an Animal Identification and Traceability System giving every head of livestock a unique identity and a lifetime record of origin, ownership, health, vaccination and movement, tagged by ear tag and microchip against a central platform readable by veterinarians, abattoirs and traders. The stated purposes are livestock management, theft, disease surveillance, food safety and market access; no operator, legal basis, budget or start date is on record.

2026-08-28-alchourouk-customs-strategic-.summary: The customs administration settled a 2026-2030 strategic plan built around digitisation, presented with a governance charter, its axes covering border protection, an environment for attracting foreign investment, revenue collection, working methods and social responsibility, with assignment letters issued to central and regional structures. The plan document itself is not published.

2026-08-28-alchourouk-industry-ministry-.summary: The industry ministry opened a unified digital services platform, its first service the technical cards governing effective transfer operations - more than 4,000 a year - filed and processed entirely online and interconnected with customs so data is exchanged and decisions notified in real time. It runs on the national digital identity mechanisms and is linked to the enterprise register, with import authorisations and establishment licences to follow on a phased timetable.

2026-08-28-angola-estado-biometrico-risc.summary: A named analyst argues that Angola's biometric border infrastructure, presented as an answer to porous borders and transnational crime, becomes an architecture of political control without transparent contracts, binding access rules and independent oversight. It is an argument rather than a dated development.

2026-08-28-angola-mat-peregrinacao-muxim.summary: The territorial administration ministry stationed voter-register update brigades at the Muxima sanctuary from 29 August to 6 September, run through the single public service counter, with pilgrims needing an identity card or voter card to take part. The register's national director put more than a million citizens already enrolled for the 2027 general election.

2026-08-28-angop-angosat-2-quirimbo.summary: Quirimbo municipality in Cuanza-Sul was connected under Angola's programme to recover and migrate ANGOSAT-2 connectivity antennas, delivered by startups of the national space programme. It follows a point restored at Quiage in Bengo the day before; no running total of live sites accompanies the site-by-site reports.

2026-08-28-aps-morocco-denies-data-intru.summary: Morocco denied any intrusion into its security information systems or databases after a hacking group published what it presented as the names, identification numbers and dates of birth of 70,000 police and intelligence personnel. The national security and territorial surveillance directorates placed the records instead in databases run by insurance companies and social and health cover bodies. No insurer or cover body has answered, and no regulator has ruled on the provenance.

2026-08-28-assabahnews-industry-ministry.summary: A second account of the same platform, adding that the first service is in production and that the remaining services follow in phases.

2026-08-28-au-worldbank-integrating-afri.summary: The African Union, the World Bank and UNECA announced the launch of Integrating Africa: From Threads to Hubs, a publication on how deeper regional integration could raise intra-African trade and support industrialisation, at the AU headquarters and online on 28 August. The advisory carries no findings.

2026-08-28-biometricupdate-digital-id-fi.summary: New benchmarking from four development institutions argues that interoperable digital identity, payment infrastructure and continental digital-trade work are accelerating financial inclusion at a pace that varies by country, putting Nigeria's identity register above 126 million enrolled, Ethiopia's Fayda above 15 million against a 90 million target, and Rwanda's system at near-universal adult coverage. It is a reference study rather than a dated development in any one place.

2026-08-28-citizen-za-sassa-whatsapp-sel.summary: The social security agency opened a messaging self-service channel letting a grant beneficiary check application status, review status and proof-of-life verification without visiting an office, after identity verification by mobile number, one-time PIN and identity number. No usage figure is published.

2026-08-28-clubofmozambique-press-media-.summary: Mozambique's Press and Media Law, Law No. 19/2026, was presented publicly from 28 August for entry into force in December, bringing online-only publications inside the media framework and capping direct and indirect foreign capital in a media organisation at 35 per cent of share capital. It replaces a law in force since 1991, requires prior registration and an editorial charter, and limits a foreign media organisation to two accredited correspondents.

2026-08-28-comric-telecommunications-sec.summary: The industry body for South Africa's major operators published its annual sector report, covering fraud, cyberattack, infrastructure crime, energy volatility and supply-chain disruption as risks it argues now amplify one another. The report carries no printed publication date.

2026-08-28-connectingafrica-comric-telec.summary: Subscription fraud against South African telecommunications customers and operators reached 14,897 cases in the twelve months to April 2026, a rise of 307%, with every month above its counterpart a year earlier. The industry body reports social engineering over messaging, calls and text overtaking technical intrusion, with AI-generated voices and messages used to make it convincing.

2026-08-28-dailyquery-katsina-fibre-cons.summary: Katsina State began the last-mile stage of its fibre network, the state investment promotion agency coordinating with commercial providers to move from core installation to connections for homes, businesses and public facilities across all 34 local government areas. Right-of-way fees are waived to hold access prices down, and the governor's roadmap targets 2,000 to 3,000 km of fibre and 70 per cent broadband penetration state-wide, with no date given.

2026-08-28-diggers-zambia-cyber-attacks-.summary: A second account of the same seminar, carrying the figures the other lacks: about 26.2 million mobile subscriptions in 2025 against 23.2 million in 2024, about 14.7 million of them mobile internet, and 874 cyber-related police cases in the first half of 2025.

2026-08-28-fintechgate-telecom-egypt-rdh.summary: Telecom Egypt's chief executive told the half-year results call that phase two of its Regional Data Hub should begin operating within one to two months, on economics improved against phase one, with further data-centre projects screened on internal rate of return, payback period and business model. The carve-out of the data-centre assets into a wholly owned subsidiary continues; the finance chief said retaining the business was worth more than the stake sale that was cancelled in July. The repository already records an end-2025 date for this facility that passed unconfirmed.

2026-08-28-international-economic-relati.summary: The finance ministry's international economic relations department is the administrative home managing Nigeria's bilateral economic relationships and its relations with the multilateral financial institutions and donor agencies. The page is undated and lists no agreement or financing volume; it is carried here as the closest institutional statement the repository holds on the subject.

2026-08-28-itwebafrica-econet-zimbabwe-g.summary: Econet Wireless says it has fully migrated its operations, mobile money and telecommunications infrastructure included, off on-premise computing and private data centres onto Google Cloud, and intends to sell cloud services on to Zimbabwean enterprises next. No migration date, workload split, contract term or data-residency arrangement is published, and nothing on record states a regulator's position on the country's mobile money platform running on infrastructure sited elsewhere.

2026-08-28-itwebafrica-microsoft-east-af.summary: Microsoft filled its East Africa country lead post, vacant since January 2026, with a Nairobi-based executive who has been with the company since 2012 and most recently ran customer success for East and West Africa. The outlet frames the appointment against the company preparing to bring East Africa's first Azure cloud region and a geothermal-powered data centre online; that framing carries no date, and the repository's dated record of the Kenyan build stalling on power capacity stands.

2026-08-28-itwebafrica-mozambique-amia-l.summary: Mozambique's new artificial-intelligence association inaugurated its leadership in Maputo on 27 August 2026, three months after the country published a draft national AI strategy. The national ICT institute's board chairman described it as a technical platform meant to connect government, the private sector, academia, the technology community and civil society, and said a national data governance policy and strategy is under development. That policy is not yet published.

2026-08-28-itwebza-sa-data-centre-sahrc-.summary: South Africa's major data-centre operators answered the Human Rights Commission's inquiry into the sector's electricity, water, land and environmental footprint by defending their consumption on renewable-energy and resource-management programmes, one stating science-based climate targets and full clean-energy coverage locally. The commission has published no finding, and no independent measurement of the sector's draw is on record either way.

2026-08-28-itwebza-saicta-industry-conne.summary: South Africa's ICT industry association launched Industry Connect, a portal that puts vacancies, jobseeker profiles and professional development in one place, covering roles in artificial intelligence and machine learning, data, cyber security, cloud and software development. It arrives with the government and business partnership entering the third phase of its million-jobs-by-2030 programme, and against a persistent national shortage in those same disciplines; the association's own catalogue of 151 development courses sits alongside it. No user, employer or placement figure is published.

2026-08-28-itwebza-sita-executive-recrui.summary: The State Information Technology Agency told Parliament's portfolio committee it is finalising recruitment to key executive posts, after the Public Service Commission's investigation of government IT procurement over 2020 to 2025 named leadership gaps as a root cause of instability. The commission found 86% of managing-director roles held on an acting or interim basis, board tenures too short for continuity, and irregular expenditure above R2bn across four audited years. The agency carries more than 100 departments and public entities, and some are looking elsewhere.

2026-08-28-lesahel-transformation-digita.summary: A profile of two Nigerien platforms - a domestically hosted social network and an e-commerce and delivery service whose founder won a national competition in 2021 - each downloaded tens of thousands of times. It carries no dated development, and no revenue, user or funding figure.

2026-08-28-lusakatimes-zambia-cyber-secu.summary: The technology ministry said it will keep building national cyber-security capacity and called on the private sector to share the load, the permanent secretary setting out the architecture already in place - the cyber security framework under the 2025 Cyber Security Act, the Cyber Crimes Act, the data protection statute and the electronic transactions framework - against networks, data centres and industrial control systems run across both sectors.

2026-08-28-nigeriacommunicationsweek-nig.summary: The satellite operator disclosed that the two NIGCOMSAT-2 satellites will be vendor-financed and backed by export-import banks, its managing director saying the amount becomes official once financing closes. The piece dates the current satellite's launch to December 2011 on a fifteen-year design life ending in 2026, with fuel management expected to keep it operational to 2028.

2026-08-28-nilepost-blockchain-festival-.summary: Ugandan startups are to look for investment and regional partnerships at a three-day blockchain and artificial-intelligence gathering in Nairobi on 15-17 October, expected to draw more than 3,000 participants. It is a forward notice: nothing in the piece dates a Ugandan milestone.

2026-08-28-platformafrica-emtel-icta-st-.summary: The ICT authority awarded a two-year contract to provide satellite-based internet and communications to Raphael Island in the St Brandon archipelago, a first for the archipelago, intended to strengthen maritime monitoring, meteorological capability and safety in a cyclone-prone area. No service date, capacity or contract value is stated.

2026-08-28-spaceinafrica-cote-divoire-as.summary: The space agency got its first Director General more than a year after the June 2025 decree that created it as a public administrative institution under the higher education ministry, with programme areas spanning Earth observation, space meteorology, astronomy, satellite navigation and satellite communications. The appointment date itself is not stated.

2026-08-28-techafricanews-airtel-africa-.summary: Airtel Africa's foundation reports 500 women in agri-food processing and pottery at Zinder, Niger completing a ten-day programme in business management, financial planning and digital financial tools, and 2,050 women reached across six Nigerian states under a parallel initiative combining training with account onboarding, grants and agent banking. What is established is completed training, not any measured change in access to financial services.

2026-08-28-techafricanews-airtel-uganda-.summary: Airtel Uganda's customer base grew 10 per cent to 19.7 million in the first half of 2026, with data customers up 18.8 per cent to 8.9 million, data traffic up 42.1 per cent and average use per customer up 21 per cent to 7.2GB. Smartphone penetration reached 46.6 per cent. No revenue or average-revenue-per-user figure is stated.

2026-08-28-techafricanews-arpce-congo-si.summary: The Republic of Congo's communications regulator dismantled a sixth SIM box fraud network of the year on 21 August in Brazzaville, seizing two 16-port SIM boxes and associated equipment, recovering 30 Ugandan numbers in fraudulent use, and arresting two people. It puts the network's loss at about FCFA 42m over two months on more than 422,000 diverted call minutes, on its own estimate.

2026-08-28-techafricanews-cote-divoire-p.summary: A late re-report of Côte d'Ivoire's national rural connectivity programme, whose first phase was commissioned at Djebakaha, near Korhogo, on 2 August 2024. The programme's 38 billion CFA franc budget is to reach 575 rural localities in three phases, the second worth 18 billion CFA francs across 240 localities and the third 10 billion CFA francs across 160, both scheduled for 2024 and 2025. The source carries no progress against those later phases.

2026-08-28-techafricanews-maroc-inde-com.summary: Morocco and India agreed in Rabat on 24 August 2026 to set up a joint commission on artificial intelligence and language technologies, opening on systems that handle multiple languages, variants and dialects in dealings between citizens and the administration, and on cooperation around the JAZARI Institutes. The agreement follows the two ministers' February 2026 meeting in New Delhi. The commission is agreed rather than constituted: no instrument, terms of reference, budget or standing-up date is stated.

2026-08-28-techafricanews-mtn-uganda-ebu.summary: MTN Uganda and EBus Xpress launched an electric bus route in Kira Municipality carrying cashless fare collection, attended by the ministers for science and technology and for Kampala. No fleet size, fare, ridership or payment instrument is published; it is the first instance in the repository of public-transport fares being digitised in Uganda.

2026-08-28-techcabal-4g-capital-1bn-disb.summary: A profile of a Kenyan lender to micro and small businesses, founded in 2013 on the premise that unsecured working capital repaid on time is itself the credit record a trader without collateral or accounts cannot otherwise produce. It said in June 2026 that it had disbursed more than $1bn across over seven million loans at a repayment rate of about 95 per cent, with an algorithmic underwriting engine sizing each subsequent loan from repayment behaviour. The figures are the company's own.

2026-08-28-thecitizen-tanzania-pdpc-comp.summary: The data-protection regulator begins on-site compliance inspections from 31 August, after preliminary assessment found limited understanding of legal obligations, inaccurate registration information, difficulty implementing data-subject rights, and personal data leaving the country outside the statutory procedure. Inspections verify registration status, the performance of data-protection officers, and how data is collected, processed, stored and transferred.

2026-08-28-vanguard-katsina-data-driven-.summary: Katsina State issued six planning documents on 28 August, among them a General Household Survey Report and a State Statistical Yearbook covering poverty, employment, livelihoods, agriculture, education, healthcare, housing, water, sanitation and access to basic services across its 34 local government areas, with agencies directed to align their programmes to the new frameworks.

2026-08-28-wearetech-burkina-faso-cybers.summary: Burkina Faso has put 205 state digital platforms through security testing to find and correct vulnerabilities, mapped 1,460 platforms on the .bf domain reachable from the internet, and placed 28 public bodies under reinforced protection, under its national critical-infrastructure programme. No period, finding, remediation rate or list of the bodies covered accompanies the counts.

2026-08-28-wearetech-flexee-pay-tunisie-.summary: A Tunisian fintech launched in 2025 offers 12- to 25-year-olds a payments and budgeting app that needs neither a bank account nor a physical card: users receive money, track spending and pay by QR code or contactless at partner merchants, with a savings feature, cashback and an AI coach giving personalised advice. Parents keep oversight through their own space, scheduling transfers and watching transactions in real time. The product is still in launch phase ahead of app-store release; no user figure is published.

2026-08-28-wearetech-integrity360-cyberi.summary: A cyber security group announced on 27 August 2026 that it had bought an identity and access management specialist operating in the United Kingdom and South Africa, taking the combined business to 900 staff across three continents. No deal value is stated.

2026-08-28-wearetech-pikado-egypte-ia-ap.summary: An Egyptian startup founded in 2022 teaches English to 4- to 16-year-olds through short daily exercises, stories and conversation with an AI assistant, aimed at speaking and listening rather than rote learning, and built to fit either a school curriculum or home use. Teachers get progress statistics, can replay pupils' voice recordings and send targeted feedback; the same technology is sold to employers for 15-minute daily workplace-English practice. No user or customer figure is published.

2026-08-28-wearetech-talstack-nigeria-mo.summary: A Nigerian human-resources platform added a leave module, replacing spreadsheets and email threads with a single place to request holiday and sick leave, show staff their remaining balance and give managers a view of who is absent. No customer or pricing figure is published.

2026-08-29-bbc-arabic-egypt-ai-huawei-us.summary: A tender to build artificial-intelligence data centres for the Egyptian government is reported as a contest between American and Chinese suppliers rather than a procurement. The piece is analyst commentary on the bid already recorded on 26 August, in which more than two thousand advanced Chinese chips were proposed for a training cloud and two inference clusters.

2026-08-29-cameroon-cybastion-douala-ai-.summary: A United States company announced an intention to invest US$75m in an artificial-intelligence data centre and an accompanying power plant at Douala, at the inaugural United States-Cameroon economic and commercial dialogue on 27 August. It is one project among an estimated US$7bn of investment and trade opportunities floated at the meeting, and no agreement, site, capacity or date is on record.

2026-08-29-equatorial-guinea-starlink-av.summary: The satellite operator confirmed on 29 August that its internet service is now available in Equatorial Guinea, on its own and its owner's social-media accounts. That follows the government's opening of negotiations on national digital transformation in March and a July authorisation that covered only North American companies' offshore operations inside jurisdictional waters. No licence, tariff or subscriber figure accompanies the confirmation.

2026-08-29-senegal-gambie-feuille-route-.summary: Senegal and Gambia held the first steering-committee session of their bilateral digital-cooperation agreement at Banjul on 29 August, eleven weeks after signing it at Dakar. The two sides settled four priorities: infrastructure and interoperability, cyber resilience, capacity building and regulatory harmonisation, with rural access to electronic government named among the work. No timetable, budget or named deliverable is attached to any of the four.

2026-08-29-somalia-senate-cybersecurity-.summary: The Upper House gave a six-chapter, 33-article cybersecurity bill its first reading on 29 August, at the first sitting of its eighth term, alongside a separate bill establishing a national meteorological agency. Both are short of the second and third readings the chamber requires. The House of the People approved a cybersecurity law in January, and nothing on record states whether the bill now before the Senate is that instrument.

2026-08-29-southafrica-vexa-coega-ai-dat.summary: A metropolitan council approved a developer's request on 27 August to connect a proposed hyperscale artificial-intelligence and cloud campus at the Coega special economic zone directly to the national utility rather than the municipal grid, for up to 556MW. The developer offered R3bn of municipal and community infrastructure investment against councillor objections. What was approved is the connection; the campus has no capacity in service or completion date on record.

2026-08-29-thisday-tinubu-ippis-forensic.summary: The President directed the finance minister on 28 August to coordinate a forensic audit of the federal payroll system and the payroll, pension and financial-management platforms around it, tracing how ineligible people were enrolled and examining the interfaces with the government financial management system and the Treasury Single Account. A second component is a definitive inventory of every federal agency and its legal basis. No auditor, budget or reporting date is stated.

2026-08-30-electricity-tariff-overview.summary: The energy regulator's tariff page sets out its mandate to set and review retail and bulk electricity tariffs. It names no data-centre or large-load category, which dates an absence Corpus had previously recorded only as unsearched: the country is building data centres against a tariff schedule that does not distinguish them.

2026-08-30-government-digital-payments-a.summary: The Treasury's Government Digital Payments Unit sets out the origin of the country's payments-into-government programme: a 2013 survey found more than a third of receipts still cash-based, a presidential directive that November ordered all payments into government digitised, and a taskforce was gazetted in April 2014. The unit's stated mandate is to digitise every payment into government, raising collection and cutting its cost.

2026-08-30-integrated-financial-manageme.summary: The National Treasury's financial management system, which moves public money from budget to payment, publishes its own site. It sets out six components spanning budgeting, procurement, revenue, reporting and support, alongside a supplier portal and a training academy; no coverage of ministries and counties, transaction volume or audit finding against it appears there.

2026-08-30-integrated-population-registr.summary: The State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services publishes a page for the service that holds the country's population register, the one queried when an agency needs to confirm who someone is. What the register holds, which bodies may query it and on what basis are not stated on it — a gap that matters more now that the electoral commission has confirmed it verifies voter data against the registration bureau.

2026-08-30-rdc-strategie-protection-espa.summary: The Council of Ministers adopted a government-wide strategy against abusive content on social media and digital platforms at its 97th session on 28 August. It sets up an interministerial task force chaired by the communication ministry, a citizen alert mechanism and the integration of media literacy into the school curriculum, and commissions a technical and legal review of how the sector is regulated. The strategy text is not published with the readout, so what counts as abusive content, and what follows an alert, are not stated.

2026-08-30-rwanda-business-registration.summary: Rwanda's registrar general describes company registration as wholly online and free of charge, completed within six working hours on the issue of a certificate of incorporation. There is no minimum share capital, shareholding may be entirely foreign, and a support unit at the board's Kigali offices assists applicants who cannot complete the form unaided.

2026-08-31-africa-smartphone-market-2026.summary: African smartphone shipments fell 7% year on year in the second quarter, the first decline in three years, with the sub-$100 segment down 34%. Average selling prices rose $41 to $202 as memory costs climbed, and a 26% decline is forecast for 2026. An entry-level handset can cost up to 73% of a low-income adult's monthly income in sub-Saharan Africa.

2026-08-31-africaguinee-garde-des-sceaux.summary: Opening the regulators' assembly in Conakry, Guinea's Justice Minister argued for a framework that protects without stifling and regulates without censoring, and called cybersecurity a question of sovereignty rather than a technical one.

2026-08-31-africaguinee-pra-uemoa-assemb.summary: The 12th General Assembly of the audiovisual regulators' platform of the eight UEMOA states and Guinea opened in Conakry, and its presidency passed to Guinea. The two-day agenda was harmonising the legal and technical tools for regulating social platforms against cybersecurity and social-cohesion risks, AI-generated disinformation and deepfakes among them.

2026-08-31-arulos-e-doleances-plateforme.summary: Djibouti's urban rehabilitation and social housing agency runs an online complaint portal, routing debt-recovery and technical problems to named internal divisions. It is the clearest digital citizen-feedback channel the repository holds for the country, and it covers one agency's own business rather than public services generally.

2026-08-31-beltandroad-xinhua-china-data.summary: Xinhua's report on the 2026 China International Big Data Industry Expo in Guiyang profiles Wazisana, a blockchain platform launched two years ago by Zimbabwean entrepreneur Dubuya Thulani, which requires African farmers to upload video of their production process for AI to turn into product descriptions for Chinese buyers. Thulani says coffee, red wine and avocados have been exported through it and the business is profitable; no volumes, participating countries or farmer numbers are given.

2026-08-31-botswana-btc-5g-network-inves.summary: Botswana Telecommunications Corporation will invest more than P240 million (US$17.8 million) in 2026/27 to accelerate 5G, expand 4G coverage and upgrade capacity, targeting a commercial 5G launch in parts of Gaborone by October. That would make it the third Botswanan operator on 5G, the other two live since 2022. Population coverage stands at 97% for 2G and 4G and 62% for 3G.

2026-08-31-businessday-defending-fourth-.summary: A named-analyst column argues South Africa's competition inquiry into media and digital platforms treated the platforms as an economic problem to be metered rather than as media institutions to be held to account, extracting R688m for local publishers from one platform while leaving another largely untouched on editorial conduct. The inquiry found 77% of respondents relied primarily on social media for news.

2026-08-31-cameroon-birth-registration-d.summary: Cameroon will restart special mobile court hearings from September to deliver declaratory birth judgments to one million primary-school pupils holding no birth certificate, after an August assessment found a drive launched in 2024 far from its target. Regional officials were ordered on 26 August to submit pupils' files to the courts before 15 September. The law requires a court judgment wherever the 90-day registration deadline was missed.

2026-08-31-com-justice-nous-contacter-re.summary: The Comorian justice ministry runs an online contact form that routes a request by the sender's profile — citizen, legal professional, administration, journalist — and by its object, which includes filing a complaint, following a case, and requesting access to a court document or decision. It is a structured intake channel rather than a case-tracking system, and no response time or case volume is published.

2026-08-31-com-udc-institut-universitair.summary: The University of the Comoros published the page for its Institut Universitaire de Technologie, listing the institute's departments, laboratories and publications. The page's own fields for the head of the institute, the management team and contact details are empty, so the repository records that the technology institute exists and not who runs it.

2026-08-31-fao-giews-earth-observation-c.summary: The UN food agency's earth observation service publishes country indicators for Comoros: an agricultural stress index, vegetation condition and health indices, and estimated precipitation and precipitation anomalies over a rolling 36-month period. It is satellite-derived agricultural monitoring for a country whose own record holds no national crop-monitoring product.

2026-08-31-itweb-africa-namibia-digital-.summary: Namibia's Communications Regulatory Authority and the German identity supplier Veridos signed an implementation agreement with the Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security for a national public key infrastructure. CRAN acts as national Root Certification Authority and the ministry becomes the first Certification Service Provider, issuing electronic IDs — the repository for digital identity, electronic signatures and identity verification in government services. No timetable or cost is stated.

2026-08-31-itweb-africa-south-sudan-huaw.summary: South Sudan's minister of information, communication technology and postal services, Ateny Wek Ateny, held exploratory talks with Huawei's vice-president for global public business, Eric Ma, in Hangzhou on the margins of the China-Africa Digital Capacity Building and Cooperation Conference. The government is seeking Huawei's participation in e-governance, smart cities, energy and a national data hub in Juba; the report notes the two sides fell out in 2014, when officials accused the company of hacking government email and forging documents, and dates the repair to a Juba meeting in early 2026. Nothing is committed or costed at this stage.

2026-08-31-itweb-co-za-finfluencers-enfo.summary: South Africa's Financial Sector Conduct Authority named unlicensed financial advice on social media one of its highest enforcement priorities, its enforcement head Gerhard van Deventer telling a Regulatory Actions Report roundtable that operating through a platform is no exemption from the licensing law and that penalties have already been imposed on finfluencers. He drew a distinction between financial education and regulated advice, and said the regulator is also looking for a way to engage finfluencers on where that line falls.

2026-08-31-itweb-co-za-home-affairs-reve.summary: South Africa's Department of Home Affairs re-advertised its tender for the supply, hosting and support of the revenue administration system that handles collection, reconciliation and Basic Accounting System reporting, replacing June's generic "400+" site count with a two-tier footprint of 275 fixed sites and 230 mobile units. The revision reframes transaction channels around point-of-sale devices and mobile offices rather than the standalone kiosks and e-Home listed earlier, so bidders must price deployment, licensing and support against a larger and more dispersed estate. Bidding is restricted to suppliers on SITA transversal contract RFB 1183, with a non-compulsory briefing on 4 September and submissions closing 18 September.

2026-08-31-itweb-co-za-mamor-capital-r30.summary: A black women-owned South African venture firm reached a R300 million ($18.8 million) first close on its inaugural fund, anchored by the state asset manager, against a R550 million target. It will back post-revenue South African technology companies. Its founder says the raise took more than three years and that institutional appetite for venture capital in the country is still developing.

2026-08-31-itweb-co-za-samsung-digital-w.summary: Samsung South Africa added Scan to Pay QR-code payments, provided by EFT Corp, to Samsung Wallet, four years after launching the wallet locally in November 2022. The company puts Scan to Pay at more than 600,000 acceptance locations in South Africa and inside over 19 million banking, fintech and financial-services app installations; no figure for Samsung Wallet's own local user base is given.

2026-08-31-itweb-inforeg-alarming-data-b.summary: South Africa's Information Regulator has received more than 8,000 security-compromise reports to date, 1,220 of them since April, a rate its chairperson called very alarming and expects to pass 3,000 for the financial year. It served an enforcement notice on the national bureau of standards over a 2024 ransomware attack, and referred two direct-marketing matters to its enforcement committee.

2026-08-31-mamor-capital-ventures-first-.summary: A second account of the same first close puts the gap the fund targets more precisely: companies with paying customers that are still too small or too risky for a bank loan, in a market where limited exits and thin follow-on funding remain the barriers. Southern Africa recorded R13.35 billion across 1,325 deals in 2024.

2026-08-31-nigeria-chassis-gpu-cloud-sta.summary: A profile of a Nigerian cloud startup building domestic GPU infrastructure rather than reselling foreign compute, aimed at AI model training, real-time fraud detection for fintechs and generative applications. It is positioned against hyperscale data centres and telecom-backed GPU deployments racing to meet the same demand.

2026-08-31-paystack-acquires-allawee-nig.summary: Nigeria's largest payment processor acquired card-issuing fintech Allawee in a 2025 deal never publicly announced, and Allawee will close its business and personal account services on 1 December 2026. Balances, account numbers, transaction history and verification records will not carry over. It is the third brand folded in this year, after a business-banking startup and a microfinance bank bought for its licence.

2026-08-31-puc-gouv-km-portail-unique-ci.summary: Comoros published the concept note for a Portail Unique du Citoyen, a single citizen portal intended to harmonise the country's e-government environment. It places the portal under the Comores Numerique 2028 strategy and the national e-government plan, and names the government enterprise architecture and the interoperability framework as what it is to be built on. No delivery date, budget or service list is stated.

2026-08-31-spaceinafrica-starlink-equato.summary: Starlink went live in Equatorial Guinea on 29 August, its 30th African market, with a consumer order page and residential tariffs in CFA francs. The entry is not a permanent licence: it runs under a provisional approval granted by Vice-President Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue on 29 July, with the state infrastructure company GITGE assessing operations and deciding what regulatory conditions should apply longer term. An earlier framework had confined authorised access largely to oil, gas and strategic infrastructure, and whether that restriction survives the review period is unresolved.

2026-08-31-starlink-16-nouveaux-marches-.summary: Starlink's availability map lists 16 further African markets from 2026 - Mauritania, Mali, Gambia, Guinea, Burkina Faso, Togo, Tunisia, Uganda, Tanzania, Comoros, Namibia, Angola, Congo, Gabon, Cameroon and Mauritius - with no launch dates and regulatory approval pending. Eight of them had been listed for 2025 and the service is still unavailable there, which is the more useful half of the notice.

2026-08-31-techafricanews-banco-bcs-mast.summary: Banco BCS and Mastercard announced a collaboration to expand card and digital payments in Angola, covering Mastercard-enabled debit and credit products, a rollout of contactless payments and improved e-commerce functionality.

2026-08-31-techafricanews-huawei-agentic.summary: Huawei launched its Agentic AI Cloud in Nigeria at a summit in Lagos on 27 August, presenting local cloud infrastructure with data residency and low latency as a base for deploying AI agents in finance, telecommunications, government and enterprise. It follows the company's first hyperscale local cloud in Nigeria in 2024 and an industry-focused expansion in 2025. NITDA's director-general Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi placed it against the National Sovereign Cloud Initiative and the country's ambition to move from consuming technology to hosting AI and cloud innovation.

2026-08-31-techafricanews-lbpay-cameroon.summary: Cameroon-based Looping Binary launched LBPay, a payments platform for transfers, wallet management and moving money between mobile money networks, with bill and airtime payment alongside. It also offers payment links, developer tools and APIs for businesses integrating payments; the company says Cameroon is the initial market with the intention of scaling elsewhere in Africa, and no licensing or partner-institution detail is given.

2026-08-31-techafricanews-mtn-momo-schoo.summary: MTN MoMo Uganda marked ten years of its partnership with SchoolPay Uganda for digital school-fee payment, and handed the SchoolPay team a van at the anniversary event. Neither party gives transaction volumes, fee value or the number of schools and parents using the channel.

2026-08-31-techafricanews-mtn-south-suda.summary: MTN South Sudan opened the Aweil ICT Hub in Northern Bahr el Ghazal State, a digital-skills training, scholarship and innovation facility unveiled at a ceremony attended by government, education and development-partner representatives. It is the first hub the record holds outside Juba, and no capacity, budget, term or intake figure is published.

2026-08-31-techafricanews-mtn-uganda-dig.summary: MTN Uganda graduated 503 young people from its MTN Ace digital skilling programme at the National ICT Innovation Hub, on a hybrid course covering ICT, digital marketing, e-commerce, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. The initiative has now trained 1,191 people in total, and the MTN Uganda Foundation put UGX 5.1 billion through its programmes in 2025, which it says reached more than 60,000 people.

2026-08-31-techafricanews-nitda-infracor.summary: NITDA's director-general Kashifu Inuwa received Infracorp chief executive Lazarus Angbazo for talks on Nigeria's sovereign cloud agenda, focused on operationalising the Investment Strategy — unlocking local funding, increasing private-sector participation and attracting foreign investment into sovereign cloud and digital infrastructure. No commitment, sum or project is attached to the meeting.

2026-08-31-techafricanews-nitda-trains-c.summary: Nigeria's National Information Technology Development Agency closed its 2026 Kids Long Vacation Coding Bootcamp in Kano, Kwara, Jigawa and Gombe, with training still running in the South-South, South-East and South-West. Participants covered coding, computational thinking and digital creativity and received certificates and devices at closing ceremonies; the number of children trained is not given.

2026-08-31-techafricanews-nssf-airtel-mo.summary: Uganda's National Social Security Fund renewed its partnership with Airtel Money to expand voluntary savings through the Smartlife Flexi service, which the fund says lets savers contribute from UGX 500 by mobile phone from any location. No subscriber count, balance or contribution volume is published for it.

2026-08-31-techafricanews-senegal-gambia.summary: Senegal's Minister of Telecommunications and Digital Affairs, Samba Diouf, visited Banjul to review the implementation roadmap for the telecommunications and digital-development memorandum of understanding signed between Senegal and The Gambia. Connectivity, cybersecurity, capacity building and digital transformation were named as the areas discussed, with initiatives to be advanced according to readiness; no first projects, funding or timetable are stated.

2026-08-31-techafricanews-smart-africa-u.summary: Smart Africa and Uganda's Ministry of ICT and National Guidance convened a national validation workshop in Kampala on the findings of Uganda's Digital Entrepreneurship and Innovation Country Assessment. Priorities identified were advancing the Startup Bill, strengthening science and innovation policy, widening access to regulatory sandboxes, and using public procurement to create a market for local startups. The work sits under the Africa-Europe Digital Innovation Bridge (AEDIB 2.0); the assessment itself is not published with the report.

2026-08-31-techafricanews-ttcl-zff-nfc-t.summary: Tanzania Telecommunications Corporation and the Zanzibar Football Federation signed a sponsorship and partnership agreement in Zanzibar on 30 August to introduce e-ticketing at football stadiums through TTCL's N-Card platform. The agreement is also said to cover the federation's wider digital systems and football administration; no value, term or start date for the ticketing service is given.

2026-08-31-techafricanews-yango-fellowsh.summary: A ride-hailing company's STEM fellowship, begun in Zambia in 2024 with 30 students, has become a six-country programme covering Ghana, Zambia, Senegal, Ethiopia, Mozambique and Cote d'Ivoire. It selected 24 fellows from more than 600 applications, with a graduation and pitch day set for Abidjan on 17-19 September. The 2026 cohort is smaller than the single-country intake it grew from.

2026-08-31-techafricanews-zamportal-lupo.summary: An official at Lupososhi District Administration in Zambia's Northern Province printed a road-tax document from his own office rather than travelling to Kasama for it, after the Northern Provincial ICT Unit connected the office and ran orientation on Zamportal, Microsoft Teams and Outlook. The report is a single demonstration rather than a rollout figure: how many district offices have been connected, and which Zamportal services they can now transact, are not stated.

2026-08-31-techcabal-assistive-tech-acce.summary: The Nigerian Communications Commission ran its fourth Hackathon Live Show in Abuja on 26 and 27 August under the theme "Technology Without Barriers", producing prototypes for speech-to-text, real-time sign-language translation, voice-enabled complaints and image-to-voice navigation. TechCabal sets that against the platforms Nigerians are already expected to use: NITDA's guidelines require government websites to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, and the Nigeria Web Design Standards toolkit promised for public feedback within 8 to 10 weeks of its July 2025 launch could not be found published, nor any evidence of Federal Executive Council approval or rollout — while the communications ministry's 2025 Year in Review still lists the launch as an achievement. The National Commission for Persons with Disabilities estimates 35 million Nigerians have disabilities.

2026-08-31-techcabal-sec-crypto-custody.summary: Nigeria's Securities and Exchange Commission opened for comment on 20 August a framework requiring digital-asset firms to segregate customer funds from their own, notify the regulator of material incidents within 24 hours and file a detailed report within 48. Minimum paid-up capital would be ₦2 billion (about $1.5m) for exchanges and custodians, ₦500 million for platform operators, offering platforms and tokenisation platforms, and ₦200 million for virtual asset service providers, each backed by a fidelity insurance bond covering at least a quarter of that. The rules also require a share of customer assets to be held in offline cold storage and SEC approval before a foreign-issued stablecoin may be listed.

2026-08-31-tlcom-eloho-omame-african-ven.summary: A partner at an Africa-focused venture firm managing over $250m argues that African venture is compounding rather than stalling: the building blocks for building and scaling companies are more solidly in place than a decade ago, which changes what investors can reasonably underwrite. It is an argument about conditions, made against three years of commentary about what the market lacks.

2026-08-31-undp-malawi-digital-agency-vi.summary: A second cohort of an introductory computer course for people with visual impairments ran at the Malawi School of Government, training participants as master trainers rather than as beneficiaries alone - among them a secondary-school teacher and a senior labour officer. No commitment, disbursement or budget figure for the project behind it is stated.

2026-08-31-unsd-datas-in-comoros.summary: The statistics division's country page records an ongoing Data for Now project with INSEED as national project owner, prioritising disaster and fisheries data alongside modernisation of the institute's own digital infrastructure for statistical collection, processing, dissemination and storage. The page is undated and carries no output, milestone or completion date.

2026-08-31-von-nigeria-sovereign-ai-gite.summary: Nigeria set out a sovereign-AI agenda at a government leadership summit in Abuja, the technology agency's director-general arguing that sovereignty must cover the whole stack - connectivity, compute, data centres, cloud and models. The Secretary to the Government put figures behind it: a cloud policy targeting US$750m of private cloud and data-centre investment within 24 months, 90,000 km of planned fibre, and a talent programme at about 1.87 million registrations.

2026-08-31-wearetech-benin-phital-azah-w.summary: A profile of Beninese developer Phital Azah, founder of Xèdo, a 2024 company whose platform lets merchants build an online shop by importing a WhatsApp Business catalogue with its photos, descriptions and prices, then centralise orders. It automates WhatsApp notifications through payment and delivery, chases abandoned baskets, settles by Mobile Money or cash on delivery, and carries an analytics dashboard. Azah is also lead mobile developer at Benin's Commission électorale nationale autonome.

2026-08-31-wearetech-cote-ivoire-anka-af.summary: ANKA has separated its businesses at its tenth anniversary and relaunched its consumer marketplace under the Afrikrea name, through which African and diaspora creators sell fashion, art and crafts internationally with cross-border payment and delivery handled on the platform. What the remaining ANKA business now covers is not stated in the report.

2026-08-31-wearetech-gabon-rwanda-digita.summary: A Gabonese Interior Ministry delegation spent nearly two weeks in Kigali studying Rwanda's e-government, digital identity, cybersecurity and public-service digitisation. Gabon is preparing its own government services portal: interministerial consultations for the pilot opened in June 2026 across five ministries, with at least ten services to be integrated by December.

2026-08-31-wearetech-ghana-drone-deliver.summary: A profile of Ghanaian aerospace engineer Ebenezer Sasu, founder of Wingxtra Aerospace, which since 2019 has combined drones with electric bikes, motorcycles and vans for last-mile delivery in African cities, switching mode automatically on parcel size, distance, urgency and traffic. An allocation and tracking system matches vehicle position and drone status to each order and exposes real-time tracking to customers and merchants. Sasu co-founded OrcaDynamics in 2025, designing drones and aerial systems through 3D modelling and printing.

2026-08-31-wearetech-kenya-online-misinf.summary: Kenya's National Assembly has asked the Supreme Court to overturn a Court of Appeal ruling that struck down sections 22 and 23 of the 2018 Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, which criminalised knowingly publishing false or misleading data presented as authentic, with penalties up to KES 5 million (about $38,600) and, for some offences, ten years' imprisonment. The Court of Appeal held the wording too broad, capable of catching people who share content unaware it is false as well as journalists and ordinary users; Parliament argues the provisions reach neither opinion, satire nor good-faith error.

2026-08-31-wearetech-nomba-synafare-sola.summary: A Nigerian fintech and an energy company announced a $1.4 million partnership to finance solar installations for 300 small and medium enterprises, lending directly for batteries and inverters. The stated aim is to cut costly generator use and give businesses stable power.

2026-08-31-wearetech-swvl-egypt-sofico-i.summary: The Egyptian mobility company Swvl agreed a $1.5 million investment with Sofico Holdings, taking its recent raising to $14.5 million. The company says the capital will fund day-to-day working needs and accelerate its expansion into the United States market.

2026-09-01-africa-finance-corporation-wi.summary: The Africa Finance Corporation's own announcement of the combined US$300 million equity subscription with Vision International Investment Company, stating the proceeds as data-centre deployment and consolidation, expansion of open-access terrestrial fibre and investment in new subsea assets. See the WIOCC entries for the transaction.

2026-09-01-ai-smart-tech-digital-transfo.summary: Government and business figures at a Lusaka engagement urged Zambia to accelerate digital transformation through artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, automated sensing and smart security. The call carries no commitment or programme behind it.

2026-09-01-airtel-africa-1-1bn-investmen.summary: Airtel Africa plans to invest about US$1.1 billion across its 14 African markets, its chief executive said, while naming power supply and infrastructure vandalism as the constraints on expanding coverage.

2026-09-01-ben-gouvernance-ia-transforme.summary: Benin placed third in the first Africa AI Governance Index, which scores all 54 African states across eight domains. The accompanying argument is that a governance lead has yet to become anything citizens can point to.

2026-09-01-bfa-facture-electronique-cert.summary: Certified electronic invoicing systems go on sale in Burkina Faso from 7 September 2026 for large and medium enterprises, under the general tax code — the point at which the invoicing regime becomes equipment a business has to buy.

2026-09-01-businesstimesug-uganda-nin-re.summary: Uganda's cabinet approved phasing out the standalone taxpayer identification number for individuals, replacing it with the national identification number already printed on the identity card. Nothing states a commencement date or a transition arrangement for the roughly nine to ten million Ugandans not yet on the register.

2026-09-01-camerounlink-car-submarine-ca.summary: A fibre cut in Cameroon disrupted internet service in the Central African Republic last week, prompting an assessment of the landlocked country's options for reaching submarine cable capacity by another route.

2026-09-01-cisd-computer-support-central.summary: Mauritius runs a central offsite backup service for government electronic media out of the central information systems division, alongside technical support and equipment commissioning for ministries and departments. It is the state's standing backup arrangement; the page publishes no capacity, retention period or restoration-test record.

2026-09-01-cod-cartographie-recensement-.summary: The cartography phase of the DRC's second population census is being operationalised with digital tools and satellite imagery, the central census bureau's technical coordinator said — 42 years after the country's only previous census, in 1984.

2026-09-01-connectingafrica-nokia-lozano.summary: A Nokia executive's account of African infrastructure investment accelerating on artificial intelligence and data growth. Vendor commentary.

2026-09-01-dni-frogfoot-vox-fibre-billio.summary: The DNI consortium subscribed R1.6 billion, about US$99 million, for 34.8% of the fibre network operator Frogfoot and the internet provider Vox, valuing the two at R14.4 billion. The stated purpose is township fibre.

2026-09-01-egypt-mcit-cisco-letter-of-in.summary: Egypt's prime minister witnessed the signing of a letter of intent between the communications ministry and Cisco Systems. A letter of intent carries no value, scope of works or delivery date.

2026-09-01-egypt-pandemic-fund-health-da.summary: Egypt's Pandemic Fund steering committee, chaired by the deputy health minister, named surveillance systems and data exchange as the mechanism for joining the public-health and animal-health sectors under a One Health approach. It is a stated project priority rather than a system in service.

2026-09-01-ghanaiantimes-afcfta-digital-.summary: An editorial on what the AfCFTA Digital Trade Corridor has to get right to matter, following the joint venture agreement signed in Accra. See the corridor entry above.

2026-09-01-gis-mauritius-digital-service.summary: Mauritius will develop a Digital Service Framework setting mandatory principles and standards for every government digital service, from planning through operation, binding all services developed, procured or maintained by ministries. Cabinet noted it on 28 August; no compliance date is set.

2026-09-01-govmu-justice-info-page.summary: The government's justice portal sets out the constitutional and institutional frame — separation of powers, a single-structure judiciary, a human rights action plan — and is the public face of a sector whose digital systems sit in the 2026-2031 investment programme rather than in service. It describes the aim; no court case-management system is named on it.

2026-09-01-independent-uganda-ucc-smartp.summary: Uganda's communications regulator launched a study of smartphone penetration, device cost and usage, against a stated target of full national network coverage by 2030.

2026-09-01-itweb-africa-airtel-nigeria-p.summary: Airtel Nigeria opened two premium experience centres in Lagos, taking its nationwide retail total past 350.

2026-09-01-itweb-africa-egypt-ai-trainin.summary: Egypt is expanding artificial-intelligence and cybersecurity training inside its judiciary under a cooperation agreement between the National Telecommunications Institute and the State Lawsuits Authority.

2026-09-01-itweb-africa-japan-malawi-inn.summary: Japan's ambassador to Malawi met the communications regulator's director general with a Japanese delegation, exploring stronger digital and innovation ties. Nothing was signed.

2026-09-01-itweb-digital-finance-consume.summary: South Africa ran Money Smart Week from 24 to 30 August, an initiative of the committee the Treasury and the conduct authority established to co-ordinate financial literacy, as digital finance growth widens the consumer-protection question.

2026-09-01-itweb-hungry-lion-data-breach.summary: Customer credentials for the fast-food chain Hungry Lion were exposed for about nine months through its consumer-facing web portals, on analysis of stealer-log data finding 23 records tied to its South African domain, 13 of them customer accounts.

2026-09-01-itweb-shoprite-fintech-inform.summary: Shoprite finalised the acquisition of an initial 51% of R&A Cellular, whose point-of-sale platform is used by informal retailers to sell prepaid airtime, electricity, gaming and entertainment — extending the retailer's financial services into South Africa's informal economy.

2026-09-01-mydailynewsonline-afcfta-dtc-.summary: The AfCFTA Secretary-General set out the case for the Digital Trade Corridor: cutting the cost and complexity of intra-African business by ending the routing of African payments through third countries.

2026-09-01-national-payment-system-bill-.summary: South Africa's Reserve Bank governor said the National Payment System Bill will soon go out for public comment, moving payment regulation from an entity-based model to an activity-based one — the change that would open payment licensing beyond banks.

2026-09-01-newvision-uganda-nira-registe.summary: Uganda's identification authority holds 36.15 million people on the national register, close to 77% of a population the 2024 census put at 45.9 million, leaving nine to ten million unregistered. The figure matters because cabinet has just made that register the basis of tax identity.

2026-09-01-nsia-kasi-100mw-ai-data-centr.summary: Nigeria's sovereign wealth fund announced plans for KASI, a 100MW artificial-intelligence-ready hyperscale data centre campus in Lagos offering co-location, cloud, storage and high-performance compute. It is framed as import substitution for compute currently bought abroad; no construction start or cost is stated.

2026-09-01-observer24-namibia-diginam-pk.summary: Namibia's National Root Certification Authority, operated by the communications regulator at the top of the country's digital trust chain, is technically live after a key-signing ceremony; the electronic signature provisions of the transactions act took effect on 15 June 2026.

2026-09-01-reuters-us-hands-off-ai-regul.summary: The United States pressed G20 members against creating new artificial-intelligence oversight bodies at a technology meeting in North Carolina, a position that would leave the largest American model developers unregulated by any new international body. African states negotiating continental AI governance are on the other side of that argument.

2026-09-01-senegal-national-cybersecurit.summary: Senegal's National Assembly adopted the bill on protecting critical information infrastructure and digital security, creating a national cybersecurity authority with legal personality and a special status, backed by a national response team. Adopted is not promulgated.

2026-09-01-shoprite-ra-cellular-techcent.summary: The group's results disclose that the R&A Cellular acquisition closed with effect from 14 August 2026 and that the initial stake is 51%. Financial terms remain undisclosed and the initial accounting for the combination is incomplete.

2026-09-01-techafricanews-egypt-fra-fint.summary: Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority granted preliminary approval for two further projects to enter its regulatory sandbox for non-banking financial technology.

2026-09-01-techafricanews-wiocc-300m-inv.summary: A third account of the same WIOCC subscription agreement, adding no new terms. See above.

2026-09-01-techcabal-chipmango-raises-1-.summary: ChipMango, a California-headquartered chip design and engineering training company, closed a US$1.9 million seed round led by Atlantica Ventures to expand its engineering work and workforce platform across Africa.

2026-09-01-techcabal-grey-yuan-payments-.summary: The cross-border payments startup Grey launched direct yuan payouts into Chinese bank accounts from dollar, euro, sterling and stablecoin balances, aimed at African importers trading with China.

2026-09-01-techcabal-mtn-momo-south-afri.summary: MTN sees the overhaul of South Africa's payment infrastructure as its opening for MoMo in a market where cash still dominates everyday payments and where its mobile money product has not taken hold.

2026-09-01-techcabal-nokia-ai-africa-tel.summary: Nokia's account of a shift in what African networks are expected to do — from moving data to processing and acting on it — as artificial intelligence workloads change network design. It is the vendor's framing of its own market.

2026-09-01-techcabal-tanzania-kimambi-su.summary: The Tanzanian activist and influencer Mange Kimambi filed a 36-page complaint against Meta in a California court on 21 August, alleging her accounts were disabled under pressure from Tanzanian authorities during a period of political unrest. The allegation is untested.

2026-09-01-techcabal-tim-cook-apple-afri.summary: An assessment of Apple's African position as Tim Cook departs: no retail store on the continent, limited reach for its payment service, and a market served largely through third parties and grey imports.

2026-09-01-techcity-nigeria-nin-healthca.summary: Field reporting from May 2026 documented how national identification number registration barriers were blocking access to Nigeria's Basic Health Care Provision Fund; this account follows the community-level responses that resulted.

2026-09-01-techreviewafrica-world-bank-b.summary: The World Bank opened a five-day implementation support mission on Malawi's US$150 million Digital Acceleration Project, to review progress and set priorities for the next phase. No disbursement or results figure accompanies it.

2026-09-01-techtrends-ai-rewiring-legal-.summary: An account of artificial intelligence entering routine legal work for African small businesses, most of which never see a lawyer until something goes wrong.

2026-09-01-thecitizen-tanzania-digital-h.summary: Electronic medical records, interoperable health information systems, digital primary-care tools and artificial intelligence are moving onto Tanzania's health procurement agenda, changing what suppliers are being asked for.

2026-09-01-thecitizen-tanzania-korea-ai-.summary: Tanzania and South Korea discussed using artificial intelligence, hospital information systems and other digital tools to connect health facilities and share patient records. The talks produced no named instrument.

2026-09-01-thecitizen-tanzania-mobile-mo.summary: Active mobile money subscriptions in Tanzania reached 87.05 million in June 2026, up 7.5%, on the communications regulator's figures.

2026-09-01-thestar-monari-when-itax-fail.summary: A column on Kenya's tax portal failing on the evening of the 30 June filing deadline, when the revenue authority itself notified a traffic surge and intermittent delays. The penalties for late filing continued to run.

2026-09-01-togoofficiel-fsrp-agri-numeri.summary: A Chadian delegation from the West African food system resilience programme visited Lomé to study Togo's deployment of digital solutions in agriculture. The account is the host government's.

2026-09-01-undp-malawi-police-digital-fo.summary: Malawi Police officers were trained to identify, preserve and analyse digital evidence, as offences committed through digital platforms grow more complex.

2026-09-01-virtual-reality-primary-schoo.summary: Mauritius is putting immersive virtual reality into Grade 4 to 6 classrooms in state primary schools, across mathematics, science, history and geography and health and physical education. The digital promotion agency implements it for the technology ministry with the education ministry, the Rodrigues Regional Assembly and a university immersive media laboratory. No school count or pupil reach is published.

2026-09-01-wearetech-madagascar-actualis.summary: Madagascar is overhauling its 2014 cybercrime law, with judicial cooperation across borders the central problem where offenders and evidence sit in several countries at once.

2026-09-01-wiocc-300m-techcentral.summary: WIOCC Group signed a shareholder subscription agreement with the Africa Finance Corporation and Saudi Arabia's Vision International Investment Company for a combined US$300 million — by some distance the largest capital raise in the carrier-neutral infrastructure operator's history. The agreement was signed at a technology exhibition in Riyadh.

2026-09-01-wiocc-afc-vision-invest-inves.summary: WIOCC's own announcement of the US$300 million subscription agreement sets out that the money is to accelerate its digital infrastructure expansion across Africa. See the entry above for the transaction.

2026-09-01-wmc-tunisia-germany-financing.summary: Five agreements worth more than EUR100 million were signed between Tunisia and Germany, with about EUR40 million more under discussion for the green economy. The piece asks the question the announcements do not answer: which Tunisian firms will be able to reach the money, in what form and at what cost.

2026-09-02-aljazeera-us-eu-ai-regulation.summary: At a G20 innovation ministerial in Chapel Hill on 1 September, the United States urged other governments to adopt the Carolina Principles, a framework arguing that regulation should not single out particular technologies. The European Commission moved the other way in the same week, sending information requests to more than 30 AI companies worldwide under the AI Act. The two positions are the choice most African governments drafting AI rules will be asked to pick between.

2026-09-02-assabahnews-pm-circular-publi.summary: Tunisia's head of government issued a circular directing ministers, secretaries of state, heads of public enterprises and state controllers to adopt strategic action plans on the governance and performance of public establishments. Among its legal bases is the 2020 decree-law on electronic data exchange between public bodies.

2026-09-02-businessday-africa-ai-governa.summary: Roseline Ilori of Bridge57 Solutions argues that Africa cannot scale AI faster than it can govern it, and that the question worth asking is not how quickly the continent adopts the technology but whether the systems being deployed are safe, fair, transparent and accountable. The gap she names is institutional rather than technical: regulators unable to supervise automated systems, businesses that do not understand the risks, and citizens with no way to challenge an algorithmic decision.

2026-09-02-connectingafrica-egypt-cisco-.summary: Egypt's National Telecommunication Institute and Cisco signed a memorandum of understanding to train 3,000 certified technology instructors in support of the national AI strategy: 1,000 university faculty members and independent lecturers a year for three years, in data networks, cybersecurity, operating systems and AI. The target is the supply of people qualified to teach those subjects rather than the students directly. Cisco says its programmes have trained or mentored nearly 670,000 Egyptian students; no signing date is given.

2026-09-02-cote-divoire-mtnit-mistral-pa.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's Ministry of Digital Transition published its own communiqué on the strategic partnership it signed with the French AI company Mistral on 17 August in Abidjan. The work is a study and strategic audit of the national AI ecosystem, mapping the actors and resources available, and sits inside the Feuille de Route Numérique 2026-2028 and its forty structuring projects. No sum is stated and no financier of the audit is named.

2026-09-02-dayoo-guangzhou-cross-border-.summary: Guangzhou launched a national pilot for international data cooperation, opening a service that lets foreign firms send data in for local model processing and export the resulting tokens, alongside a federated research platform that already links Portuguese, Brazilian and Macau institutions by exchanging encrypted model parameters rather than data. No African place is named; the pilot sets terms that others will have to work within.

2026-09-02-gbc-ghana-cid-interpol-ai-cyb.summary: Ghana's police CID put Interpol's 2026 African Cyber Threat Assessment on the record at the awareness month launch: AI now enables 55% of reported cybercrime in Africa, with related losses of $484 million. CID director-general COP Lydia Yaako Donkor described generative AI supplying convincing phishing messages, cloned voices and synthetic images and video, with cryptocurrency, mule accounts and fraudulent investment schemes moving the proceeds — an industrialised, borderless ecosystem rather than isolated offending. She tied Ghana's exposure directly to the spread of mobile money, internet banking and instant transfers.

2026-09-02-itweb-africa-ghana-digital-fi.summary: A second account of the same National Cyber Security Awareness Month launch, adding the Financial Industry Command Security Operations Centre as standing infrastructure for threat-intelligence sharing among Ghana's regulated financial institutions. See the Cyber Security Authority's launch entry for the campaign itself.

2026-09-02-itweb-africa-mtn-nigeria-flyx.summary: MTN Nigeria launched FlyX, a 5G fixed-wireless home broadband service for locations where indoor reception is weak or its FibreX fibre product is unavailable, at ₦30,000 for 30 days at 50Mbps and ₦45,000 at 100Mbps, both unlimited. The operator holds a target of eight million Nigerian homes on fibre within three years and names lengthy approvals, the physical demands of cable installation and slow cost recovery as what stands in the way. Fixed wireless is the faster-to-deploy substitute rather than the plan.

2026-09-02-itweb-co-za-icasa-concourt-po.summary: ICASA has asked the Constitutional Court to settle whether it may condone a late licence-renewal notice from a class licensee, having lost the question in both the Pretoria High Court and the Supreme Court of Appeal to Open Heaven, a Hammanskraal community radio station that filed two weeks late. The regulator reads section 11(9) of the Electronic Communications Act as granting that power only for individual licences, and section 19(2) as deliberately withholding it for class licences; Open Heaven argues the Act leaves latitude where good cause is shown. The court heard the matter on 27 August and has not ruled.

2026-09-02-itweb-co-za-microsoft-eastern.summary: Microsoft and implementation partner NKUSI-IT Siyasebenza ran a three-day Power Apps skills-transfer programme for 20 IT specialists of the Eastern Cape Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs, at the Steve Biko Centre in Ginsberg, Qonce, covering Power Apps, Power Automate, Power Pages and Dataverse. The partner's recommendation is a province-wide skills and adoption framework around AI and Copilot, cyber security and Azure, which is where a three-day course turns into a procurement position.

2026-09-02-itweb-co-za-mtn-chairman-fint.summary: The chairman of a pan-African operator told its fintech summit that more than $2 trillion flowed through mobile money globally in 2025, of which sub-Saharan Africa accounted for about $1.4 trillion, across 2.3 billion registered accounts and 593 million active in any 30 days. He argued the next frontier is financial health rather than inclusion.

2026-09-02-itweb-co-za-popia-grace-perio.summary: South Africa's Information Regulator called the compliance grace period the data protection Act's key weakness: a public body that remedies a violation within the stated timeframe cannot then be fined. Its chair said the high-value fines issued since enforcement powers commenced in July 2021 have largely not materialised, with bodies either complying in time or challenging in court.

2026-09-02-itweb-co-za-sa-online-retail-.summary: South African online retail crossed 10% of national retail turnover in June 2026 and is forecast at R159 billion in sales for the year, growth of 22.5%, according to Online Retail in South Africa 2026 by World Wide Worx with Mastercard, Peach Payments and Ask Africa. The R29 billion added is close to the whole 2020 online market of about R30.2 billion. Takealot is used by 35.3% of online shoppers, Shein by 21.5% and Checkers Sixty60 by 15%, and PayInc processed an average 934 transactions a minute on Black Friday 2025.
