2026-09-02-kictanet-youtube-tax-pushback.summary: Kenyan creators are contesting the withholding tax on video-platform earnings, which sits alongside the digital services tax, value-added tax on digital marketplace supply and the digital asset tax. The civil-society network carrying the campaign published its own brief on digital-tax reform in 2024.

2026-09-02-lanation-djibouti-forum-natio.summary: Djibouti opened its first national forum on artificial intelligence at the Palais du Peuple on 2 and 3 September, organised by the ministry for the digital economy and innovation under the president's patronage. The framing is explicitly sovereignty: AI as a lever of independence, innovation and development rather than a technology to be received. The forum sits against Vision Djibouti 2035 and UNESCO's readiness assessment.

2026-09-02-lequotidien-reunion-nouveau-c.summary: The Réunion to South Africa cable is scheduled to enter service in 2028, adding route diversity before an older system retires from 2027. Marine surveys run in 2026, with manufacture and laying to follow.

2026-09-02-newvision-starlink-launch-uga.summary: Starlink began commercial service in Uganda, ending the regulatory process that followed a memorandum and a five-year operating licence signed with the communications regulator in May 2026. The licence requires a national gateway and physical point of presence, an operational office, and registration of every device activated in the country.

2026-09-02-nigeriainfo-npf-vigilant-app-.summary: The Nigeria Police Force launched the NPF Vigilant App on 1 September at its conference centre in Jabi, Abuja, a public channel for reporting suspected financial fraud, uploading evidence and tracking a case through to feedback. It was built by the Force ICT Department with financial-sector stakeholders and is meant to coordinate police handling with banks; the Central Bank of Nigeria, NIBSS, banks and fintechs attended. Inspector-General Olatunji Disu said the technology must be deployed lawfully and ethically, with respect for privacy and data protection.

2026-09-02-orange-free-reunion-south-afr.summary: Two French operators will fund the €93 million cable between Réunion and South Africa, one acting as landing party and its marine subsidiary laying infrastructure designed by a French manufacturer. The cable is scheduled to enter service in 2028, replacing a system commissioned in 2002; the partners did not disclose their respective shares.

2026-09-02-premiumtimes-osinbajo-cairo-d.summary: African lawyers meeting in Cairo reviewed and prioritised six pillars of a proposed declaration on children's rights and design accountability, covering safety-by-design requirements, restrictions on exploitative targeting and manipulative practices, and age-appropriate design standards. The session chair argued companies cannot engineer risk into products and then leave children and parents to manage it.

2026-09-02-reunion-submarine-cable-la-re.summary: The Réunion regional authority launched RéuNION, a submarine cable from Saint-Paul to Durban costing €93.1 million and carrying 16 fibre pairs at 20 Tbps each. It is funded by €30m from the EU's regional development fund, €20m from the Connecting Europe Facility and €43.1m from the consortium, and must be built within three years under the European funding terms.

2026-09-02-starlink-launches-uganda-pric.summary: Prices published with the Ugandan launch put a residential 100 Mbps package at Shs203,704 a month against an estimated Shs2.3 million to start, plus a Shs437,036 regulatory charge — against fibre offers from the two mobile incumbents advertised at Shs110,000 and Shs99,000 for the same speed.

2026-09-02-techafricanews-ghana-csa-awar.summary: Ghana's Cyber Security Authority launched the 2026 National Cyber Security Awareness Month on 2 September, themed on securing the country's digital finance ecosystem and observed each October. Director-general Divine Selase Agbeti pressed banks, fintechs, payment service providers, insurers and merchants to treat cyber resilience as a core governance responsibility rather than a regulatory box, warning that lost trust in digital payments would undermine the wider digital economy. CSA figures put reported incidents at 2,008 in the first half of 2025 against 1,317 a year earlier, a 52% rise, with reported losses of GH¢14.94 million, more than 90% of it online fraud and impersonation.

2026-09-02-techafricanews-ghana-nca-5g-s.summary: Ghana's National Communications Authority closed applications for 700MHz, 2.3GHz and 3GHz mobile-broadband spectrum on 2 September with four applications received, and opened Envelope A under the published Selection and Award Procedure. Envelope B, holding the Best Price Offer, stays sealed. The authority was careful to say that opening Envelope A determines nothing about the eligibility, compliance or completeness of any application.

2026-09-02-techafricanews-instarc-125m-s.summary: Instarc, a Tallinn-based regulatory-technology firm, raised a €1.25 million strategic investment from HFO Investments to commercialise its compliance platform for South African accountable institutions under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act. The platform covers client onboarding, identity and ownership verification, configurable workflows, document management, retrievable audit records and APIs into existing systems, and the company says it is built to adapt to other regulatory regimes. The date the investment was agreed is not stated in the reporting held.

2026-09-02-techafricanews-kenya-lesotho-.summary: Kenya's Communications Authority is hosting a Lesotho Communications Authority delegation to benchmark Kenya's National Addressing System and the legal framework behind it. Kenya's system is designed to give every street, building and parcel of land a verifiable address, supporting last-mile e-commerce delivery and emergency response, and the authority has driven the draft National Addressing System Bill, 2025 with standards developed jointly with the Kenya Bureau of Standards. No visit dates are stated.

2026-09-02-techafricanews-naseni-xceler8.summary: NASENI launched the Xceler8 accelerator with AfriLabs on 2 September, offering up to $25,000 in acceleration support per cohort to Nigerians aged 15 to 40 who already hold a working prototype, MVP or commercial product. The problem it names is the one that recurs across African innovation programmes: moving a promising technology past the prototype stage into something that can attract investment. The top ten pitch investors at a Demo Day in Abuja.

2026-09-02-techafricanews-nitda-uniport-.summary: NITDA and the University of Port Harcourt's Centre for Information and Telecommunication Engineering concluded the CITE-NITDA Tech Stars 2026 programme, the last of five one-month ICT training series run across Kwara, Jigawa, Gombe, Kano and Rivers states. The courses took primary and secondary school students through artificial intelligence, robotics, coding and data science, with certificates for all participants and laptops and tablets for the highest-placed.

2026-09-02-techcabal-alan-acquires-tanel.summary: French health insurer Alan acquired Dakar-based Tanel in a deal that closed in June 2026 for an undisclosed sum, its first move into Africa and a full exit for Ventures Platform, AAIC Investment and a group of angels. Tanel is a licensed insurer carrying its own risk rather than administering another underwriter's cover, selling employer health plans in Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire across a contracted network of more than 1,200 pharmacies and providers, covering about 70,000 lives and profitable in 2025. Alan had backed Tanel's $2.1 million seed round in 2024, giving it two years of visibility before it approached the founders, who stay on as general managers.

2026-09-02-techcabal-cascador-nigeria-sc.summary: Cascador selected 10 Nigerian growth-stage companies from more than 1,000 applicants for its 2026 ScaleUp Program, a 12-week hybrid accelerator; the cohort includes Venco, SunFi, ColdHubs and EHA Clinics across proptech, clean energy, agriculture, healthcare, beauty, wellness, tourism, minerals and food. Participants become eligible for Cascador's Catalytic Fund, which it says deploys up to $5 million a year in local-currency debt, equity and guarantees, and the programme closes with a Pitch Day for $50,000 in awards. Cascador says it has supported over 70 ventures since 2019 that have collectively raised $125 million.

2026-09-02-techcabal-kayode-adeniyi-geos.summary: A career profile of Nigerian geospatial engineer Kayode Adeniyi that carries unusually direct field evidence about data systems designed away from the places they run in: a 2021 Ministry of Education library survey lost weeks of collected data because the app assumed the connectivity of Abuja's Garki and Wuse, and was rebuilt offline-first around SQLite. His flood modelling in Lere LGA, Kaduna treats herder observation as a higher-revisit sensor than satellite imagery, and a flood-warning system he built issues alerts in Hausa, Yoruba, Efik and Ijebu.

2026-09-02-techcabal-kenya-phone-number-.summary: Kenya's Communications Authority published draft procedures for deactivating and recycling mobile numbers: deactivation only after three consecutive months without revenue-generating activity, then three further months of contact attempts by message and the details given at registration, with at-risk numbers published in national media. The document is out for consultation, with memoranda due 11 September 2026.

2026-09-02-techcabal-mtn-nigeria-arpu-ea.summary: MTN Nigeria's average revenue per user fell 8.82% to $3.41 in the second quarter of 2026, its first decline since Q2 2025, even as first-half service revenue rose 25.9% to ₦2.99 trillion and subscribers grew 8.9% to 92.2 million. Naira ARPU also fell, 1.67% to ₦5,101, so the drop is not an exchange-rate artefact: 7.5 million subscribers were added in the half, against inflation of 15.91%, diluting the average. Nigeria supplied 30.64% of MTN Group's half-year revenue but ranks eighth of thirteen group markets on ARPU, against Ghana's $6.66.

2026-09-02-techcabal-sa-startup-funding-.summary: South African startups raised $335.9 million in 2025, more than three times the $100.4 million of 2024, across 42 rounds rather than 25, with average deal size nearly doubling to $7.99 million. The recovery is uneven: only three of the 42 rounds carried a debt component, and continent-wide the first half of 2026 held roughly flat at $1.44 billion while deal count fell from 252 to 174 and early-stage startups took just $9 million against $25 million a year earlier. The argument is that the money is not absent but badly matched to stage.

2026-09-02-thisdaylive-fg-boost-telecoms.summary: Nigeria's communications ministry named a federal constituency in Abia State a priority area under its universal communications access programme. A tower on the Umuahia–Ohafia road is nearing completion, and a preliminary assessment indicates five to eight further sites may be needed to cover the local government area.

2026-09-02-timeslive-iec-cybersecurity-e.summary: South Africa's Electoral Commission rejected claims that a system failure blocked a party's candidate submissions for the November local elections, its chief electoral officer saying the commission held no reports of a non-functional online nomination system on deadline day. More than 140,000 candidates have been nominated for about 10,500 council seats, to be scrutinised between 4 and 16 September.

2026-09-02-universfreebox-free-cable-sou.summary: A French operator set out its investment in the Réunion to South Africa cable, one of four consortium members behind a system carrying 16 fibre pairs at 20 Tbps each. The consortium is wholly French and about 79 per cent of the cost rests on public bodies.

2026-09-02-wearetech-abe-marcellinus-pme.summary: A profile of Cameroonian engineer Abe Kelvin Bemarc Marcellinus, whose company WorqSphere, founded 2025, gives small and medium businesses device monitoring, threat detection and remote isolation of a compromised or stolen machine that keeps working offline. It holds critical data locally through power and network outages and counts electricity cuts in attendance tracking, and an AI assistant translates security alerts into plain language for firms with no cybersecurity staff.

2026-09-02-wearetech-abwaab-rachete-edua.summary: Jordanian education platform Abwaab acquired the Egyptian company EduAct, which builds software for tutoring centres to manage courses, payments and student tracking. The combination pairs online learning content with physical tutoring centres in Egypt. No transaction date, price or terms are stated.

2026-09-02-wearetech-benin-expert-identi.summary: Benin's ANIP, through the World Bank-financed WURI programme, called for expressions of interest in an international expert on digital public infrastructure strategy, to define a sustainable economic model and institutional framework for the identification agency. The 60-day mission spread over five months covers a strategic diagnosis, a comparison of international DPI and national identity models, and a roadmap for financing, operation, maintenance and modernisation. Applications closed 8 September 2026. The question being asked is how a national ID agency pays for itself once the donor project ends.

2026-09-02-wearetech-koffi-nusiko-dabla-.summary: A profile of Koffi Nusiko Dabla, Togolese and based in Côte d'Ivoire, who co-founded Afoomarket in 2021 as an online marketplace for African agro-processors. Sellers run their own storefront, and the platform carries ordering, card and mobile money payment, a local delivery partner network, seller vetting and WhatsApp support, so a small producer gets a commercial presence online without building the infrastructure for one.

2026-09-02-zap-fibra-benguela-angola.summary: Angola's telecommunications ministry inaugurated an operator's fibre network in Benguela province, the operator having installed a data centre at Lobito as the platform behind its internet and television services along the coastline. The minister named nationwide fibre coverage as the objective and said a submarine cable landing at Benguela is being prepared.

2026-09-03-afdb-koafec-ai-digital-infras.summary: The Korea-Africa Economic Cooperation partnership will put artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure at the centre of its eighth ministerial conference in Seoul, where a new action plan is to be unveiled on its twentieth anniversary.

2026-09-03-almadar-aljadid-mobile-intern.summary: A Libyan operator's live retail tariff card runs from 0.5 dinars for 50MB over one day to 80 dinars for 80GB over thirty. Libya publishes no regulated price basket, so operator cards are the only evidence of what data costs there.

2026-09-03-cardinalstone-nomba-record.summary: CardinalStone Finance extended the facility as a commercial loan, recorded as closed.

2026-09-03-daba-coronation-nigeria-capit.summary: The digital investment platform Daba partnered with Coronation Securities and Coronation Asset Management to give eligible users access to Nigerian capital market products, signed in Lagos.

2026-09-03-dgi-autres-demandes-immatricu.summary: Morocco's tax directorate publishes two online routes to obtaining a tax identifier, which is registration as a service rather than a counter visit. The Fund attributes a 2025 tax take of 24.6 per cent of national output to the full digitalisation of collection.

2026-09-03-ec-international-partnerships.summary: The European Commission programmes EUR 193m of grants for The Gambia over 2021-2027, with digitalisation named only as one clause under jobs and growth. The digital share is not stated, against delivered items that are smaller and specific.

2026-09-03-isdb-ict-sector-ecowas-fibre-.summary: The Islamic Development Bank records financing the regional fibre backbone reaching The Gambia, alongside two other lenders. No date or sum is given, so the scale of the contribution cannot be stated.

2026-09-03-iso-member-profile-gambia-sta.summary: The Gambia Standards Bureau holds Correspondent, non-voting status at the international standards and electrotechnical organisations, and is the country's technical-barriers enquiry point. A correspondent member may adopt standards; it does not help make them.

2026-09-03-iswap-ai-units-nigeria.summary: Former insurgents describe Islamic State West Africa Province running prompt-engineering cells and encrypted satellite links paid for by central Islamic State cadres, turning consumer software to tactical use.

2026-09-03-itweb-africa-east-africa-inla.summary: A fault on an undersea cable can stop card payments and mobile money hundreds of kilometres inland; business leaders and policymakers meeting in Mombasa argued that the continent's digital resilience is decided away from the coast.

2026-09-03-itweb-africa-malawi-connectiv.summary: The World Bank-financed programme carries US$150 million across digital connectivity, the universal service fund's 100-tower rollout, an e-services portal and the national data centre in Lilongwe. Its latest phase is expected to connect more than 500 public institutions and more than 2,000 schools.

2026-09-03-itweb-africa-mtn-momo-ghana.summary: The chief executive of MTN Mobile Money Ghana said that fewer than 0.3% of its users are actively investing and only a small proportion save regularly, against more than 26 million transactions a day, and rejected the description of Ghana as a mature market.

2026-09-03-itweb-africa-tn-cybertech-ai-.summary: The Zimbabwean group TN CyberTech reported profit after tax of ZWG151 million for the six months to 30 June, about 38% up on the comparative period, on a strategy of technology partnerships and low physical infrastructure cost.

2026-09-03-itweb-co-za-implats-ai-cyber-.summary: Implats recorded a limited-impact cyber security breach at a managed operation's IT environment, which does not appear on the Information Regulator's website; its audit and risk committee has made cyber a focus area for the coming financial year.

2026-09-03-itweb-co-za-sita-smme-procure.summary: South Africa's state IT procurement agency spent R183 million with small, medium and micro enterprises and designated groups between 1 April and 31 July, 49% of its available procurement spend against a 45% annual target.

2026-09-03-itweb-co-za-tfg-online-retail.summary: South African retail group TFG reported online sales in Africa up 54.1% in the 21 weeks to 22 August, taking online to 10.5% of sales from 7.1%, while overall sales grew 0.2% to R23 billion.

2026-09-03-itweb-co-za-uct-ai-regulation.summary: A University of Cape Town doctoral thesis argues that South Africa can no longer defer artificial-intelligence regulation, and proposes a constitutional approach built on bias and the rule of law.

2026-09-03-mansat-raqib-lil-shakawi-wal-.summary: Libya's administrative oversight authority has a live complaints and reporting platform covering about 750 reportable state bodies. It launched at a Tripoli anti-corruption event in December 2025; no count of reports received or resolved is published.

2026-09-03-morocco-dgssi-prestations-pro.summary: Morocco's information security directorate publishes its register of regulated providers: audit and incident-response firms are listed, and no qualified cloud provider yet is. The gap matters for a state building government cloud capacity.

2026-09-03-nigeria-kogi-cooperative-digi.summary: Kogi State launched digital registration and mandatory revalidation for cooperative societies, ending manual registration, with transparency and accountability given as the objects.

2026-09-03-nilepost-roke-telkom-paratus-.summary: Roke Telkom and Paratus Uganda launched Starlink connectivity for businesses and organisations, aimed at locations where fibre and wireless networks are unavailable or unreliable.

2026-09-03-nomba-raises-3-million.summary: The Nigerian fintech Nomba raised a US$3 million debt facility to expand cross-border payments across Central Africa, giving it dollar liquidity through banking relationships in Hong Kong and Singapore.

2026-09-03-reaol-remote-areas-solar-elec.summary: Libya's renewable energy authority sets out its off-grid programme: 400 solar systems at 310 kW peak, serving remote population clusters and border posts. It is the largest counted state provision outside the cities the repository holds for the country.

2026-09-03-techafricanews-badili-refurbi.summary: An entry-level smartphone cost 26% of monthly income per head in sub-Saharan Africa in 2024 on GSMA's estimate, and 64% for the poorest 40%. The industry answer has been cheaper new devices; the piece argues the refurbished market is moving faster.

2026-09-03-techafricanews-camtel-anipes-.summary: The state operator CAMTEL signed a framework agreement on 2 September with the association of Cameroon's private higher education institutions, to improve their connectivity and support their modernisation.

2026-09-03-techafricanews-escwa-morocco-.summary: The UN Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia and Morocco's minister for digital transition signed a memorandum in Rabat framing regional cooperation on modernising public administration and digital governance reform.

2026-09-03-techafricanews-gabon-itu-coun.summary: Gabon announced its candidacy for the Council of the International Telecommunication Union at the World Telecommunication and ICT Policy Forum in Nassau.

2026-09-03-techafricanews-kenya-italy-ko.summary: Kenya's ICT principal secretary and Italy's ambassador discussed turning existing partnerships into infrastructure, skills and economic opportunity at Konza Technopolis.

2026-09-03-techafricanews-malawi-36th-ru.summary: The government switched on the 36th tower under the Last Mile Rural Connectivity Project, at Kalira Village in Traditional Authority Kalumbu.

2026-09-03-techafricanews-mtn-ghana-univ.summary: MTN Ghana signed a memorandum with the University of Ghana and launched a hackathon for students and emerging innovators.

2026-09-03-techafricanews-mtn-zambia-alo.summary: MTN Zambia added the Alola Max 2 and Alola 5G to its low-cost handset range, priced from K1,150; the range has sold more than 200,000 units since November 2024.

2026-09-03-techafricanews-smart-africa-p.summary: Smart Africa called for stronger public-private collaboration at the opening panel of the Global Digital Collaboration conference in Geneva.

2026-09-03-telecom-egypt-sharm-el-sheikh.summary: Telecom Egypt signed an agreement to build a multiple-petabit subsea cable between Sharm El Sheikh and Taba, which it frames as extending the country's eastern digital corridor.

2026-09-03-telecomreviewafrica-billing-i.summary: Legacy billing platforms are described as a commercial constraint on African operators, leaking revenue and limiting the pricing models available for 5G, machine-to-machine services and network interfaces.

2026-09-03-telecomreviewafrica-mmwave-mo.summary: Millimetre-wave spectrum has been a long-term bet rather than a revenue source for most African operators; the question is shifting from acquiring high-band spectrum to earning from it.

2026-09-03-telecomreviewafrica-non-terre.summary: Low-Earth-orbit constellations are moving from a last-resort backup layer into operators' core network planning, particularly where terrestrial infrastructure has not reached.

2026-09-03-telecomreviewafrica-private-5.summary: Private 5G is being deployed in African mining corridors, factories and logistics hubs for automation and predictive maintenance, with telcos, hyperscalers and neutral hosts competing to supply it.

2026-09-03-telecomreviewafrica-telecom-c.summary: Attackers are turning artificial intelligence on telecom networks that now carry financial transactions, government services and industrial systems, eroding what had been a defensive advantage for operators.

2026-09-03-telecomreviewafrica-wholesale.summary: A trade analysis argues that African broadband is now shaped less by how much fibre is laid than by wholesale economics: who may sell capacity, who benefits from infrastructure, and at what price.

2026-09-03-the-star-acbf-leaps-public-se.summary: The African Capacity Building Foundation argued that sound policies and public financial management reforms are failing at implementation because of leadership gaps, institutional fragmentation and resistance to change.

2026-09-03-uptime-institute-km4-data-cen.summary: A tier III design certification is recorded for the Libyan national telecom company's KM-4 site, the first independent assessment of a Libyan facility the repository holds. It certifies design rather than construction or operation, and no capacity figures are disclosed.

2026-09-03-utg-school-of-information-tec.summary: The University of The Gambia's technology school offers three bachelor's degrees plus six-month diplomas in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and data science. It is the widest named domestic provision the repository holds for the country.

2026-09-03-village-capital-nga-record.summary: Village Capital deployed US$450,000 from its US$4 million Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility into two Nigerian companies, the small-business lending platform Trade Lenda and the agricultural-waste firm AirSmat. The per-company split is not stated.

2026-09-03-village-capital-nigeria-inves.summary: The facility's first Nigerian investments follow two Ghanaian ones earlier in the year, taking its portfolio further across the region.

2026-09-03-wearetech-askya-fund-ai-start.summary: Askya Investment Partners opened a free support programme for African artificial-intelligence startups, offering strategic advice and up to US$200,000 of investment without taking equity.

2026-09-03-wearetech-drc-ai-education-di.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo intends to give internet access, digital resources and artificial intelligence more room in the 2026-27 school year, against access constraints that start at connecting pupils at all.

2026-09-03-wearetech-techstars-bunge-fin.summary: FindHomes, founded in South Africa in 2024 by Adrian Bunge, applies artificial intelligence to property search and market data for buyers.

2026-09-03-wearetech-techstars-faul-akil.summary: Akili AI, co-founded in South Africa in 2025 by Charles Faul, builds artificial-intelligence tools for consultation data and hospital workflow.

2026-09-03-world-bank-id4d-2-8b-excluded.summary: The World Bank's ID4D Global Dataset 2025 estimates that 2.8 billion people remain outside government-recognised digital identity systems, and finds new gender gaps opening in digital identity even as the gap in standard legal identity has closed.

2026-09-04-africa-cdc-biim-framework-val.summary: Africa CDC and member states validated components of a continental behavioural intelligence and infodemic management framework at a five-day meeting in Mombasa, with participants from six countries alongside the ECOWAS regional surveillance centre and the WHO Africa Infodemic Response Alliance. The framework is to turn community feedback, social listening, service-delivery and programme data and rapid research into decision-ready intelligence; Africa CDC states it is not another database or reporting platform.

2026-09-04-ben-cadastre-a-parakou-196-47.summary: Parakou became the first Benin commune with complete cadastral coverage, 196,474 parcels registered across about 56,390 hectares, with results presented to a Netherlands embassy delegation. Platform data put 38% of registered parcels in men's ownership against 7% women's and 3% collectivites, with the owners of 21% unidentifiable; more than 11,500 cadastral registration certificates had been distributed door to door.

2026-09-04-bizwatch-lagos-nigeria-digita.summary: A technology adviser to the Lagos State governor called for Nigeria to lead Africa in digital finance, tokenised assets and cross-border settlement, at the close of a three-day digital finance summit in Lagos. He said regulation, infrastructure and trust are what would attract global capital, and urged Lagos to position itself as a hub for cross-border settlements.

2026-09-04-cod-le-pari-de-la-banque-cent.summary: The Central Bank of Congo instructed its technical services to draw up a roadmap for modernising the national payments system, its governor said after a central bank payments conference in Istanbul. The stated aims are the security, fluidity and continuity of transactions and assessing the uses and risks of artificial intelligence, tokenisation, stablecoins and central bank digital currencies; the delegation gave sustained attention to offline payment, given electricity and internet constraints in several parts of the country.

2026-09-04-connectingafrica-sa-ecommerce.summary: South African cross-border e-commerce growth fell to 7% in 2025 from an annual range of 30 to 50% before 2024, after the November 2024 removal of the small-parcel import concession put parcels under R500 on the standard 45% duty plus 15% VAT. Shein's growth slowed to 11% and Temu recorded an average monthly decline of 42%, while roughly 19 million cross-border platform orders in 2025 still made up 18.6% of South African e-commerce transactions.

2026-09-04-developingtelecoms-egypt-taba.summary: Telecom Egypt signed an agreement with the Greek contractor Power Sub Link to build a 200 km repeaterless subsea cable from Sharm El Sheikh to Taba up the Gulf of Aqaba coast, designed for 5 Pbps. It will interconnect with the Red Sea festoon system that forms the southern half of the Red2Med route to Port Said. No cost or in-service date is stated.

2026-09-04-ecofin-egypte-cable-sous-mari.summary: Egypt plans a roughly 200 km subsea cable from Sharm El Sheikh on the Red Sea to Taba on the Gulf of Aqaba, carried by Telecom Egypt with the Greek company Power Sub Link, adding high-capacity domestic routing options. The account notes the country already has the continent's largest concentration of submarine cables, about twenty connected with five more under construction.

2026-09-04-ecofinagency-malawi-private-i.summary: The information and communications technology ministry called for private investment in telecommunications and fibre infrastructure at a rural broadband consultation on 31 August, arguing that public resources cannot finance the expansion alone.

2026-09-04-egypt-sovereignty-huawei-us-a.summary: A commentary sets out Egypt as the first country to receive competing artificial-intelligence data-centre bids from both superpowers: a 102-page Huawei proposal covering military, surveillance and public-sector use obtained on 26 August, against a United States counter-offer that has not been published. China's president arrived in Cairo on 1 September and agreements on artificial intelligence and technology transfer were reported being signed that week; no award is on file.

2026-09-04-igad-ai-framework-consultatio.summary: IGAD opened a two-day consultation in Addis Ababa to develop a common Horn of Africa framework and strategy for artificial intelligence. Its executive secretary put data sovereignty and accountability at the centre, set three priorities - directing investment where socioeconomic impact is greatest, closing gaps in infrastructure, policy and skills, and building regional synergies through harmonisation - and insisted the framework be owned by member states rather than treated as a secretariat project.

2026-09-04-inatel-kinshasa-kia-mona-prot.summary: The Algerian state electronics firm INATEL, with PGS Africa and DABYAN, signed a protocol with the coordination of the DRC's Kinshasa expansion project for an integrated digital, industrial and technological programme covering digital technologies, electronic payment systems, digital equipment and services, knowledge transfer and a centre for innovation in payment systems, cybersecurity and applied artificial intelligence. No amount is stated.

2026-09-04-infosgabon-ceeac-frontiere-nu.summary: ECCAS member states met in Douala from 31 August to 4 September to draft a regional framework governing cross-border data flows in Central Africa, assessing national readiness and consolidating country contributions into a consensus on the pillars of a future instrument. Technical and financial support came from GIZ, AUDA-NEPAD, the Economic Commission for Africa and the African Union Commission.

2026-09-04-itweb-discovery-bank-ai-super.summary: Discovery Bank, South Africa's digital-only bank, reported a R370 million normalised operating profit for the year to 30 June 2026, reversing a R68 million loss. Client numbers rose 26% to 1.57 million and revenue 31% to R3.1 billion; it targets R3 billion annual profit by 2029 and launches on 1 October the second phase of a strategy connecting the group's banking, health, insurance and investment businesses through AI-driven personalisation in one app.

2026-09-04-itweb-lelapa-ai-african-langu.summary: The South African artificial-intelligence research and product lab Lelapa AI plans to add text-to-speech to its product line and to expand its language base beyond Africa, its chief executive told an ITWeb interview, framing the work as building efficient models relevant to the African context while growing revenue enough to sustain the mission.

2026-09-04-itweb-rand-water-cyberattack.summary: Rand Water, Africa's largest bulk water utility and supplier to more than 16 million people, disclosed a cyber security incident on 3 September and is operating from its Centurion disaster-recovery site while it establishes the extent of the damage. Its debt officer said intruders reached some servers at night before IT staff could block them and that some servers were damaged; water treatment, quality control and bulk supply are stated to remain fully operational.

2026-09-04-itwebafrica-egypt-heka-data-h.summary: Egypt is exploring an integrated hub for hyperscale data centres and artificial intelligence with the United States digital infrastructure company Heka Data, in talks that would draw on the country's location, fibre networks and subsea cables to strengthen its position as a regional hub for data centres, cloud computing and digital services.

2026-09-04-itwebafrica-malawi-police-dig.summary: The Malawi Police Service introduced electronic payment of traffic fines, going live at headquarters in Lilongwe and across the country's six police regions from the week of 4 September, with payment through named commercial banks and both mobile money services. The ICT industry association welcomed it as fraud-reducing but urged the service to secure the system and to train staff and inform the public.

2026-09-04-itwebafrica-uganda-500bn-digi.summary: Uganda's ICT and national guidance minister set digital infrastructure, data and artificial intelligence as instruments of a tenfold growth strategy toward a US$500 billion economy, opening the third annual ICT National Summit in Kampala. She called for investment in digital skills, stronger local innovation and scaled homegrown solutions, and named digital fraud, misinformation and cyber threats as the counterweight.

2026-09-04-itwebafrica-zimbabwe-internet.summary: Zimbabwe's internet and data traffic rose 57.28% in the first quarter of 2026, the regulator reported, attributing it to faster LTE and 5G deployment, rising smartphone adoption and data-hungry applications. Operators added 13 5G base stations in the quarter to reach 379, covering 18.94% of the population, and deployed 161 further LTE sites; mobile internet and data was the largest revenue contributor at 46.34% of quarterly operator revenue.

2026-09-04-kenya-digital-economy-private.summary: Kenya's Cabinet Secretary for Information, Communications and the Digital Economy opened the digital economy to greater private investment at an East Africa private capital conference, naming fibre and wireless networks, data centres, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, digital services and business process outsourcing as the opportunities and citing growth of 4.6% in 2025 and 5.3% in the first quarter of 2026. No instrument, amount or counterparty is named.

2026-09-04-kenya-ruto-at-four-ecitizen-d.summary: A four-year retrospective on Kenya's eCitizen platform records the count of services rising from about 350 in 2022 to 20,855 by 2024, with the president saying in November that the platform hosted 22,515 services and more than 13 million users. The piece sets that expansion against the platform's contested governance and reliability.

2026-09-04-liberia-massaquoi-lta-strateg.summary: Liberia's telecommunications regulator is being run to its 2025-2029 strategic plan, which puts universal connectivity, digital inclusion, consumer protection, regulatory oversight, innovation and investment at its centre. Its acting chairperson's programme is described as extending internet access to schools and underserved communities, strengthening consumer protection, opening the country to satellite connectivity and returning it to regional telecommunications affairs.

2026-09-04-malawi-farmers-digital-plant-.summary: Farmers, extension workers, agro-dealers and policymakers tested Malawi's digital plant-health service and proposed changes before wider rollout. Its voice platform reaches basic-phone users in Chichewa and other local languages and takes around 30,000 calls a month despite never having been publicly promoted since its June 2025 launch; participants asked for coverage of soil health, fertilisers, irrigation and weather and for changes to visualisations, language and accessibility.

2026-09-04-malawi-mahis-digital-health-r.summary: Malawi's health ministry has begun piloting a digital health records system intended to replace hard-copy health passport books, at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital in Blantyre and selected health centres nationwide. Each patient is given a unique identifier stored on a server linked to facilities through an interoperability layer, and the ministry expects most facilities digitised within about a year.

2026-09-04-malawi-pppc-dmap-momentum.summary: A World Bank mission team on the Digital Malawi Acceleration Project called on the ICT minister in Lilongwe, its task team leader saying the project anticipates funding for around 100 additional cell towers and connectivity for 500 government institutions, with biometric digital ID among key procurements. The minister said existing capacity of 12.5 Gbps is insufficient and called for at least 50 Gbps, a future-ready national data centre and integration of all ministries under the Bomalathu eService Portal.

2026-09-04-mozambique-atdi-portal-do-cid.summary: Mozambique's digital transformation agency formally presented the Portal do Cidadao at the 61st Maputo international fair, a platform to centralise and digitise about 140 public services nationwide and remove the need to travel to different state institutions.

2026-09-04-mtn-ghana-ai-training-media-c.summary: MTN Ghana trained journalists and civil society representatives in Accra on the capabilities, limitations and responsible use of artificial intelligence in their work, covering prompting and practical applications of tools including ChatGPT for research, content development, data analysis and everyday workflow.

2026-09-04-mznews-mozambique-portal-cida.summary: Mozambique's digital transformation agency unveiled the Portal do Cidadao at the Maputo international fair, a single virtual counter for about 140 public services where citizens check requirements, submit applications, track case status, receive notifications and obtain official documents remotely. The agency named two supporting pillars - interoperability between public bodies so citizens are not asked twice for the same data, and a digital identity for secure authentication.

2026-09-04-niger-mobile-network-quality-.summary: Niger's electronic communications and post regulator launched a campaign on 27 July to verify mobile network coverage and the voice and data service map. A press account reports users facing poor quality for several months - interrupted calls, correspondents shown as unavailable or engaged - with the regulator's expert findings still awaited.

2026-09-04-ohlgs-celltel-261-assemblies-.summary: Ghana's Office of the Head of the Local Government Service signed a memorandum with Celltel Networks to turn all 261 metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies into what both parties call smart assemblies, under a Local Government Service IT Infrastructure and Systems Improvement Programme spanning waste management, public safety, education, healthcare, environmental monitoring and citizen engagement. No contract value, financing structure or timeline is stated.

2026-09-04-op-ed-nigerias-digital-future.summary: An opinion piece argues that Nigeria's digital future depends on pairing innovation with accountable institutions and a fairer distribution of opportunity, taking a 1973 newspaper report of a N44,000 fraud at the electricity authority as its starting point for a question about turning resources and ingenuity into lasting public benefit.

2026-09-04-punch-katsina-fibre-optic-inv.summary: Katsina State called for public-private collaboration to expand fibre optic infrastructure and make connectivity affordable, at a sensitisation programme on fibre deployment. The state investment promotion agency's director-general told regulators, operators and businesses that fibre is investment infrastructure rather than a telecommunications issue, and that the state's fibre drive should be measured by the businesses, households and institutions actually connected rather than by kilometres deployed.

2026-09-04-sanews-south-africa-ai-workfo.summary: South Africa's government told NEDLAC's annual summit that the transition to an artificial-intelligence-enabled economy must not leave workers behind, warning that technological progress is not automatically inclusive and can deepen inequality, displace workers and widen the digital divide if poorly managed. The answer was put in education and re-skilling, worker protection as workplaces automate, and social dialogue; no programme, budget or instrument was announced.

2026-09-04-syc-travizory-former-minister.summary: Seychelles' Commission of Inquiry into the border management agreement with Travizory Border Security heard testimony from two former ministers on how the country initially explored established international providers before Travizory entered the picture. The report is paywalled beyond that point.

2026-09-04-techafricanews-egypt-heka-dat.summary: Egypt's communications minister met the data-centre developer Heka Data and the United States consortium it leads to discuss an integrated data-centre and artificial-intelligence hub, covering the project's concept, scale, implementation phases, investment and job potential and the integration of digital infrastructure with power supply. No investment figure, site or timetable was stated.

2026-09-04-techafricanews-ethio-telecom-.summary: Ethio Telecom set 2026/27 targets of 96.2 million customers and ETB 295 billion revenue in its annual business plan, the second year of its Next Horizon strategy. The plan raises 4G capacity from 22.79 million to 35.31 million subscribers and 4G population coverage from 82.23% to 95%, 5G sites from 340 to 648 and 5G towns from 33 to 73, backbone fibre from 23,442 km to 25,642 km and gateway capacity from 4.3 Tbps to 5.2 Tbps, with telebirr targeted at 67.69 million customers.

2026-09-04-techafricanews-icasa-cybertek.summary: South Africa's communications regulator approved the transfer of Cybertek's individual electronic communications network service and electronic communications service licences to Optipulse on 18 August, in a notice under section 9(5) of the Electronic Communications Act. The approval is a change of ownership of the licensed operations.

2026-09-04-techafricanews-nitda-digital-.summary: NITDA's director-general told GITEX Nigeria that digital skills, innovation and human capital rather than physical resources will decide the country's economic future, pointing to the integration of digital skills into formal education and to the 3 Million Technical Talent programme as the pipeline, and saying the agency's remit extends past producing skilled Nigerians to making those skills into businesses and products.

2026-09-04-techafricanews-orange-cote-di.summary: Orange Cote d'Ivoire warned it may take legal action after construction works severed several of its telecommunications cables in an Abidjan district on 2 September, disrupting fixed, mobile and internet services for more than 1,121 customers. The operator named the construction company responsible, cited repeated damage to its fibre and called on construction firms to coordinate better when working near telecommunications infrastructure.

2026-09-04-techafricanews-safaricom-ethi.summary: Safaricom Ethiopia passed 15 million 90-day active subscribers in under four years of commercial operation, marking five years since its unified licence of 9 July 2021. It has deployed more than 3,500 network sites, all 4G-enabled and 5G-ready, reaching about 60% of the population, and says the growing base is moving the business towards breakeven; it puts community investment at ETB 684 million over four years.

2026-09-04-techcabal-mtn-fintech-serigne.summary: MTN Group Fintech's chief executive set out a plan to convert the group's 317 million telecom subscribers into a single closed-loop financial ecosystem, from a base of about 70 million mobile money users, in an interview covering a lending business processing 18 loans per second and a partnership with Ant International.

2026-09-04-techcabal-nigeria-telecom-mar.summary: Nigeria's telecoms regulator published three consecutive months of unchanged subscriber figures for T2 Mobile because the operator filed no reports, putting its base at 802,534 for April, May and June 2026 while its own porting data showed a net loss of 1,824 subscribers. Glo grew 7.8% between April and May then lost 7.3% in June, and the regulator recorded more than 5,000 fibre cuts nationally in the first half of 2026.

2026-09-04-techcabal-sun-king-smartphone.summary: Sun King began selling financed smartphones in Kenya, entering the market M-KOPA and Watu built. Its handset is sold only on a pay-as-you-go contract - a KES 2,299 deposit and KES 55 a day for 365 days, KES 22,374 in all - repaid through the phone's own lock screen, app, SIM toolkit or USSD, with the device locked if payments stop. The company opened a Tatu City assembly plant with capacity for 700,000 units a year in October 2025.

2026-09-04-techreviewafrica-africanenda-.summary: AfricaNenda's deputy chief executive called for a balanced regulatory approach as artificial intelligence, digital currencies, stablecoins and tokenised assets reshape payments, telling a central bank payments conference in Istanbul that financial stability, security, competition and inclusion remain central priorities while policymakers must reconcile innovation with stability and changing geopolitical realities.

2026-09-04-thewill-vertiv-airtel-africa-.summary: Vertiv, the power and cooling vendor named in October 2025 for Airtel Africa's Nxtra data centre in Lagos, agreed to acquire UtilityInnovation Group for up to US$2.6 billion, about US$1.45 billion in cash at closing with the balance tied to earnings targets over 12 and 24 months. The report puts the Lagos site's planned capacity at 42MW over four construction phases to 2028, where Airtel Africa's own website gives 38MW, a difference neither company has reconciled.

2026-09-04-tza-fintechs-banks-partnershi.summary: The UN Capital Development Fund counted 171 active fintech companies in Tanzania in 2026, up from 33 in 2021, against more than 70% of adults holding a mobile money account and 6.4 billion digital payment transactions in 2024. Founders and the fund told a Dar es Salaam session that partnerships with banks and mobile operators remain the main barrier to scale, citing banks assessing early-stage firms through a static lens, limited patient capital, talent shortages, regulatory and tax uncertainty and customer acquisition costs.

2026-09-04-tza-wtpf-session-ict-prioriti.summary: Tanzania set out three ICT priorities at the ITU's seventh World Telecommunication/ICT Policy Forum in Nassau: expanding affordable access, strengthening digital skills and AI use across social groups, and building secure and inclusive infrastructure that protects personal data. The communications minister said the country had completed 758 4G towers reaching more than 1,400 villages and about 8.5 million people, established 800 digital clubs, provided Wi-Fi at 100 public locations and computer laboratories in 250 public schools.

2026-09-04-uga-jica-makerere-ai-research.summary: Makerere University and Japan's international cooperation agency explored strengthening academic, research and innovation collaboration between Uganda, Japan and other African countries, with a focus on artificial intelligence, aerospace engineering, materials and remote sensing, food value chains, energy, water and climate change.

2026-09-04-uneca-quantum-computing-afric.summary: An Economic Commission for Africa blog argues that quantum computing is advancing fast enough to reshape economies, digital security, payment systems and scientific discovery, and that the question for Africa is not whether it will transform the world but whether the continent will be ready when it does.

2026-09-04-wearetech-cote-divoire-700-se.summary: Cote d'Ivoire set a target of 700 high-impact digital public services by 2029 and a zero-paper administration by 2030, at a national prioritisation workshop in Abidjan. A first portfolio of about 100 services is to be built or rebuilt on the national interoperability platform so one administration can draw on data another already holds; the ministry acknowledged that data exchange between existing platforms remains limited and that some functions were built twice.

2026-09-04-wearetech-djibouti-strategie-.summary: Djibouti presented the main lines of its first national artificial-intelligence strategy, covering 2026 to 2030 around six priorities: data and AI governance, cybersecurity, training, research, innovation and inclusion. A UNESCO-supported readiness assessment presented alongside it classes the country as emerging, with an ICT development index of 61.6 against AI readiness of about 24.5 out of 100 and no legislation dedicated to artificial intelligence beyond the data-protection provisions of the digital code.

2026-09-04-wearetech-nigeria-decide-ia-t.summary: The Nigerian firm Decide has built its own artificial-intelligence model for spreadsheet management, correcting formulas and cleaning data, after finding external technologies more expensive to run.

2026-09-04-wearetech-techstars-iraki-unc.summary: Uncovr, co-founded in Morocco in 2025 by Ines Iraki, turns operating-theatre video into medical reports, addressing both the traceability of surgical procedures and the administrative load on clinicians.

2026-09-04-wearetech-techstars-makdour-n.summary: Notiverse, founded in Algeria in 2023 by Salah Eddine Makdour, offers a mobile note-taking and personal data application built to run without sending data off the device.

2026-09-04-zaf-digital-profiteers-sassa-.summary: Open Secrets published the final part of an investigation into South Africa's digitalised grants system, arguing anti-fraud effort falls on beneficiaries rather than on the private actors deducting from their grants. SASSA flagged more than 420,000 beneficiaries for review in 2025/26 claiming R1 billion saved and targets up to 350,000 in 2026/27 for R1.5 billion; the piece documents a pensioner losing R205 a month to a funeral policy he never consented to.

2026-09-04-zaf-home-affairs-visa-fraud-s.summary: South Africa's Special Investigating Unit found Home Affairs adjudicators took kickbacks to approve visas on fraudulent supporting documents without conducting any verification. It has flagged 205 visas for revocation and deportation with seven disciplinary referrals, under a 2024 proclamation covering almost two decades of visa administration, and recommends reducing human intervention through technology and integrating departmental systems so verifications run automatically.

2026-09-04-zaf-swims-portal-data-integra.summary: The Western Cape's Social Work Integrated Management System now accepts secure external reports of child abuse and neglect, identified or anonymous, from the professionals the Children's Act obliges to report - health professionals, legal practitioners, teachers, traditional leaders and religious leaders - routing them into the provincial case-management system rather than a separate channel.

2026-09-04-zmb-mobile-money-liquidity-cr.summary: MTN mobile money executives told the group's fintech summit in Johannesburg that high adoption numbers mask weak use of savings and investment products. The Ghanaian chief executive said the platform processes more than 26 million transactions a day but that fewer than 0.3% of users actively invest; the Zambian chief executive said agent numbers were not on their own solving access and that the company had deployed artificial intelligence to monitor agent activity and liquidity to find where customers cannot get cash.

2026-09-05-alwasat-tripoli-financial-lit.summary: Tripoli hosts the fifth Arab conference on saving and financial literacy from 7 to 9 September, with Arab and international financial institutions attending to discuss the sector's shift as digital services widen and artificial intelligence and cryptocurrencies grow.

2026-09-05-citizen-north-coast-ngos-devi.summary: South Africa's communications minister handed smart devices to two KwaZulu-Natal non-profits working with vulnerable children, one of them a cluster foster centre running three homes for twelve children whose house mothers had been using their own phones and data. It is a donation to two organisations rather than a programme with a stated budget or reach.

2026-09-05-civ-numerique-59-services-qui.summary: A national prioritisation workshop closed having examined 140 of 620 inventoried public services through nine working groups, retaining 59 for immediate priority and expecting ten quick wins by the end of 2026 - among them diploma authentication, digital proof of life for pensioners and the computerised patient record. The list itself is not published.

2026-09-05-cnbc-reuters-us-china-ai-safe.summary: The United States and China are reported to be preparing mid-September talks devoted to artificial-intelligence safety, the first bilateral discussions of their kind under the current US administration, with cooperation on monitoring AI-directed cyberattacks among the topics. A White House official said no such meeting is planned; the report rests on anonymous sources.

2026-09-05-ena-ethiopia-ai-capabilities-.summary: IGAD's deputy executive secretary said Ethiopia's work on human capital, digital infrastructure and applied artificial intelligence positions it to compete globally, speaking during a member-state visit to the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute. The regional body wants a partnership letting other member states draw on that experience; the assessment is IGAD's, with no measure behind it.

2026-09-05-koaci-cote-divoire-ouattara-d.summary: The same workshop's other conclusion was that the state lacks a common direction: the digital transition minister put a governance framework ahead of the service list as the first priority, against ministries each building their own tools, platforms and systems. No such framework is on the record.

2026-09-05-lapresse-tunisia-cybersecurit.summary: An analysis of the head of government's circular of 2 September sets out what it requires of the administration: encrypted connections, mandatory renewal of security certificates, two-factor verification for administrator access, protection against traffic-saturation attacks and hosting on state-approved servers, with messaging apps and social media banned for official documents and shared credentials ended. It binds the administration rather than the wider economy, and carries no compliance deadline.

2026-09-05-madagascar-cybercrime-bill-vo.summary: The National Assembly deferred five bills to a later session rather than vote them, the recast cybercrime law and the electronic communications and digital infrastructure bill first among them; deputies said they needed longer on texts turning on both security imperatives and fundamental freedoms. No resumed date is set.

2026-09-05-newsmada-madagascar-cybersurv.summary: Commentary on the deferral reads the contested articles as written to suit the state's own control interests rather than to fight cybercrime, singling out the surveillance powers the bill would create. The Assembly's president said he did not care to imagine what would have followed had the two lead texts not been deferred.

2026-09-05-nimasa-digitisation-ship-regi.summary: Nigeria's maritime administration said it is moving towards full automation of the national ship registry so operators can register and transact remotely, including payment, without attending its offices, framing it as part of reforms to remove human contact and block revenue leakages. No date, cost or vendor is stated.

2026-09-05-tanzania-drc-tanganyika-fibre.summary: Tanzania and the DRC agreed to fast-track a fibre-optic cable from Kigoma to Kalemie across Lake Tanganyika, alongside a standard gauge railway link through Burundi and the establishment of a joint economic commission. The commitment was reaffirmed at a farewell meeting for the Congolese ambassador; no route survey, cost, financing or delivery date is published.

2026-09-05-tvcnews-nigeria-nitda-digital.summary: Nigeria's technology development agency called for a risk-based approach to digital sovereignty, arguing the concept should rest on the classification and risk profile of data rather than on where data is stored or who controls it. The position was set out on a panel at a hyperscaler conference in Lagos.

2026-09-06-arp-tunisia-proposition-loi-2.summary: Parliament's own case file for the bill amending Tunisia's 2022 cyber-offences decree-law puts dates on a revision that has been called a priority: deposited on 20 February 2024, referred to committee on 10 April 2025, carrying 38 sponsors, and still unvoted. The amendments themselves are not published on the page, so what the bill would change remains unstated.

2026-09-06-bcm-strategie-nationale-paiem.summary: Mauritania's central bank publishes its National Digital Payment Strategy on its fintech portal, presented as a natural extension of the national financial inclusion strategy and aimed at widening access to financial services for rural and under-banked citizens. It sets five objectives: easing the regulation of payment and electronic-money institutions to attract fintech investment, rebuilding the digital payments infrastructure, modernising financial services around innovation, building adoption and use, and putting a governance system in place across the whole financial-digital sector. No implementation report or measured outturn against any of them appears on the page.

2026-09-06-togo-atd-guide-architecture-e.summary: Togo's government enterprise-architecture guide, and with it the common interoperability framework it defines, is still a draft on the digital agency's own live status page: version 1.0, status Brouillon, with the version date, reviewer and review date fields blank and the revision table carrying only its column headers. The framework exists as a published normative text and has not been given force of law.

2026-09-07-afrinic-ipv6-for-ipv4-control.summary: A draft AFRINIC policy would tie any new IPv4 request to IPv6 eligibility, a deployment plan and percentage targets over 12, 24 and 48 months. The registry's own impact assessment says the evidence standard and the top-25 measurement method are not defined and warns smaller operators may face a disproportionate burden; AFRINIC 37 reached no consensus and the proposal returned to the mailing list.

2026-09-07-alchourouk-ai-in-vocational-t.summary: Tunisia’s employment minister said artificial intelligence is being added to vocational training, with twelve laboratories to be created in training centres from the new training year.

2026-09-07-aps-algeria-second-meeting-un.summary: Algeria's digitalisation high commission and the domestic trade ministry held a second joint meeting on a unified digital mechanism for regulating the national market, taking the data sources themselves as the subject — how they are produced, updated and kept consistent.

2026-09-07-aps-parlementaire-senegalais-.summary: A Senegalese parliamentary committee chair called in Dakar for African data-protection authorities to be given stronger means of action.

2026-09-07-aslm-ebola-laboratory-systems.summary: A multi-country laboratory assessment completed before the current Ebola outbreak covered 26 countries, finding every one with a functioning surveillance system and core diagnostic capacity and 3,964 laboratories mapped across fourteen. It named digital interoperability between laboratories and surveillance platforms, alongside specimen referral, workforce surge and domestic financing, as the weak points — the seams the response has since had to improvise at.

2026-09-07-bfa-ecofin-video-verbalisatio.summary: Burkina Faso's video-verbalisation cameras recorded 19,910 road offences over August 2026, generating CFA146.559m in fines of which CFA16.1m had been recovered at the 4 September review. A motorised police brigade was created on 2 September specifically to trace drivers who evade the camera-issued fines.

2026-09-07-businessexplainer-oosthuysen-.summary: An industry argument that South Africa is not positioning itself as future-ready cites employer survey findings that about 55% of workers show little or no proficiency in mathematics or data skills, 52% of businesses find it difficult to hire anyone prepared for digital transformation and 70% rate workforce technology skills poor or very poor, against 118,500 unfilled ICT vacancies of which 36% are junior roles.

2026-09-07-capacity-telecom-egypt-red-se.summary: Telecom Egypt named the contractor for a 200km subsea cable between Sharm El Sheikh and Taba, extending its Red Sea festoon into a continuous Suez-to-Taba route designed for about 5 petabits per second.

2026-09-07-civ-aip-fenacci-observatoire-.summary: Four days after nationwide checks on electronic standardised invoicing began, Côte d'Ivoire's traders' federation created a National Observatory on Electronic Standardised Invoicing, announced at a press conference in Adjamé. The observatory has no published mandate, membership or reporting arrangement, and the federation's earlier demand that the checks be suspended is not withdrawn on the record.

2026-09-07-cmr-businessincameroon-cybast.summary: A United States firm plans US$75m, about FCFA 42.25bn, for a Douala data centre designed in part for artificial-intelligence workloads with dedicated power generation. The planning ministry describes it as an intention presented at the first bilateral economic forum rather than a commitment; the same vendor's Ivorian project was underwritten by a US$66.14m export-credit guarantee.

2026-09-07-digital-realty-nairobi-nbo2-d.summary: A second facility on the operator's Nairobi campus adds 6.4MW of capacity, opened alongside the retirement of the iColo brand in Kenya and Mozambique in favour of the parent's. The figure is critical IT load rather than delivered live load, and no occupancy or campus total is published.

2026-09-07-drc-qr-code-product-traceabil.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's standards control office plans a national QR-code system letting consumers scan a product — medicines included — to verify its certification status, with consumer checks stated as opening within weeks and resting on 88 laboratories across 29 sites. No launch date, register or enforcement route is published.

2026-09-07-eswatini-auditors-ai-inter-sa.summary: Eswatini's audit office hosted a week-long peer programme at which supreme audit institutions across the region weighed the use of artificial intelligence in government audit. No tool, pilot, audit methodology or procurement is named.

2026-09-07-eta-egypt-homepage.summary: The Egyptian Tax Authority's own portal carries the state of its digital systems: electronic invoicing with registration guidance and online training for businesses joining it, an e-receipt system defined as an electronic document proving business-to-consumer transactions, and value-added tax return automation. A consumer-incentive scheme rewarding shoppers for taking a receipt or invoice is in trial operation at five shopping malls.

2026-09-07-ethiopia-fayda-proof-of-ident.summary: The national identity programme's own page lists the 33 documents accepted as proof of identity for registration, from the local administration card and passport to birth, education, marriage and business records. The page carries no publication date of its own.

2026-09-07-falana-serap-n33-75bn-cash-tr.summary: The Auditor-General's 2024 report states that the government could not provide auditors with sufficient evidence that ₦33.75bn of cash transfers intended for more than 3.29 million vulnerable households reached genuine beneficiaries, the payment platform's statements not having been supplied. A rights lawyer has asked the financial crimes commission to investigate and a civil-society organisation puts over ₦78.8bn across social protection programmes as diverted, unaccounted for or irregularly spent.

2026-09-07-gabonactu-digitalisation-titr.summary: A Gabonese commentary places the digitalisation of transport titles and documents among the state's modernisation projects, and puts the open question as who governs it and whether local suppliers are used. No contracting authority, supplier, scope, cost or timetable for the project is on the record.

2026-09-07-gauteng-egovernment-annual-re.summary: The Gauteng provincial department's 2025/26 annual report records 96 public Wi-Fi hotspots offering up to 500MB of free internet a day, 33 e-services live, 99% provincial network uptime and 7,271 cameras on the provincial safety network. The figures are the department's own, with no audited outturn or prior-year comparison in the account.

2026-09-07-gdn-dpi-inclusivity-survey-de.summary: The Global Development Network has begun fieldwork on a five-country DPI Inclusivity Survey covering Sierra Leone and Ghana alongside Chile, Bangladesh and Indonesia, with partner teams at the Institute for Development and the University of Ghana. Running to April and engaging more than 5,000 households, it asks whether digital identity and digital payment systems leave people feeling more economically, socially and politically included, rather than measuring registration and access.

2026-09-07-gha-myjoyonline-5g-deployment.summary: Ghana expects to complete 5G spectrum assignment and begin deployment by December 2026, its communications minister said.

2026-09-07-gha-myjoyonline-digitisation-.summary: Ghana signed a contract to digitise 3.5 million public records held by the archives department, presented as records-management modernisation and better access to official information.

2026-09-07-gha-myjoyonline-mobile-data-p.summary: Ghana’s communications minister said households and businesses are getting more data for less money after government engagements with the mobile operators.

2026-09-07-gha-myjoyonline-mous-11-unive.summary: Ghana signed memoranda with eleven universities to embed digital certifications into degree and diploma programmes.

2026-09-07-gha-myjoyonline-one-million-c.summary: Ghana’s coders programme held 141,954 registered accounts and 27,782 actively engaged learners at the start of August.

2026-09-07-gha-myjoyonline-sam-george-ch.summary: Ghana’s communications minister was unanimously confirmed as the next chair of the African Union technical committee on communication and ICT, for two years.

2026-09-07-gha-myjoyonline-sovereign-vir.summary: Ghana is building a government-owned virtual meeting platform for secure high-level operations, the deputy chief of staff said.

2026-09-07-ghana-biometric-sim-verificat.summary: Ghana's communications minister said Parliament has passed the legislative instrument governing SIM registration and the biometric verification phase will be introduced before the end of 2026. The same account puts completion of the 2021–2023 exercise it replaces at 44.28% of subscribers.

2026-09-07-ghana-marrify-digital-marriag.summary: A privately operated platform launched in Accra on 28 August lets users search and verify registered marriage and divorce records drawn from the registrar-general's department, the courts, district assemblies and the Gazette. No data-sharing agreement, fee schedule, coverage figure or record count is published.

2026-09-07-ghana-nca-public-education-te.summary: Ghana's communications regulator took radio-frequency exposure messaging to traders, transport operators and commuters at Koforidua Central Market, after opposition to a mast at a lorry station. It is the consent side of a build the same week's ministerial account puts at about 6,000 sites short.

2026-09-07-ghana-sam-george-government-a.summary: Ghana's communications ministry gave a full public account of its January–August delivery, and the arithmetic is the interesting part: 141,954 registered accounts against 5,812 logged completions on the national coders programme, 8,578 fibre cuts projected for 2026 at roughly US$2,045 a repair, and a dig-once policy still awaiting Cabinet. It also records voice over LTE rising from about 7% of traffic to 22.43% and smartphone penetration at 71.8% in June 2026.

2026-09-07-ghana-seevcash-visa-card.summary: A Ghanaian remittance startup moving money from the United States to Ghana raised US$333,000 from a blockchain foundation's community fund, to launch an international payment card usable online and in stores. The commitment date is not stated in the account.

2026-09-07-gitex-mint-africa-lagos-finan.summary: A financial-innovation platform was unveiled in Lagos with backing from governments and financial-sector regulators, its full debut deferred to the 2027 edition of the technology week. No participants, funding or programme of work is published with the announcement.

2026-09-07-gmb-standard-gamcel-9-digit-m.summary: Three Gambian operators moved to nine-digit mobile numbers at midnight, with the fourth to follow in a second phase on a reserved prefix, the regulator confirmed.

2026-09-07-gnb-ang-bissau-municipal-digi.summary: Bissau city council announced the launch of a modernisation and digital transformation programme for the institution, on a plan approved at its first strategic retreat.

2026-09-07-graphic-ghana-customs-valuati.summary: An industry commentary traces Ghanaian customs valuation from manual assessment through pre-shipment inspection to an artificial-intelligence-assisted future.

2026-09-07-graphic-ghana-hunger-project-.summary: A development organisation opened an ICT centre at a rural development centre in Ghana’s Eastern Region.

2026-09-07-independentnews-eswatini-ers-.summary: Eswatini’s national business body backed the revenue service’s move to electronic invoicing while asking that it be made affordable and workable across existing technologies before national rollout.

2026-09-07-ippmedia-vodacom-bridge-for-b.summary: The leading Tanzanian mobile operator entered a three-year partnership with a global entrepreneurship network to reach 1,000 entrepreneurs and 40 ventures, with a first cohort of entrepreneur-support organisations due in October 2026. No commitment amount is stated, so the agreement carries targets and no measurable resource behind them.

2026-09-07-kenya-ict-authority-kdeap-cyb.summary: Kenya's technology authority put the National Information Security Framework's audit, risk-management and certification mechanisms to a Nairobi stakeholder workshop, to establish whether they are practical for national implementation ahead of certifying critical information infrastructure. The framework text and the certification criteria are not published.

2026-09-07-lanation-benin-indabax-langue.summary: The Beninese edition of a continental machine-learning meeting opens a track on large language models and low-resource African language corpora, at Cotonou from 10 to 12 September.

2026-09-07-lby-zero-cash-initiative-halt.summary: Libya’s banking sector development forum said it has stopped pursuing its cashless initiative in the form submitted to the central bank, because the executive framework it needed was never issued.

2026-09-07-liberia-ul-ebu-tripartite-mou.summary: A tripartite memorandum signed on 27 August has a foreign online university covering 97% of online tuition for more than 200 students of the national university, with three smart classrooms due in 2027. No commitment amount is stated.

2026-09-07-libya-cbl-governor-financial-.summary: Libya's central bank governor launched a link to the Arab regional payments platform, a study track on a central bank digital currency and stablecoins, and a cyber-skills programme, and put a pilot for accession to China's cross-border interbank system at early 2027. None of the four carries an instrument, budget, participant list or delivery date.

2026-09-07-linfodrome-cepici-e-licences.summary: Côte d’Ivoire’s investment promotion centre is taking investor licences, permits and authorisations onto an online platform, with ministry focal points trained to keep it current.

2026-09-07-mtn-ghana-commits-1-1bn-netwo.summary: The dominant Ghanaian operator's US$1.1bn three-year commitment is restated against the site build behind it: 800 new cell sites of which 180 are already active, and a second operator targeting 2,698 sites in 2026. The communications minister dates the regulator board's removal of wholesale 5G exclusivity to 15 July 2026.

2026-09-07-myjoyonline-accra-africa-inte.summary: Ghana is to host the fifteenth Africa Internet Governance Forum in Accra in November.

2026-09-07-myjoyonline-ghana-cert-gh-336.summary: Ghana’s national incident response team handled 3,363 cybersecurity incidents in the first half of 2026.

2026-09-07-myjoyonline-ghana-dpc-regulat.summary: Ghana’s data protection commission increased its regulatory activity by 51.5 per cent in the first half of 2026, alongside a rise in data-controller registrations.

2026-09-07-myjoyonline-ghana-ministry-st.summary: Ghana’s communications minister directed his ministry’s senior staff and those of its agencies to enrol on the national coders programme by the end of the week.

2026-09-07-nassit-mobile-app-pensioners-.summary: Sierra Leone's social security trust is to launch a self-service application for pensioners and contributors, with a short-code fallback for feature phones, biometric verification and integration with the three mobile-money services. It is announced rather than launched, with no date published.

2026-09-07-newvision-ucc-explains-intern.summary: Uganda’s communications regulator published the text of its suspension directive: public internet, new SIM sales and outbound data roaming stopped, mobile VPNs disabled, a whitelisted exclusion list from referral hospitals to railway signalling, and restoration only on written notice.

2026-09-07-nigeria-nin-62-5-million-gap-.summary: Nigeria had issued national identification numbers to 117.5 million people out of 134.6 million enrolments at 30 June 2026, against a target of 180 million by December. Closing the gap would need monthly enrolment to rise from 1.5–1.8 million to about 7.4 million.

2026-09-07-nigeria-police-vigilant-app-f.summary: The police fraud-reporting app launched on 1 September is the fourth police reporting platform in a decade, and it arrives over a cybercrime centre already logging about 146,000 reports and about ₦58bn in recovered assets. Nothing published says how the new channel routes against the centre already running, or what became of the earlier platforms.

2026-09-07-nilepost-mpigi-national-id-de.summary: Residents of a Ugandan district report waiting more than a year for identity cards, making repeated trips to registration centres and losing access to services tied to the number.

2026-09-07-nilepost-nira-national-id-exp.summary: Uganda’s identity authority is to hold a national ID expo, with millions still outside the register and the number framed as the gateway to services.

2026-09-07-nilepost-ura-nin-replace-tin.summary: Uganda's revenue authority says the move from taxpayer numbers to national identification numbers will not automatically make every citizen a taxpayer, the purpose being a single more secure identifier for government services and more accurate taxpayer records. It follows the finance minister's statement four days earlier that the two numbers must be interoperable rather than one replacing the other.

2026-09-07-novojornal-paga3-standard-ban.summary: The founders of an Angolan payments startup accuse a commercial bank of using information shared in a pilot to build a similar product; the case has run about a year and the bank calls the claim abusive.

2026-09-07-openserve-third-fibre-route-s.summary: The state-affiliated wholesale operator completed a third long-haul fibre route from Cape Town to Pretoria via Springbok and Mahikeng, built so the network stays up through major breaks. It sits inside a wholesale network of about 180,000km carrying just under R3bn of capital expenditure a year.

2026-09-07-papss-ai-fraud-detection-cryp.summary: The continental payment system's chief executive put transaction volume growth above 1,000% and value growth at 125% since 2022, with settlement averaging seven seconds against an original 120-second design target and an artificial-intelligence layer screening for suspicious activity before value is released. He declined to give the absolute volume and value, saying disclosure is still being agreed and a report will follow in early 2027.

2026-09-07-papss-canex-creative-economy-.summary: The continental payment system is being extended towards creative-economy payments, with third-party rails for royalties and licensing described and a Lagos creative-industries event in November set as the pilot occasion. No design, timetable or participant list is published.

2026-09-07-sa-internet-costs-competition.summary: Wired internet prices rose 3.5% and wireless 4.1% over the first half of 2026, both ahead of cumulative headline inflation of 3.8%, on the competition authority's cost-of-living report. Over the six years to July 2026 the two rose 18.6% and 6.4% against headline inflation of 36%, so the recent move reverses the longer pattern for a service the authority treats as essential.

2026-09-07-saps-ai-generated-police-imag.summary: Provincial police in the Free State have warned that creating and sharing artificial-intelligence face-swap images of oneself in police uniform can breach section 68 of the South African Police Service Act 68 of 1995, which makes impersonating a police official an offence. It is an existing statute asserted against a new practice, not a new rule.
