The call, implemented by Expertise France and financed by the French foreign ministry, closes on 14 September 2026; the page carries no date of its own.

2026-09-12-gha-graphic-nca-700mhz-spectr.summary: Ghana's National Communications Authority awarded two 700 MHz lots to MTN Ghana, the only qualified bidder, after opening best price offers on 11 September 2026. This account gives the fee as US$109.9 million; the regulator's release puts it at US$100.9 million.

2026-09-12-gin-mediaguinee-revue-mi-parc.summary: Guinea's Ministry of Modernisation of the Administration and the Public Service began a four-day mid-term review of its operational action plan at Forécariah on 12 September 2026, chaired by minister Faya François Bourouno. The review is to assess delivery, identify obstacles and set priorities for the rest of 2026.

2026-09-12-hiiraan-somalia-first-satelli.summary: Türkiye's ambassador to Somalia, Alper Aktaş, said in Mogadishu on 10 September 2026 that Somalia is expected to launch its first satellite in 2027, with a satellite operations and space research facility planned in Warsheekh district, Middle Shabelle. No Somali government agreement, budget or instrument is cited.

2026-09-12-iafrica-vodafone-egypt-cassav.summary: Vodafone Egypt and Cassava Technologies launched what they call Egypt's first AI factory, selling GPU capacity on NVIDIA hardware to government and business with data kept in the country. The piece places it within Vodafone Egypt's plan to invest more than EGP 20 billion this fiscal year and the minister's stated policy of courting several infrastructure partners at once.

2026-09-12-newswatch-nigeria-national-so.summary: Nigeria's IT development agency NITDA is driving a National Sovereign Cloud Initiative to keep sensitive data and essential digital services under Nigerian law and reduce reliance on infrastructure hosted abroad. The programme builds on the 2019 Cloud First Policy; no budget or timetable is given.

2026-09-12-nga-thisday-cac-ai-corporate-.summary: Nigeria's Corporate Affairs Commission is working with Google and other partners to bring AI into company registration, including service in English, Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo and Pidgin, registrar-general Hussaini Ishaq Magaji said at the commission's retreat in Bauchi. No launch date is given.

2026-09-12-nga-thisday-drli-independent-.summary: The Digital Rights Lawyers Initiative called for an independent audit of Nigeria's electoral technology and protection of voters' biometric data before the 2027 elections, at a PrivCon 2026 panel in Lagos on 1 September. It warned that weak oversight of the electoral commission's systems could damage public trust.

2026-09-12-primenews-ghana-nca-mtn-700mh.summary: Ghana's National Communications Authority assigned two 700 MHz lots, the most one applicant may win, to MTN Ghana for a licence fee of US$100.9 million. MTN was the only qualified bidder, which closes the 700 MHz stage of the 5G spectrum process; the 2.3 GHz and 3 GHz bands remain open.

2026-09-12-projectm-malawi-nzika-digital.summary: Malawi's National Registration Bureau is to launch the Nzika Digital ID Wallet at the Bingu International Convention Centre in Lilongwe, letting citizens carry a verified digital copy of their national ID on a phone. The homeland security minister will preside; no launch date is given.

2026-09-12-rfi-koafec-seoul-afdb-korea-a.summary: The Korea-Africa economic cooperation summit, KOAFEC, closed in Seoul on 11 September 2026 with agreements between the African Development Bank and South Korea towards an AI hub for Africa. One is a memorandum on co-financing and preparing government projects; no sums are reported.

2026-09-12-sanews-nzimande-global-south-.summary: South Africa's science and innovation minister Blade Nzimande told the Pujiang Innovation Forum in Shanghai on 12 September 2026 that the Global South must produce and own emerging technologies such as AI and quantum, not only consume them. He warned that science and technology are being used as weapons by some states.

2026-09-12-sen-seneweb-hackathon-cif-dig.summary: Team Mule Hunters won the first Senegalese edition of the CIF-DigiCoop-WA+ hackathon run by the West African financial institutions' confederation, taking 1.5 million FCFA for an anti-money-laundering compliance tool. Ten finalist teams, chosen from 65, spent 72 hours on compliance and automated microcredit scoring.

2026-09-12-sen-seneweb-nelvia-plateforme.summary: A school management platform called NELVIA was launched in Thiès on 12 September 2026 for Senegal's public and private schools, bringing pupil records, timetables, marks, finances and parent communication into one system. It issues QR-verifiable documents and a unique pupil identifier, the NELVIA ID.

2026-09-12-shuttlers-lagos-ride-share-te.summary: Lagos bus-sharing company Shuttlers is bringing back doorstep pickup through a service called Shuttlers Pod from 25 September, its chief executive told TechCabal. The firm says it runs more than 430 buses a day and has carried more than 10 million journeys.

2026-09-12-the-hindu-brics-new-delhi-dec.summary: BRICS leaders adopted the New Delhi Declaration at their 18th summit on 12 September 2026, calling for wider access to AI resources and international cooperation on safe and inclusive AI. The Hindu reports its technology agenda spans AI, cybersecurity, digital public infrastructure, telecoms and submarine networks.

2026-09-12-us-h1b-visa-fee-african-tech-.summary: A TechCabal analysis argues that a proposed US$103,265 H-1B fee and a wage-weighted visa lottery, put forward by the US Department of Homeland Security, will make distributed teams in Lagos, Nairobi and Cape Town cheaper for American firms than hiring through the visa route. It is an opinion piece on a proposal, not a rule in force.

2026-09-12-von-ncc-8526-telecom-sites-ca.summary: Nigeria's mobile operators have built 8,526 of 12,179 committed coverage and capacity sites, about 70%, up from around 5,000 at the previous meeting, the Nigerian Communications Commission board said after its 110th meeting. The board also said its Device Management System is live, allowing stolen devices to be blocked across networks, and restated zero tolerance for call masking.

2026-09-12-zaf-sundaytimes-sumsub-deepfa.summary: Identity fraud in South Africa fell 31% year on year while deepfake incidents rose 269%, according to figures from verification firm Sumsub. Its chief executive credits tighter regulation and SIM-ID linkage for the fall and says the remaining attacks are fewer but more sophisticated.

2026-09-12-zmb-diggers-mansa-tailor-arre.summary: Police in Mansa arrested a 38-year-old man over a TikTok video allegedly insulting President Hakainde Hichilema, charging him under Zambia's Cyber Crimes Act with harassment using electronic gadgets. The police statement is dated 11 September 2026, after the Secretary to the Cabinet warned that insulting the President would be prosecuted.

2026-09-12-zmb-diggers-zamstats-15000-ta.summary: The Zambia Statistics Agency handed 15,000 tablets from the 2022 census to government ministries on 11 September 2026. Statistician General Sheila Mudenda said they will go to selected institutions in the national statistical system, which increasingly need to collect and exchange data electronically.

2026-09-13-africell-investors-page-four-.summary: The operator's investor page lists four markets — The Gambia, Sierra Leone, Angola and the Democratic Republic of Congo — with more than 14 million subscribers, more than 2,500 towers and revenue above US$400m. Its US$360m of 10.5% senior secured notes mature in October 2029.

2026-09-13-eth-capital-ai-legal-framewor.summary: Capital Ethiopia reports expert warnings that AI systems trained on works without permission undermine copyright, patent and trademark protection, and that Ethiopia's data infrastructure leaves structural gaps. A York University law professor told the paper that copyright and patent laws are being dismantled by artificial intelligence.

2026-09-13-gab-agp-ged-electronic-docume.summary: Gabon's digital economy ministry announced the launch on 16 September 2026 of an electronic document management project for the administration, to modernise document handling and improve traceability. It falls under Ordonnance 0006/PR/2025 on digitalisation; no scope, supplier or cost is stated.

2026-09-13-ken-kachwanya-technopolis-dev.summary: Kenya's Technopolis Development Authority Board was fully constituted with three appointments, as the authority takes up a national mandate under the Technopolis Act 2026, commenced on 29 May 2026. The board moves the authority from developing Konza towards planning technopolises nationwide; no new locations, budgets or timelines were announced.

2026-09-13-lbr-moe-apo-standardize-schoo.summary: Liberia's Ministry of Education opened a five-day session in Kakata to develop and validate a Statutory School Record-Keeping Booklet, one nationwide system for school records on students, teachers, attendance and infrastructure. County teams are then to finalise education operational plans from the 2024/25 school census fact sheets.

2026-09-13-lso-finmark-gis-financial-acc.summary: FinMark Trust issued terms of reference for Phase 2 of Lesotho's GIS Financial Access Points Mapping Project, to update a 2018 baseline of 5,597 geo-referenced access points. The work covers every mobile-money agent, bank branch, ATM and post office across ten districts, with spatial analytics and a web map.

2026-09-13-mar-consonews-generation-aiot.summary: Morocco's Génération AIoT programme opened seven cohorts in Casablanca, Fès and Oujda, aiming at 1,200 trained people a year from February 2027. Launched in February 2026 by the digital transition ministry with a foundation and ABA Technology, it had drawn 2,118 applications and gathered 95 participants.

2026-09-13-nam-namibian-universal-servic.summary: An opinion piece argues that cancelling and recycling inactive mobile numbers cuts people with irregular incomes off from employers, banks and government services, since a phone number now works as part of a person's digital identity. It calls for universal-service rules that weigh those consequences against efficient number management.

2026-09-13-nga-business-times-tinubu-bri.summary: At the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Vice President Kashim Shettima, representing President Bola Tinubu, sought BRICS investment in Nigeria's artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, telecommunications and critical minerals. He cited Project BRIDGE's broadband and fibre expansion; no agreement or amount was announced.

2026-09-13-sdn-aswatnews-e-learning-regu.summary: The president of Sudan's National Council for Higher Education and Scientific Research approved the E-learning and Blended Learning Regulation 2026 by decision 138, signed and in force from 12 September 2026. An academic's commentary says it gives e-learning in higher-education institutions a formal legal basis rather than treating it as a wartime stopgap.

2026-09-13-sen-rts-cyberattaques-jamais-.summary: Colonel Aly Mime, Senegal's national cybersecurity chief at the DCSSI, said on RTS that the state has never paid a ransom after a cyberattack. He named the attacks on the DAF, the Treasury and the tax directorate and called attackers' claims about stolen data volumes largely bluff.

2026-09-13-techreviewafrica-world-bank-m.summary: A World Bank implementation-support mission reviewed the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project–GovNet with NITA-U and the ICT ministry. It visited the National Data Center, the national CERT, the Personal Data Protection Office and a skilling centre in Nakawa; the mission dates are not given.

2026-09-13-techtrends-edtech-out-of-scho.summary: A commentary argues that Nigeria's EdTech products were built to supplement schooling for enrolled students and do little for out-of-school children, whose exclusion is driven by poverty, insecurity and distance. It points to offline tools such as uLesson's preloaded devices and calls for donor and government partnership rather than venture funding.

2026-09-13-uga-independent-kitgum-reside.summary: Residents of Lagoro sub-county in Kitgum District agreed to pay shs 500 each to transport NIRA officials delivering national ID cards locally, against shs 30,000–40,000 per trip to the municipal office. The district's chief administrative officer said it would seek approval for local structures to distribute IDs.

2026-09-13-xgl-fmprc-xi-brics-summit-sta.summary: President Xi Jinping proposed five initiatives at the 18th BRICS Summit, among them a BRICS AI open-source community and a BRICS digital ecosystem cloud platform, and called for a consensus-based global AI governance framework. He restated China's zero-tariff treatment for the 53 African countries it has diplomatic relations with; no timeline or funding was attached.

2026-09-13-zaf-presidency-ramaphosa-bric.summary: President Cyril Ramaphosa proposed at the 18th BRICS Summit that BRICS set up an international mechanism for the independent scientific evaluation of artificial intelligence, resting on human-control principles and mandatory reporting of serious incidents. He also backed formal external checks and audits of AI companies; no draft terms or BRICS response are on record.

2026-09-14-actuniger-presse-en-ligne-pro.summary: Fourteen Nigerien online editors welcomed the government's electronic-press text in a declaration dated 13 September and asked to be consulted on its implementing rules. They offered to work with the communication regulator and announced a representative body of their own.

2026-09-14-ago-angop-huambo-igca-janela-.summary: Angola's cadastral institute trained Huambo province's 17 municipalities on the land-concession single window created by Presidential Decree 84/25. Provincial officials said it will align municipalities with the government, raise revenue and tighten control of the cadastre.

2026-09-14-almasryalyoum-egypt-moj-defen.summary: The justice ministry added that SMS notification packages are paid to the contracted provider at the regulator's tariff rather than to the ministry. A full case file as a PDF is priced at the paper-copy rate of EGP 150 per 50 pages.

2026-09-14-babacar-mbengue-dechets-elect.summary: A profile of Senegalese engineer Babacar Mbengue, whose company RKovera, founded in January 2026, runs a traceability platform for e-waste collection, certified data erasure and recovery of metals.

2026-09-14-bamboo-cowrywise-dangote-ipo-.summary: Bamboo and Cowrywise apps failed on the opening day of the Dangote refinery IPO sold through approved fintechs. Cowrywise restored service in about an hour; Bamboo said it had opened more than 236,000 accounts the week before and that allocation is pro rata.

2026-09-14-bfa-lefaso-cn-mabg-transforma.summary: A second account of the same council session reports the permanent secretary's figures: hundreds of procedures dematerialised, more than 10,000 recruitments and over 200 organisation charts revised. The session set orientations for 2027.

2026-09-14-bfa-sidwaya-cn-mabg-modernisa.summary: Burkina Faso's National Council for the Modernisation of the Administration and Good Governance met under Prime Minister Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel OuÃ©draogo and rated the administration's 2025 performance at 85.38%. The Prime Minister named weak citizen uptake of digital service platforms among persistent shortcomings and called for national languages in public information systems.

2026-09-14-bosun-tijani-withdraws-itu-de.summary: Nigeria's communications minister Bosun Tijani withdrew his candidacy for ITU Deputy Secretary-General to stay on the domestic programme. He cited Project BRIDGE's 90,000 km of planned fibre, the tower programme, two planned satellites and a national postcode system.

2026-09-14-burkina-faso-administration-s.summary: Burkina Faso's digital transition ministry set the official launch of electronic signature in administrative procedures for 15 September in Ouagadougou, under the 2009 electronic-transactions law. More than 250 procedures were dematerialised in 2025, 95 of them on the Service Public BF portal.

2026-09-14-busha-mastercard-crypto-crede.summary: Nigerian crypto platform Busha made Mastercard Crypto Credential available, letting users send supported digital assets to verified email or phone aliases instead of wallet addresses.

2026-09-14-cell-c-easyequities-bidvest-t.summary: Cell C, EasyEquities and Bidvest Bank notified South African customers of a breach at an unnamed third-party provider, reported on 9 September. Cell C Fiber customers' names, emails, numbers and account numbers were exposed; Bidvest Bank's exposure awaits a forensic investigation.

2026-09-14-cod-digitalbusiness-rdc-pass-.summary: DR Congo's digital economy ministry said more than 9,000 candidates sat the recruitment test for RDC Pass agents and a first cohort of 50 was retained for the Kinshasa pilot. Training starts on 15 September, followed by extension to other Kinshasa zones and then nationwide.

2026-09-14-cod-ouragan-enquete-arptc-reg.summary: A joint press investigation calls DR Congo's telecoms regulator ARPTC unlawful and ineffective, noting that the successor authority created by a 2023 decree has never been installed. It details failings on service quality and equipment approval.

2026-09-14-djezzy-ugcaa-digital-transfor.summary: Djezzy signed a framework agreement with Algeria's traders' and artisans' union UGCAA to support their digital transformation. No date, terms or figures were published.

2026-09-14-dni-r2-1bn-digital-economy-in.summary: South African investment firm DNI announced more than R2.1 billion across Frogfoot, Vox and Hypa, Mission Mobile and KnowRoaming. Its consortium holds 34.8% of Frogfoot and Vox at an aggregate R14.4 billion valuation, with Frogfoot's capital aimed at 360,000 lower-income homes over 12 months.

2026-09-14-eswatinipositivenews-sadcopac.summary: SADCOPAC secretary-general Madala Mhlanga told public accounts committees across the region to act before scandals and losses. He urged digital forensics, data analytics and audits of the algorithms in government digital systems.

2026-09-14-fawry-dms-pos-medical-payment.summary: Fawry is linking its business POS terminals to DMS's medical and management software so hospital cashier amounts pass straight to the terminal and payment status updates in real time. No commercial terms or rollout figures were given.

2026-09-14-flutterwave-dangote-refinery-.summary: Flutterwave opened online subscriptions to the Dangote refinery IPO as a receiving agent, at NGN 525 a share with a ten-share minimum and a Bank Verification Number required. The offer closes on 13 October.

2026-09-14-flutterwave-stablecoin-paymen.summary: Flutterwave's stablecoin lead describes using stablecoins as settlement rails rather than a product, through its Circle partnership since April 2025 and several tokens on Polygon and Tempo. The company has applied to the central bank's second sandbox cohort.

2026-09-14-gha-myjoyonline-gaps-suicide-.summary: Ghana launched a national suicide situational report with media guidelines, which finds the country's data incomplete. Health records, the births and deaths registry and police data each miss age or method, and death certificates do not reliably reach the registry.

2026-09-14-gmb-thepoint-gala-condemns-fr.summary: The Gambia Action for Local Accountability condemned reports that citizens who had paid for national ID cards were told to reapply after a change of system operator. It asked the immigration department to explain and said it is documenting cases.

2026-09-14-gsma-refugee-women-digital-in.summary: GSMA research finds identity rules for SIM registration push refugee women in Ethiopia and Tanzania to register lines in others' names, limiting control of mobile money and communication. In Uganda about 25% of refugee women use the internet against 50% of men.

2026-09-14-intra-city-digital-divide-afr.summary: Okey Chigbu argues the digital divide runs inside cities as well as between city and village, contrasting dense fibre in Lagos's Ikoyi with thin coverage in Ajegunle and Makoko. He calls for broadband to be measured by ward rather than by state.

2026-09-14-itd-fintech-trust-developing-.summary: A journal article surveying 392 participants in emerging and developing economies treats fintech as a stand-in institution where capital markets fail, resting on trust in the platform.

2026-09-14-ken-techweez-airtel-telesonic.summary: Airtel Africa is winding up Airtel Kenya Telesonic, its wholesale fibre subsidiary, two years after launch, with a KES 16.1 million loss and no revenue in 2025. Its facilities licence was returned to the Communications Authority in February, with gazettement pending.

2026-09-14-kenya-keiyo-south-public-wifi.summary: Kenya installed a free public Wi-Fi hotspot at Nyaru in Keiyo South, carrying fibre on Kenya Power poles. The ICT principal secretary also inspected the Chepkorio digital hub under construction.

2026-09-14-lbr-fpa-officials-post-vulner.summary: Liberian officials, among them the water utility's managing director, posted spreadsheets of children in a UNICEF-funded social protection programme to Facebook, with names, schools, home addresses and caregivers. A lawyer called it a breach of the Children's Law of 2011; no response from the ministry or UNICEF is reported.

2026-09-14-lebara-nigeria-mvno-launch-te.summary: Lebara Nigeria began commercial service as the second virtual network operator under the 2022 framework, after Vitel Wireless. It runs on Airtel's network under a 2023 licence and sells eSIMs with remote identity checks in its app.

2026-09-14-liberia-nid-crvs-link-osd-ppp.summary: Liberia's identification registry plans one system linking national ID with civil registration and vital statistics under its proposed US$54 million partnership with Austria's OSD. The signed agreement still needs parliamentary approval, and ID issuance has been suspended since June 2025.

2026-09-14-madica-adegboye-early-stage-f.summary: Emmanuel Adegboye, head of Flourish Ventures' Madica programme, says its US$200,000 cheques across ten markets including Algeria and Cameroon are not enough on their own, so the programme now co-invests. He is backing voice AI and calls for incentives to grow angel investment.

2026-09-14-mar-nichan-niyaba-bahth-tajas.summary: Morocco's prosecutor general at the Casablanca Court of Appeal ordered a judicial investigation into a party leader's claim that his party's phones were being spied on. The national judicial police will verify the claim, which the prosecution tied to the proper conduct of the elections; the party is not named.

2026-09-14-mauritiustimes-ai-decision-ri.summary: Columnist Gleb Tsipursky argues Mauritius should map which AI tasks may execute, recommend, be verified or stay with humans before scaling adoption. He points to the AI Innovation Lab as the place to train for it.

2026-09-14-meta-ai-academy-kenya-itweb-a.summary: Meta and accelerator This Is Digital launched an AI Academy in Kenya on 11 September with free training and equity-free funding. A startup pitchathon closes applications on 30 September for a Nairobi final on 15 October, and an eight-week masterclass starts on 3 November.

2026-09-14-mli-maliweb-abdrahamane-keita.summary: Mali's cybercrime tribunal sentenced journalist Abdrahamane KeÃ¯ta, publication director of Le TÃ©moin, to two years in prison and 1 million CFA francs in damages over a television remark about Kidal. He has been detained since June, and his defence intends to appeal.

2026-09-14-moz-clubofmozambique-correiog.summary: Mozambique's digital transformation agency said the government email service CorreioGOV was restored after maintenance, with some peripheral services still restricted. Neither the start of the outage nor its cause was given.

2026-09-14-mtn-nigeria-fibre-market-shar.summary: Regulator data for June put MTN at 176,468 of Nigeria's 319,735 fibre connections, a 55% share. Fibre remains about 0.2% of roughly 156.8 million internet subscriptions.

2026-09-14-mtn-south-sudan-network-cover.summary: MTN South Sudan says population broadband coverage rose from 76.6% to 85% and network availability to 99% over two years, after more than 500 sites were modernised with CREI's solar-hybrid power. Diesel use at supported sites fell by more than half; no investment figure is given.

2026-09-14-nga-africaintelligence-meta-2.summary: Meta is negotiating a settlement with Nigeria's consumer protection commission over its US$220 million fine after a first appeal was rejected, Africa Intelligence reports. No terms or timetable are given.

2026-09-14-nga-businessday-200-telecom-t.summary: Nigeria's communications ministry said at least 200 towers for unconnected communities will be live by December, out of about 3,700 planned, with a new satellite for places neither towers nor fibre reach. The remarks came at the opening of the data protection commission's new Abuja headquarters, which reported 356 licensed compliance organisations.

2026-09-14-nga-cyberera-ndpc-arcon-data-.summary: Nigeria Data Protection Commission head Vincent Olatunji told an advertising regulator's webinar that only 12.3% of advertising agencies comply with the data protection law. He called for the two regulators to work together on data processing in marketing.

2026-09-14-nga-thales-alenia-space-nigco.summary: Thales Alenia Space signed a contract with Nigeria's NIGCOMSAT to build the NigComSat-2A geostationary satellite on a Spacebus B2 platform, with a service life above 15 years and coverage from West to Southern Africa. No contract value, financing or launch date is stated.

2026-09-14-nga-vanguard-okoye-2023-cyber.summary: Former INEC commissioner Festus Okoye said the commission's platforms faced many cyberattacks during the 2023 presidential election but he could not say they caused the IReV portal failure, which he attributed to a technical malfunction.

2026-09-14-nigeria-ai-defences-elections.summary: An INEC delegation led by chairman Joash Ojo Amupitan met Google, Microsoft and IFES in Ottawa on AI, cybersecurity and electoral resilience ahead of Nigeria's 2027 polls. No agreement or programme was announced.

2026-09-14-optasia-h1-revenue-itweb.summary: Optasia's revenue rose 58% to US$185.3 million in the six months to June, with mobile financial services 72% of the total and Ghana about 31.5%. In Nigeria all operator partners were live again by 24 June after a suspension of airtime-credit services, and FirstRand raised its stake to 26.1%.

2026-09-14-rwa-techreviewafrica-irembo-s.summary: Rwanda's Irembo hosted a Guinean water utility delegation, the Congolese ambassador and a Smart Africa workshop on cross-border digital public infrastructure to share its experience of digital public services.

2026-09-14-sajim-online-admission-system.summary: A scoping review of 18 studies on online admission systems in education frames South Africa's systems as e-government and finds gaps in usability and equity of access.

2026-09-14-seevcash-dawuda-iddrisu-trans.summary: A profile of Ghanaian engineer Dawuda Iddrisu, co-founder of SeevCash, a cross-border transfer fintech set up in 2022 in the United States with a Ghana base. It handles dollars, sterling, euros, cedis, naira and USDC and offers a business suite.

2026-09-14-sen-lesoleil-cybastion-300m-t.summary: US company Cybastion announced a US$300 million investment in Senegal's digital infrastructure, data security and sovereignty, in Washington. No date, instrument, projects or timetable are given.

2026-09-14-sen-lesoleil-nouveau-directeu.summary: Cheikh Tidiane Sarr, a former SONATEL and Orange Finances Mobiles SÃ©nÃ©gal executive, was appointed director-general of the regulator ARTP by a decree of 10 September after an open call for applications. He inherits a market of 21.7 million internet lines, with rural access gaps, high tariffs and weak fibre competition.

2026-09-14-som-hiiraan-eac-trade-digital.summary: An opinion piece notes intra-EAC trade reached US$14.33 billion in 2024 while its share of total trade fell to 11.8%. It argues for sharing cross-border trade data once rather than repeatedly at each border.

2026-09-14-thisday-dele-oye-uber-exit-re.summary: Dele Oye of the Alliance for Economic Research and Ethics says Uber's exit from Nigeria exposes gaps in transport regulation. He calls for transparent airport e-hailing rules and equal treatment of ride-hailing firms and car-hire operators.

2026-09-14-thisday-fg-n10-5bn-digital-tr.summary: Nigeria launched a Digital Training Academy in Abuja with more than N10.5 billion to train over 32,000 young people in six-month online courses. The National Open University and Yaba College of Technology host study centres, and the academy certifies the 3 Million Technical Talent programme.

2026-09-14-thisday-mtn-ihs-deal-antitrus.summary: A lawyer reads MTN's acquisition of IHS Towers against Nigeria's competition law, setting out the regulators' conditions: a Nigerian sell-down of up to 30%, no exclusivity and existing contracts left unchanged.

2026-09-14-togo-otr-employers-certified-.summary: About 50 businesses met Togo's revenue office on 10 September on the certified electronic invoicing introduced by the 2026 budget law. 2026-09-14-top-ict-tenders-sita-activity.summary: South Africa's State IT Agency placed four of the week's top ten ICT tenders, including a 36-month incident management system for the police, whose tender says it has no single integrated system for logging reported incidents. 2026-09-14-tun-assabah-tunis-taamir-buil.summary: The Municipality of Tunis began adopting the Taamir platform for filing and tracking building-permit applications, keeping the paper route open for now. 2026-09-14-twiga-foods-administration-ke.summary: GT Flow, formerly Twiga Foods One, entered administration on 17 August, according to a gazette notice of 11 September. Twiga raised about US$185 million; the notice does not say what sits in the company or whether its distributors are affected.

2026-09-14-xaf-aip-apm26-4-abidjan-posit.summary: CÃ´te d'Ivoire hosts the fourth and final African preparatory meeting for the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Abidjan from 15 to 17 September, under the African Telecommunications Union. Delegations will settle common proposals and candidacies before Doha in November.

2026-09-14-xaf-steyn-au-ai-strategy-impl.summary: Johan Steyn contrasts the African Union's 2024 endorsement of a continental AI strategy with the thirteen national strategies adopted since 2018. He cites South Africa's withdrawn draft policy as an example of the implementation gap.

2026-09-14-xaf-techzim-open-letter-afric.summary: Engineer Jacob Mutisi, a former Zimbabwe ICT association chair, wrote to African leaders urging an AU threat-monitoring centre, joint cyber defence and AI safety standards.

2026-09-14-xaf-thisisafrica-algorithm-di.summary: Blessing Vava argues that platform algorithms shape what African voters see, drawing on Zambia's 2026 election, including fake GEN-20 forms and a disputed video. He calls for rules on algorithmic governance before the next elections.

2026-09-14-xna-aljazeera-shamal-afriqia-.summary: An Al Jazeera analysis asks whether North Africa will become an AI compute hub or merely host foreign capacity, weighing cables, renewable power and land against water limits on cooling. 2026-09-14-youm7-egypt-moj-remote-litiga.summary: Egypt's justice ministry defended the charges on its remote criminal litigation platform ahead of the new Criminal Procedure Law taking effect on 1 October, citing Article 531 as the basis for remote sessions. 2026-09-14-youm7-egypt-ntra-mobile-walle.summary: Egypt's telecom regulator counted 57.01 million operator mobile wallets in the first half of 2026, up 23% in a year, with EGP 2.96 trillion transacted and penetration at 45%. Vodafone Cash held 77% of transaction value, and 67% of wallets were registered to men.

2026-09-14-zoyk-zoykpay-autorisation-rdc.summary: Zambian fintech Zoyk received DR Congo central bank approval to deploy Zoykpay, which brings banks and mobile-money operators into one collection system for businesses. The approval date is not given.

2026-09-15-ago-lusa-unita-registo-eleito.summary: The main opposition leader accused the government of using state means to register the governing party's own members early in the electoral roll update for the 2027 elections, speaking after completing his own proof-of-life step.

2026-09-15-ben-techreviewafrica-apdp-17-.summary: Seventeen officers of the data protection authority were sworn in before the Cotonou court of first instance on 14 September under the digital code, formally binding them to the obligations of their duties.

2026-09-15-biometricupdate-e-gova-camero.summary: A digital government summit in Yaounde from 14 to 17 October will address how to build connected, interoperable, secure and accessible public service delivery systems across the continent.

2026-09-15-biometricupdate-south-africa-.summary: The state IT agency is seeking a supplier to equip the police with facial recognition integrated into body-worn and dashboard cameras, the software also to include automatic number plate recognition.

2026-09-15-caf-agenceecofin-cardip-banqu.summary: The country's component of the Central Africa digital integration programme is to launch in April 2027, after a week of work in Bangui by a financier mission covering connectivity, public services, data and cybersecurity.

2026-09-15-cipesa-beyond-ai-safety-afric.summary: A policy organisation argues that safety is not the whole question for African countries in global artificial intelligence governance: without infrastructure, skills, resources and representation, safety without sovereignty and agency is not enough.

2026-09-15-citinewsroom-ghana-200m-digit.summary: The communications minister said government has begun implementing measures against gaps a UNESCO readiness assessment identified in digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence capacity and cybersecurity, putting US$250m against an AI computing centre and US$200m against digitalisation.

2026-09-15-cmr-journalducameroun-4e-rgph.summary: Counting closed on 15 September for the fourth population and housing census, coupled with the agriculture and livestock census, after a start on 24 April and extensions in May and July. Coverage remained below expectation.

2026-09-15-cmr-journalducameroun-minjec-.summary: The youth ministry signed a three-year renewable partnership with a company on 14 September to digitise, unify and speed access to employment and training for 15- to 35-year-olds, across six areas including socio-economic integration.

2026-09-15-cog-adiac-central-africa-tele.summary: A regional workshop in Brazzaville on 15 and 16 September worked towards a common framework for national emergency telecommunications plans across central Africa, convened by the international telecommunications union with the regional regulators' assembly and the economic community.

2026-09-15-com-lagazette-udc-pnud-unipod.summary: The national university and the United Nations development programme signed a memorandum on training, research and innovation, at its centre a shared innovation space intended to bring students, researchers, entrepreneurs and institutions together on local problems.

2026-09-15-connectingafrica-dni-129m-sou.summary: A privately owned South African investment company announced investments above R2.1bn, about US$129.2m, across a fibre network operator, two internet service providers, an eSIM company and a mobile technology and fintech company.

2026-09-15-connectingafrica-gates-founda.summary: A foundation committed US$1bn over two years to artificial intelligence tools for health workers, farmers and teachers in the world's poorest regions, published alongside its tenth annual progress report on whether AI narrows or widens global disparities.

2026-09-15-dailynews-world-bank-digital-.summary: With the US$150m Digital Tanzania Project due to complete on 31 October, its financier signalled support for a second phase in which artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies would take a central place. Nothing about a second phase is committed or costed.

2026-09-15-dza-elmawkie-avancees-paiemen.summary: The national economic, social and environmental council held a conference in Algiers on making electronic payment general, setting out the progress made against wider economic change.

2026-09-15-dza-radioalgerie-zerrouki-ai-.summary: The posts and telecommunications minister called for closing the global gap in artificial intelligence capability and for an international AI governance agency, speaking at a ministerial meeting on the margins of a global forum on AI ethics.

2026-09-15-egy-enterprise-digital-egp-ve.summary: A market explainer sets out how a digital pound would differ from existing instant payments and wallets: central bank money held directly rather than a claim on a bank or telco. 2026-09-15-egy-maspero-toya-technology-i.summary: A military production ministry subsidiary signed a memorandum with a global chip maker at the ministry's training complex in Cairo, framed as part of a push to localise technology and deepen domestic manufacturing. 2026-09-15-fasoamazone-oni-cib-aes-enrol.summary: Burkina Faso's national identification office opened nine extra enrolment sites across Ouagadougou for the Sahel alliance biometric identity card after heavy demand at its main centre. 2026-09-15-gha-onuaonline-african-approa.summary: The same minister called for a distinctly African approach to artificial intelligence, arguing African values, data, computing infrastructure and human capacity should be reflected in how AI is built and governed globally.

2026-09-15-gha-u-s-commerce-department-e.summary: A United States commerce delegation met the communications regulator in Accra on artificial intelligence regulation, emerging technologies and closer cooperation between the two institutions.

2026-09-15-gnq-el-ministerio-de-transpor.summary: The transport, telecommunications and civil aviation ministry handed out certificates in Malabo after a two-month executive programme in artificial intelligence, machine learning and cybersecurity for its own staff.

2026-09-15-gnq-equatorial-guinea-starlin.summary: All satellite internet sales are to run through the telecommunications regulator, under the supervision of the artificial intelligence state secretariat, and contracts citizens obtained outside official channels are to be cancelled, decided at a working session on 9 September.

2026-09-15-itweb-acsa-metaverse-patrol-r.summary: Airports Company South Africa's annual report sets a plan to 2031 to bring AI, connected sensors, blockchain and robotics into airport operations, from check-in and baggage handling to patrol robots and a metaverse proof of concept. 2026-09-15-itweb-africa-sadc-bloc-rethin.summary: The Communications Regulators' Association of Southern Africa opened its 46th executive committee meeting in Mangochi, Malawi, chaired by the Malawian regulator, with AI, satellite services, cross-border platforms and cybersecurity on the agenda. 2026-09-15-itweb-bma-digital-port-health.summary: South Africa's Border Management Authority launched a Port Health Management System at Durban Harbour, replacing shipping agents' e-mailed requests with online inspections, free pratique applications, endorsements, invoicing and payment. 2026-09-15-itweb-dbsa-backs-48000km-fibr.summary: The Development Bank of Southern Africa said businesses it financed through fund management contributed to 47,545km of fibre deployed in South Africa in the year to March 2026. 2026-09-15-itweb-integrity360-cape-town-.summary: A 40-desk security operations centre opened in Cape Town on 14 September under a R55m investment, providing monitoring and incident response for customers across Africa and internationally, and stated to create about 100 jobs over three years.

2026-09-15-itweb-woan-comeback-kzn-uk-fu.summary: A R7m UK-funded programme in KwaZulu-Natal, run with South Africa's communications department, will support 25 local community network operators to deploy 250 public Wi-Fi hotspots, connect 150 schools, libraries and clinics and reach 1,500 homes. 2026-09-15-ken-businessdaily-somaliland-.summary: Berbera is being positioned as an alternative digital gateway for landlocked Ethiopia and South Sudan, offering providers, businesses and governments another route to global data connections beside the established Mombasa gateway.

2026-09-15-ken-digital-health-agency-pus.summary: The digital health agency, established under the Digital Health Act to coordinate health systems, is working to link facilities so patient records can be shared and patients need not carry physical files to treatment or referral.

2026-09-15-ken-kenya-in-talks-with-china.summary: The treasury's principal secretary met a Chinese development bank executive in Beijing to review projects the lender already supports and seek more funding for roads, water and connectivity.

2026-09-15-ken-kenya-takes-13-mega-proje.summary: The public-private partnership directorate took thirteen priority infrastructure projects to international investors in Seoul, covering transport, energy, water, irrigation and technology development for the current financial year.

2026-09-15-lby-economy-ministry-makes-el.summary: The requirement bites in stages: a transitional period runs to the end of 2026, then from January 2027 for businesses whose annual transactions or shipments are worth US$1m or more.

2026-09-15-mar-moroccoworldnews-ebrd-25m.summary: A development bank approved a EUR 25m loan to a Moroccan bank for small and medium businesses financing climate-related investments, part of a wider EUR 65m package.

2026-09-15-mar-panorapost-mou-vertiv-inf.summary: The digital transition ministry and a critical digital-infrastructure supplier signed a memorandum in Rabat on developing digital infrastructure, cloud computing and artificial intelligence.

2026-09-15-mar-panorapost-seghrouchni-ia.summary: The digital transition minister said the country aims to make artificial intelligence a lever of digital sovereignty, territorial equity and inclusive development, speaking at an event on AI in public services.

2026-09-15-mdg-2424-task-force-reclamati.summary: The finance ministry announced a task force on mobile money complaints, bringing the banking supervision commission and the communications regulator together to speed up resolution. Users report lost money, failed transactions and long waits.

2026-09-15-mdg-fid-location-serveurs-clo.summary: A development fund opened a tender, closing 29 September, to rent two cloud servers under a World Bank-financed girls' empowerment and resilience project.

2026-09-15-mwi-mwnation-digital-rights-c.summary: Three district councils each won US$20,000 under a youth innovation challenge to develop and test youth-led digital solutions to service delivery problems inside existing council systems.

2026-09-15-nam-namibian-beyond-certifica.summary: A commentary sets vocational training against an unemployment rate of 36.9 per cent and youth unemployment of 44.4 per cent, alongside reported shortages in more than seventy occupations, arguing the country produces qualifications faster than capability.

2026-09-15-rwa-taarifa-university-forum-.summary: A university faculty head called on educators, researchers and policymakers to rethink education as artificial intelligence changes how people learn and work, speaking at the fifth conference of a lifelong-learning project bringing together universities from Rwanda, Uganda, Ethiopia and Norway.

2026-09-15-sanews-dpsa-batho-pele-ai-cha.summary: The public service department's chatbot, launched in late August, gives public servants access to policy updates, circulars and legislation in nine official languages.

2026-09-15-sdn-alradar-white-nile-electr.summary: The standards and metrology body's White Nile branch began collecting fees electronically, issuing a receipt at the moment of payment, presented as enforcement of a state-wide electronic collection decision.

2026-09-15-swz-times-businessmen-switch-.summary: The revenue service says some businessmen change the order or variation of their names to avoid detection, making taxpayers hard to identify, and that digital identification would establish when different names belong to the same person.

2026-09-15-syc-statehouse-hydrographic-o.summary: Cabinet approved a hydrographic office inside the maritime safety authority, to bring hydrographic information together from across government and international partners for navigation, search and rescue, marine planning and the blue economy.

2026-09-15-tcd-alwihdainfo-abeche-adetic.summary: Abeche's town hall, the provincial telecommunications delegation and the ICT development agency met on 15 September to strengthen a partnership digitising municipal services and training staff in digital tools.

2026-09-15-tcd-lendjampost-commerce-nume.summary: With a world trade forum in Geneva debating the digital transformation of services trade, expected to grow 4.8 per cent in 2026, a commentary asks what a landlocked country can take from a shift that moves trade onto screens rather than through ports.

2026-09-15-techafricanews-orange-egypt-c.summary: An operator and a pharmacy management company signed a partnership to combine pharmacy management technology with connectivity, covering sales, dispensing, inventory and customer management in one connected system.

2026-09-15-techafricanews-senegal-wave-d.summary: Senegal's government held talks with mobile-money company Wave on 10 September 2026 about digitising transport, health and Treasury services, with data management and the Telecommunications Code also discussed. 2026-09-15-techcabal-terrahex-bitcoin-mi.summary: A Nigerian founder plans bitcoin mining sites built around stranded power, treating oil fields as mines: cheap electricity that has no other buyer.

2026-09-15-tgo-savoirnews-lome-surveilla.summary: About forty biologists, technicians, researchers and bioinformaticians from west and central Africa are in Lome from 9 to 22 September for a workshop under a thirteen-country genomic surveillance programme built after the Covid-19 period, strengthening sequencing capacity and outbreak response.

2026-09-15-tun-realites-ai-forward-summi.summary: A second artificial intelligence summit opened on 9 September in Yasmine Hammamet, organised by the Arab ICT organisation with the communications ministry, bringing more than 450 participants to questions of sovereignty and governance.

2026-09-15-tun-tunisienumerique-tradenet.summary: The trade network opened a web portal for electronic invoicing from 15 September, aimed at businesses and professionals with low invoicing volumes, letting them configure their environment and prepare and track invoices.

2026-09-15-tza-dailynews-data-governance.summary: A commentary argues the country is generating more data than ever while its capacity to govern, integrate, protect and use that data has not kept pace, and that the gap threatens the growth digital transformation is meant to deliver.

2026-09-15-tza-habarileo-helios-camara-m.summary: A tower company opened an ICT laboratory worth 30m shillings at a secondary school in Iringa, with 26 desktop computers and a projector, for 873 students and 43 teachers.

2026-09-15-tza-thecitizen-digital-transf.summary: A commentary argues digital transformation amounts to more than connectivity, and that treating network reach as the measure mistakes the means for the end.

2026-09-15-tza-timesmajira-kairuki-ttcl-.summary: The ICT minister, after visiting the state telecom's fibre centre, said smartphone use has reached 47 per cent and that the ten-year digital transformation plan continues, including wider access to modern devices.

2026-09-15-tza-timesmajira-omdtz-ramani-.summary: A mapping organisation working with government began handing ward flood preparedness plans to communities in five Dar es Salaam wards, over five days from 14 September, under an externally funded project using mapping and geographic information to reduce disaster risk.

2026-09-15-uga-businessoftech-sandi-ai-g.summary: A Ugandan startup using artificial intelligence and agricultural data to help rural farmers reach finance without conventional collateral won a US$50,000 prize at a continental agrifood forum.

2026-09-15-uga-cajnews-stricter-measures.summary: The communications regulator said it is working with parliament on a framework allowing targeted denial of service to repeat abusers of cyberspace, its director likening the measure to withdrawing a driving licence. No bill, offence definition or appeal route is published.

2026-09-15-wearetech-benin-nigeria-douan.summary: The two countries' customs administrations launched a pilot interconnection of their systems at the Seme-Krake border post on 11 September, to exchange data in real time and cut repeated formalities.

2026-09-15-wearetech-tesfa-ai-natnael-ke.summary: A profile of an Addis Ababa company founded in 2025 to embed artificial intelligence in organisations' operations, building virtual assistants that carry out complex tasks rather than answer questions.

2026-09-15-wearetech-vula-mobile-3-milli.summary: South African referral app Vula Mobile, which connects rural health workers with specialist doctors, has passed three million patients referred. It operates in five southern African countries, which the report does not name.

2026-09-15-xwa-gouvernement-burkina-aes-.summary: A regional bloc meeting in Ouagadougou called for closer coordination between the administrative authorities of member states' border regions, framed around borders serving peace and development.

2026-09-15-zaf-sowetan-gumede-cybersecur.summary: An opinion piece argues the redrafted national artificial intelligence policy must carry sovereignty — independent control over technology, data security, privacy and infrastructure — against the dominance of a small number of foreign AI companies.

2026-09-15-zaf-thesouthafrican-sassa-gra.summary: A grant recipient describes being asked for bank statements, school enrolment letters and the full first-application paperwork to keep her children's social grants through the agency's review process.

2026-09-15-zmb-zambiamonitor-zicta-revok.summary: The communications regulator revoked an operator's network and service licences with effect from 14 September, citing persistent failures to meet regulatory, operational and financial obligations after considering the operator's representations.

2026-09-16-ago-angop-manutencao-preventi.summary: Angola's interbank payments operator EMIS warned that maintenance from 17 to 19 September 2026, between 01:00 and 04:00, may briefly disrupt the Multicaixa card network.

2026-09-16-ago-angop-ministro-mario-oliv.summary: Angola Telecom switched on its Tudonosso fibre-to-the-home service at the 1,000-dwelling Baía Farta housing centre in Benguela on 16 September 2026, the first site of a project the telecoms minister placed within the national broadband network.

2026-09-16-ago-angop-rede-de-banda-larga.summary: Angola inaugurated the first link of its national fibre broadband network at Lobito on 16 September 2026, on a route from Luanda through Bengo and Cuanza Sul. Angola Telecom named Huambo, Namibe and Cabinda for the next phase, with all 21 provinces as the aim.

2026-09-16-bceao-communique-homologation.summary: The BCEAO certified the business APIs of a first group of participants on the regional instant payment platform on 16 September 2026, letting firms send and receive payments, submit bulk settlements and track transactions across the monetary union whatever the other party's provider.

2026-09-16-bceao-liste-api-business-pi-s.summary: The BCEAO's list of September 2026 names 23 participants whose business APIs are certified on the regional instant payment platform: nine in Senegal, seven in Côte d'Ivoire, two in Niger and one each in Benin, Burkina Faso, Guinea-Bissau, Mali and Togo.

2026-09-16-ben-lanation-economie-la-cryp.summary: La Nation explains that no law in Benin bars individuals from holding cryptocurrency, but it is not legal tender in the West African monetary union and no merchant must accept it. Taxes cannot be paid in it directly, and the union's own framework for crypto-assets is still being built.

2026-09-16-ben-lanation-recensements-gen.summary: ECOWAS member states began validating a practical guide for population and housing censuses in Cotonou on 15 September 2026, meant to make West African census data more reliable and comparable across countries.

2026-09-16-bfa-libreinfo-fasosign-lancem.summary: Burkina Faso launched FasoSign, a national electronic signature platform for the public administration, on 15 September 2026. It is already built into the mission-order, mail and cadastre systems, and the government says its keys and certificates are held under state responsibility.

2026-09-16-biometricupdate-international.summary: International Identity Day 2026 turned the emphasis from population coverage to trust, with ID4Africa's executive chairman arguing that identity systems should be judged on whether they are useful, secure and under people's control throughout their lives.

2026-09-16-broadcastmediaafrica-crasa-46.summary: Southern African communications regulators meeting in Mangochi, Malawi, for the 46th executive committee of their association, CRASA, called for more agile and collaborative regulation as AI, satellite services and cross-border platforms reshape the sector. Host regulator MACRA's director-general urged more knowledge sharing and harmonised approaches.

2026-09-16-civ-aip-pnd-2026-2030-sept-pi.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's digital minister presented seven pillars and 40 projects for the digital part of the 2026-2030 development plan, from universal connectivity and interoperable administration to AI, cybersecurity and skills. The target is to raise the digital economy from an estimated 6 to 8% of GDP to 15% by 2030.

2026-09-16-cod-7sur7-rdc-pass-formation-.summary: DR Congo began training the first 50 enrolment agents for its RDC-Pass digital identity platform on 15 September 2026, three months after its launch. The digital economy minister said RDC-Pass is an authentication tool, not a national identity card, and does not replace civil registration.

2026-09-16-connectingafrica-vodacom-keny.summary: Vodacom and Kenya's Treasury both said on 16 September 2026 that they will appeal the High Court ruling that voided the sale of a 15% government stake in Safaricom. The court found the deal lacked meaningful public participation and hid material information, and ordered the stake returned to the state.

2026-09-16-cpv-expressodasilhas-ministro.summary: Cabo Verde's health minister said on 16 September 2026 that sharing clinical records and test results across health facilities would stop patients repeating examinations as they move between islands. He set digitalisation beside new financing sources as Global Fund support declines.

2026-09-16-dgi-mauritanie-teleservices.summary: Mauritania's tax directorate runs an online filing and payment system for businesses and a set of teleservices for all registered taxpayers, covering online returns, the taxpayer's file, payment schedules and a secure channel to the administration.

2026-09-16-dji-adi-ministre-telecommunic.summary: Djibouti's telecoms minister received a Huawei vice-president to discuss cooperation on new-generation infrastructure and services, calling the company a leading partner in the country's ambition to be a regional connectivity hub. No agreement was announced.

2026-09-16-dji-lanation-previsions-meteo.summary: Djibouti's meteorological agency and its disaster risk secretariat held regional workshops in Ali-Sabieh and Tadjourah under the WISER programme, working with local officials, farmers and herders on turning forecasts into early action.

2026-09-16-dpi-map-mali-country-profile.summary: The DPI Map profile for Mali records the NINA identity number but no identity or civil registry act, no regulation for digital ID, no biometric use and no digital authentication function, while noting a national data protection law is in place.

2026-09-16-egy-ahram-mcit-intel-mou-ai-t.summary: Egypt's communications ministry signed a three-year memorandum with Intel on 16 September 2026 to train one million citizens a year in AI online and certify 500 trainers a year, in support of the national AI strategy for 2025-2030.

2026-09-16-egy-youm7-civil-registry-digi.summary: A Youm7 feature describes Egypt's interior ministry moving civil-registry services onto self-service machines that issue civil status documents at any hour, placed beyond registry offices in busy public locations. The piece gives no count of machines or transactions.

2026-09-16-gab-gabonreview-data-center-i.summary: A Chinese government delegation inspected La Poste and Gabon Telecom sites in Libreville on 15 September 2026 as a possible home for an AI data centre serving the public administration. The postal site can host more than 300 servers; the project depends on the Gabon-China partnership being finalised.

2026-09-16-gha-myjoyonline-bog-digital-a.summary: The Bank of Ghana told a digital assets summit on 16 September 2026 that firms should build compliance, transparency and customer asset protection into their operations from the start. The organiser named the virtual assets law passed in December 2025 as the main change since the previous edition.

2026-09-16-gha-myjoyonline-customs-reven.summary: Ghana's revenue authority says customs collections have risen from about US$350 million to as much as US$450 million a month since an AI valuation system was installed at the ports in April 2026. It attributes the rise to more accurate valuation and classification rather than new taxes.

2026-09-16-gha-myjoyonline-household-reg.summary: Ghana's National Household Registry now covers 11.24 million people in 2,906,288 households across all 16 regions, 508,870 of them classed extremely poor. It is the targeting base for the LEAP cash grant, whose ceiling has risen to 450,000 households.

2026-09-16-gimtel-missions.summary: GIMTEL, the Mauritanian interbank card group set up under the central bank, groups ten banks and the postal service to develop card payments, including acceptance of international card networks and a domestic interbank network for payments and withdrawals.

2026-09-16-gnq-seneweb-coupure-facebook-.summary: Facebook and TikTok have been unreachable in Equatorial Guinea without a VPN since 2 September 2026, with internet speeds throttled, AFP reports. The restrictions followed a viral video accusing Vice-President Teodoro Nguema Obiang of corruption; its author was arrested.

2026-09-16-ipr-digital-sovereignty-empty.summary: An Internet Policy Review essay argues that digital sovereignty has come to mean so many conflicting things, from rights protection in the EU to content control in China, that it is empty as a concept, though not without limits.

2026-09-16-itweb-africa-kenya-ica-nation.summary: Kenya's ICT Authority tendered two framework agreements, national backbone links and cross-border and metro links, each for three years extendable by two. Treasury puts the public-sector fibre network at 30,454km against a 100,000km target before the 2027 election.

2026-09-16-itweb-africa-nigeria-governme.summary: An assessment presented to Nigeria's IT development agency found only 47% of about 30 government digital platforms met an accessibility threshold, with failures also on banking and payment platforms. The agency said it has written accessibility into revised website guidelines and is considering national standards.

2026-09-16-itweb-hollard-rejects-hacking.summary: An extortion attack on insurance technology provider MIP Holdings, detected on 14 June 2026, exposed personal data linked to customers of about 45 South African insurers. Hollard said a ransomware group's claim against it traced to that incident, not to its own systems.

2026-09-16-itweb-sa-banks-ai-value-micro.summary: PwC's review of South Africa's six largest banks for the first half of 2026 finds them moving from counting AI use cases to measuring returns, judged on fraud prevention, credit decisions, service speed and cost. Combined headline earnings rose 9.3% to R82.3 billion.

2026-09-16-ken-nation-opposition-irreduc.summary: A Kenyan opposition and civil-society coalition led by former Chief Justice David Maraga set five electoral demands for 2027, including an independent international audit of the voter register and biometrics and mandatory biometric voter identification. It also wants the electoral commission's technology policy, source code and procurement specifications published by 30 September 2026.

2026-09-16-ken-standard-ai-outpaces-regu.summary: The 2026 International AI Safety Report, presented at Daystar University in Kenya, warns that general-purpose AI is advancing faster than regulation. It notes at least 700 million weekly users of leading systems, with adoption below 10% across much of Africa, Asia and Latin America.

2026-09-16-ken-techtrendske-icta-kdeap-n.summary: Kenya's backbone tender will be scored 80% on technical factors and 20% on cost, with winning bidders required to disclose beneficial ownership. Public-sector fibre stood at 30,454km in 2026, up from 22,486km in 2022.

2026-09-16-lbr-fpa-cbl-financial-inclusi.summary: Liberia's draft national financial inclusion and education strategy went through a two-day validation and will be revised. Participants said its success depends on the identity registry, business registration and credit reference systems, and parts will need legislation and budget.

2026-09-16-lbr-fpa-prime-credit-sues-cbl.summary: Prime Credit Reference Bureau is suing the Central Bank of Liberia for US$1,180,953, alleging the bank never supplied or ordered lenders to supply the loan data its November 2025 licence depended on. It says the bank later wrote that it lacked clear authority to license private bureaux; the claims are untested.

2026-09-16-lby-libyaherald-customs-autom.summary: Libya's Customs Authority met foreign contractors on 15 September 2026 to revive automated inspection, container scanning and coastal monitoring contracts signed in earlier years but never completed. The meeting reviewed what had been delivered and what had blocked the rest; no contract values or dates were given.

2026-09-16-mar-assabah-rni-poursuites-im.summary: Morocco's National Rally of Independents said on 16 September 2026 that it will take to court anyone who made or spread doctored images and false content about two of its figures, Fatima Khair and Benaissa Al-Jarrari, during the election campaign.

2026-09-16-mar-hespress-ai-campagne-elec.summary: A New Democrats candidate in Tangier-Assilah for Morocco's 23 September 2026 legislative election has put QR codes on his posters linking to a site where an AI system answers voters' questions from the party programme.

2026-09-16-mdg-lexpressmg-etat-civil-20-.summary: About 20% of Madagascar's population remains outside the civil register, L'Express reports from the National Identity Day launch in Antananarivo. Officials named biometric registration in the communes and simpler procedures at communal offices as priorities.

2026-09-16-mdg-midimadagasikara-cooperat.summary: Madagascar's industrialisation ministry handed biometric cards to the first 124 registered cooperatives in Analamanga on 15 September 2026, under a UNDP-funded census building a verified national database of cooperatives. The census has also begun in Atsinanana and Analanjirofo.

2026-09-16-mdg-midimadagasikara-etat-civ.summary: Madagascar opened a second phase of its Izaho Tokana 2.0 birth-registration drive on National Identity Day, 15 September 2026, with support from the Francophonie organisation's civil status project. The 2025 multiple indicator survey found close to 20% of children under five without a birth certificate, 21% in rural areas against about 12% in towns.

2026-09-16-mesrs-etablissements-enseigne.summary: Mauritania's higher education ministry lists 17 public and 10 private higher education institutions on its site, with 33,049 students and 500 teaching staff.

2026-09-16-moz-mznews-regulamento-segura.summary: Mozambique's Council of Ministers approved a Postal Security Regulation on 15 September 2026, setting controls against theft, fraud and cyber threats to the postal network as e-commerce parcels increase.

2026-09-16-mrt-ami-conseil-ministres-pro.summary: Mauritania's Council of Ministers took a statement on 16 September 2026 proposing a national framework on minors' use of social media, with an access threshold at 16. It would switch off recommendation algorithms, infinite scroll and autoplay for minors by default, ban advertising aimed at them and add a reporting route for children harmed online; no draft text has been published.

2026-09-16-mrt-instant-payment-system-in.summary: Mauritania sought providers for an instant payment system to make financial services interoperable, under the World Bank-financed regional digital integration programme. The call closed on 3 June 2025.

2026-09-16-mrt-internet-society-pulse-co.summary: The Internet Society rates Mauritania's internet resilience at 43%, with 3% of the 1,000 most-visited websites served from local servers or caches against a 50% target. About 46% of the population uses the internet.

2026-09-16-mwi-malawi24-drops-expiry-dat.summary: Malawi's homeland security minister ordered on 16 September 2026 that national identity cards be issued without expiry dates from that day. He gave the order at the launch of the Nzika digital ID wallet, which lets citizens show government credentials on a phone by QR code.

2026-09-16-nam-namibiansun-itransfer-tea.summary: iTransfer, a self-funded Namibian platform launched in January 2026, matches public servants who want to swap postings and has registered 970 teachers across the 14 regions. It does not approve transfers and charges N$200 for three months.

2026-09-16-ner-actuniger-lancement-passe.summary: Niger opened mass enrolment for the Sahel confederation's biometric passport in Niamey on 15 September 2026, with enrolment kits to go to every region and the diaspora. An ordinary passport costs 45,000 FCFA and runs five years, with online pre-enrolment through mobile money services.

2026-09-16-nga-authorityngr-au-pre-elect.summary: An African Union pre-election mission, in Nigeria from 13 to 19 September 2026, asked the electoral commission for details of its readiness for the 2027 elections on voter registration, technology, logistics and funding. The mission described its role as supportive, not supervisory.

2026-09-16-nga-thisday-fg-december-deadl.summary: Nigeria's government set December 2026 as the deadline for 95% national identity number coverage, announced on National Identity Day. Officials put the database at close to 140 million and said physical e-ID cards will be issued before the end of the year.

2026-09-16-nga-thisday-nhrc-accountabili.summary: Nigeria's human rights commission and AccountabilityLab called for coordinated mechanisms so victims of digital rights violations can get justice quickly, at a meeting of agencies, regulators, lawyers, media and technology firms in Abuja.

2026-09-16-nga-thisday-sanusi-telcos-ent.summary: Former central bank governor Sanusi Lamido Sanusi said at the launch of Nigeria's 2026 Access to Financial Services survey that he was wrong to delay telecoms operators' entry into financial services during his tenure. He said concern for depositors after the banking crisis drove the decision and that it slowed financial inclusion.

2026-09-16-sen-seneweb-identite-synapsys.summary: Senegal marked International Identity Day with a first Senegal ID Day in Dakar on 16 September 2026, organised by Synapsys Conseils, the deposit fund's digital subsidiary, where partners presented biometric and digital trust products.

2026-09-16-swz-eswatinipositivenews-come.summary: A COMESA official told the regional AI validation meeting in Eswatini that AI could improve public services, agriculture, health and education across the region if member states invest in the skills, infrastructure and data it needs.

2026-09-16-swz-eswatinipositivenews-nati.summary: Eswatini has hired a consultant to draft a national AI strategy, the ICT minister's representative said at a COMESA regional validation meeting in Ezulwini on 16 September 2026.

2026-09-16-swz-eswatinipositivenews-sadc.summary: Public accounts committees across SADC adopted 32 resolutions in Eswatini on 16 September 2026, committing each to map major digital transformation projects and review at least one digital system for value for money within 12 months. Oversight is to extend to e-government, digital identity, e-procurement and e-payment systems.

2026-09-16-swz-network-blackout-home-aff.summary: A network outage on 16 September 2026 halted all identity card and passport processing at Eswatini's Home Affairs headquarters in Mbabane and at postal counters, with no restoration time given. Pupils needing original ID cards to sit examinations that week were among those turned away.

2026-09-16-swz-times-comesa-regional-ai-.summary: Eswatini is hosting a three-day COMESA meeting, opened on 16 September 2026, to validate a draft study on AI and emerging technologies. It precedes work on a regional AI strategy, model policy guidelines and a model regulatory framework under the World Bank-funded IDEA programme.

2026-09-16-techafricanews-egypt-intel-ai.summary: Under Egypt's agreement with Intel, the training covers basic AI concepts and safe, responsible use, alongside a digital trust programme.

2026-09-16-techafricanews-kenya-digital-.summary: Kenya began the second phase of its Digital Literacy Programme, putting teacher laptops and interactive smartboards into 10,382 public junior schools. In Nairobi all 98 targeted schools had devices and 91 had completed installation and acceptance.

2026-09-16-techafricanews-kenya-icta-fib.summary: Kenya's ICT Authority opened an international tender to extend the national fibre backbone and cross-border and metro links under the World Bank-backed digital economy project, which TechAfricaNews says is financed by US$390 million in World Bank credits.

2026-09-16-techafricanews-kitsoft-smart-.summary: Smart Africa's secretariat signed a memorandum with Kitsoft, a GovTech firm of Ukrainian origin, on digital public infrastructure, e-government and AI, including building public services on low-code tools. No budget or country deployment is named.

2026-09-16-techafricanews-nitda-digital-.summary: Nigeria's IT development agency said it will work with the Centre for Inclusive Development on digital accessibility after the group presented research on barriers facing people with disabilities. The agency tied the work to its target of 70% digital literacy by 2027.

2026-09-16-techafricanews-senegal-cybast.summary: US cybersecurity company Cybastion committed to mobilise about US$300 million for digital projects in Senegal, presented to President Bassirou Diomaye Faye in Washington on 14 September 2026. The money is named for cybersecurity, data centres, technology transfer and capacity building; no instrument or timetable was given.

2026-09-16-techcabal-22-on-sloane-kumii-.summary: Cape Town's 22 On Sloane launched KUMii, an AI platform matching startups and small firms to funders, tenders and mentors, with more than 4,000 already registered. Its lending arm, Sloane Capital, is raising R1 billion, about US$63 million, to finance them.

2026-09-16-techcabal-amodei-pace-the-fro.summary: A TechCabal commentary sets Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei's call to slow the pace of frontier AI against Africa's position, arguing that the continent's AI debate starts from access, compute and skills rather than from racing ahead.

2026-09-16-techcabal-botswana-mukuru-com.summary: TechCabal looks at Mukuru's Visa Companion Card in Botswana, which lets wallet holders pay at merchants without a bank account, in a country where mobile money is widespread but bank accounts reach 58% of adults.

2026-09-16-techcabal-bujeti-ai-agents-fi.summary: Nigerian fintech Bujeti launched four AI agents that process documents, chase unpaid invoices, watch transactions and answer staff finance questions for businesses in Nigeria and Kenya. They go on general release on 30 September 2026; the company says more than 1,000 teams use its platform.

2026-09-16-techcabal-pula-s2e-fsd-africa.summary: FSD Africa, a UK aid-funded agency, is paying the consultancy S2E Africa to find corporate buyers for African startups and help them through deals, with insurtech Pula among the first clients. FSD Africa takes no stake in the acquisitions.

2026-09-16-techtrends-spectrum-allocatio.summary: A TechTrends analysis argues that spectrum allocation is industrial policy in all but name, contrasting Nigeria's 2026 push for more predictable assignment with South Africa's auction delayed for close to a decade by disputes over its rules.

2026-09-16-telecompaper-macra-crasa-sadc.summary: Malawi's regulator head, chairing the Southern African regulators' association CRASA, urged members at its 46th executive committee to replace outdated frameworks with rules that keep pace with technology.

2026-09-16-tgo-siham-farmers-agricultura.summary: Togo handed its SIHAM agricultural information system and five regional kiosks to the national farmers' organisation and regional managers on 15 September 2026. Financed by the World Bank, it sends weather forecasts, prices and input availability to farmers free by SMS in local languages.

2026-09-16-tza-mwananchi-kamera-za-barab.summary: Zanzibar's automated road cameras, which catch speeding, phone use and red-light running, drew criticism in the House of Representatives over the 50 km/h limit, the Sh230,000 fine and the absence of action against government drivers. The deputy works minister said raising the limit would be examined.

2026-09-16-tza-mwananchi-nida-yaondoa-ki.summary: Tanzania's Prime Minister ordered the identity authority on 16 September 2026 to drop the age bar and start registering young children. The authority plans to bring birth certificates, health insurance and the passport onto the national ID, and the home affairs minister put registrations at 27,527,835 with 2,027,103 finished cards uncollected.

2026-09-16-uga-newvision-transitioning-f.summary: Uganda's revenue authority said the taxpayer identification number will be phased out for individuals in favour of the national identification number, with companies using their registration number instead. It said the old system reached only just over 5 million taxpayers and that the change will remove duplicate and ghost records.

2026-09-16-uga-nilepost-digital-hubs-mus.summary: MTN Foundation Uganda and the ICT ministry handed over a second innovation hub at Busitema University, part of a Shs4 billion three-year programme for four university hubs and a refurbished national hub in Kampala. The programme expects to reach more than 20,000 students and community members.

2026-09-16-uga-nilepost-uganda-stronger-.summary: Speakers at the 15th East Africa Information Security Conference in Uganda urged investment in people, information sharing and resilience rather than tools alone. A Uganda Communications Commission director said mobile money, government platforms and health services now depend on secure infrastructure.

2026-09-16-universite-sahel-faculte-info.summary: The Université du Sahel in Mali runs a computing faculty offering professional bachelor's degrees in system and network administration and in database systems built on PostgreSQL.

2026-09-16-wearetech-benin-ruddy-gbaguid.summary: A WeAreTech profile of Beninese engineer Ruddy Gbaguidi, who founded Foniva in 2009, a cloud platform for running call centres that routes calls to available agents and reports performance in real time.

2026-09-16-wearetech-cameroun-zuo-bruno-.summary: A WeAreTech profile of Cameroonian entrepreneur Zuo Bruno, whose firm Zuoix, founded in 2013, offers preventive cybersecurity services to companies and public bodies, from penetration testing to incident management.

2026-09-16-wearetech-kenya-1000-diplomes.summary: Kenya's Public Service Commission opened applications on 15 September 2026 for 1,000 ICT graduates to spend 12 months in schools and sub-county education offices supporting the Digital Literacy Programme. Applications close on 5 October 2026.

2026-09-16-wto-tfa-mauritania-article-7-.summary: Mauritania's commitment under the WTO trade facilitation agreement to allow electronic payment of border duties was due by 31 December 2024; it has asked for 31 December 2027, saying it still needs a partner to help, and the request is not yet approved. The work includes linking the customs system, the Treasury and banks.

2026-09-16-xaf-afdb-kaist-letter-of-inte.summary: The African Development Bank and Korea's KAIST signed a three-year letter of intent in Seoul on 9 September 2026 covering joint research on AI policy and datasets, advice on digital transformation and training for African officials and researchers. No funding figure is attached.

2026-09-16-xaf-afdb-kexim-five-year-cofi.summary: The African Development Bank and the Export-Import Bank of Korea signed a five-year co-financing memorandum in Seoul on 9 September 2026, replacing a 2005 framework. It targets projects in AI, digital infrastructure, critical minerals, energy and transport; no amount is given.

2026-09-16-xaf-afdb-koafec-joint-declara.summary: Korea, 45 African countries and the African Development Bank adopted a joint declaration and a 2027-2028 action plan in Seoul on 9 September 2026 centred on AI, digital infrastructure and skills. The plan names thirteen initiatives, among them a regional data embassy in Sierra Leone and compute credits for African AI start-ups; no sums are attached.

2026-09-16-xaf-afdb-korea-nia-letter-of-.summary: The African Development Bank and Korea's National Information Society Agency signed a three-year letter of intent in Seoul on 9 September 2026 on data governance, AI-ready datasets and digital public infrastructure. The agency provides expertise and the bank identifies priorities and financing.

2026-09-16-xaf-chinadaily-africa-seeks-a.summary: African health officials told China Daily that AI and connected health systems could detect outbreaks earlier and speed emergency response. An Africa CDC adviser described digital transformation as health security infrastructure rather than an IT agenda.

2026-09-16-xaf-cnbcafrica-gates-africa-n.summary: Bill Gates said the Gates Foundation is working with AI companies to collect and publish data for African languages spoken by at least a million people. He tied the foundation's commitment of more than US$1 billion to AI projects to governments first improving health, agriculture and education data.

2026-09-16-xea-thestar-rects-multi-vendo.summary: Importers, exporters and logistics firms welcomed the Kenya Revenue Authority's decision to open the regional electronic cargo tracking system to private seal vendors.
